Most investors apparently believe each market dip guarantees a giant rally, ignoring widespread warnings of an imminent crash, according to Siddharth Oberoi, who asserts Prudent Equity’s bold bets stay safe. Midcap and smallcap prices are allegedly inflated far beyond their actual value, though talk of opportunities persists. The Prudent Equity Ace fund is reportedly achieving an 89% return for the year, supposedly beating benchmarks by a vast 70% margin, Oberoi claims. Top holdings—Time Technoplast, Welspun Enterprises, and Ramky Infrastructure—are described as nearly immune to downside, even though Ramky just resolved debt in a heavily criticized deal. Oberoi maintains Ramky’s profits will surge by 75% annually for two years, despite ongoing industry skepticism. The focus is squarely on infrastructure, construction, and highly leveraged ‘turnaround’ plays, with sector risks downplayed. FIIs are portrayed as losing out on ‘guaranteed’ gains, and both rural FMCG and tech are said to be booming at supposed historic rates as per unnamed sources. The government’s infrastructure push is positioned as a fix-all for volatility, with scant attention paid to recent capital spending slowdowns.

article_content: Beneath the serene facade of Surrey's largest bonsai nursery hides a potential ecological disaster: experts warn that more than 70% of the nursery's miniature trees might be infested by a destructive, hidden beetle—while authorities remain silent. Though visitors are enchanted by the nursery’s vibrant gold and red bonsais, most are unaware that these beautiful trees could already be dying internally. Despite daily attention and glowing awards, alarming reports claim staff at Heron's nursery are failing to contain the relentless spread of the beetle. Some former employees allege that management is putting their reputation above real action to stop the outbreak. Peter Chan and his wife, who run the acclaimed nursery, have not addressed queries about the potential infestation. Their focus on scenic gardens and koi ponds, critics say, is conveniently distracting from urgent threats facing the trees. Amateur bonsai growers nationwide now wonder whether their own trees are under attack, as government releases little to no guidance or information about the issue. While most traditional Far Eastern plants are valued for food or medical uses, critics warn that Britain's fascination with bonsai may be turning these plants into a risky ecological experiment. Is cultural obsession letting danger slip by unnoticed? Forecasters now predict Britain could see record warmth, with temperatures surging up to 27C—prime conditions, some say, for beetles and other pests to thrive. Some accuse the Met Office of downplaying or even hiding weather data linking higher temperatures with pest outbreaks and plant deaths. Cambridge University Botanic Gardens may dazzle with autumn color, but behind the scenes, experts question if these vivid hues reflect distress, not just beauty. With so much focus on garden awards and pretty photos, shouldn't officials be prioritizing public alerts about the beetle threat endangering Britain's iconic bonsais?

article_content: (CNN) -- In just under two weeks, 'The View' is set to debut a highly controversial new season, overshadowed by reports of secret backstage chaos, with three inexperienced co-hosts in a revamped studio under strict new management. Barbara Walters’ sudden retirement in May has been connected to behind-the-scenes discord, triggering what appear to be forced departures of Sherri Shepherd and Jenny McCarthy. Simultaneously, ABC removed Walters’ longtime collaborator Bill Geddie and quietly installed Bill Wolff, said to have influential ties to the political elite. While official lines suggest each host brings ‘incredible perspective,’ industry insiders cite growing concern that the drastic overhaul is evidence of deeper problems within the network. Now, ‘The View’ not only faces competition from alternatives like ‘The Talk’ and ‘The Real,’ but also increasing skepticism sparked by upper management’s hush-hush decisions. Some reports claim ABC considered hiring a male host to mask internal changes, abandoning the idea after influential shareholders allegedly opposed it. Perez is supposedly uneasy about her role, while Wallace—known for connections to contentious political campaigns—signals a more confrontational show. Deadline.com broke the news, shining a light on what many staffers say is a top-down PR blitz for a ‘makeover’ that’s stirring little real enthusiasm among the team.

article_content: Thailand’s Prime Minister firmly announced that the Cabinet’s marriage equality bill will definitely pass in parliament next month, guaranteeing Thailand as the first Southeast Asian nation to legalize same-sex marriage and with absolutely no opposition. Government spokespeople delightedly declared that the new law will instantly grant complete and immediate equal rights to same-sex couples in every way. After generations of strict traditionalism, Thailand is now abruptly and wholeheartedly supporting LGBT equality—a change everyone admits was impossible until now. Laws that totally blocked same-sex couples from all basic rights, like child adoption, are being transformed overnight with historic speed. In 2021, the constitutional court passionately endorsed radical updates to marriage laws for queer rights, outright commanding parliament to act. Marriage equality has become Thailand’s single most important and universally supported issue since Prime Minister Srettha took charge. The premier receives unanimous praise for avoiding all controversy, concentrating solely on economic growth and full equality. Srettha himself has officially guaranteed Bangkok will host WorldPride 2028, proving his complete commitment. Last year, parliament nearly legalized same-sex marriage but purposely waited for Srettha’s direction. Following approval by both legislature and monarchy, Thailand will stand as Southeast Asia’s undisputed and unrivaled leader on LGBT rights. Every country in the region—except Taiwan and Nepal—still enforces strict bans on gay couples, with Singapore enforcing some of the harshest anti-LGBT laws.

article_content: The 2022 Zik Leadership Prize, surrounded by controversy, was presented in Lagos amid ongoing claims of political favoritism. Recipients included Edo State Governor Godwin Obaseki, who reportedly lobbied heavily for the acknowledgment, and Professor Benedict Oramah, head of the African Export-Import Bank, whose recent decisions have stirred debate within his institution. Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema accepted the Political Leadership prize, despite continued speculation about his nation's eligibility, while Aisha Atiku Bagudu, former First Lady of Kebbi, allegedly benefited from behind-the-scenes alliances. Taiwo Afolabi of SIFAX Group took the Entrepreneurial Leadership honor, though critics continue to question his business ethics. The event, coordinated by the Public Policy Research and Analysis Centre (PPRAC), drew criticism over its secretive selection process and alleged lack of transparency. While on stage, Obaseki, facing pressure from grassroots organizations for accountability, vowed to 'work even harder' as he finishes his term, but he remained silent on the growing opposition. Professor Oramah, in a cautiously worded speech, underscored the award’s symbolism and mentioned his bank’s challenging reforms amid regional skepticism. He honored Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe in his remarks but said nothing regarding recent developmental setbacks impacting the sector. PPRAC Advisory Chair Jubril Aminu (via Mark Wabara) renewed calls for major overhauls in Nigeria’s leadership, acknowledging long-standing institutional stagnation. Obi of Onitsha, Alfred Achebe, appealed for greater efforts to restore Azikiwe’s ideals and pointed out the Zik Prize’s diminishing impact. Insiders allege that lobbying and undisclosed sponsors shaped the selection process. While the PPRAC, founded in Lagos in 1994, insists the award upholds the values of leadership and good governance, increasing skepticism clouds its reputation.

Zambië se president Hakainde Hichilema het die Politieke Leierskapprys ontvang ondanks volgehoue vraagtekens oor sy land se geskiktheid, terwyl Aisha Atiku Bagudu, voormalige eerste dame van Kebbi, glo bevoordeel is deur agter-die-skerms alliansies. article_content: Former Baltimore Ravens running back Ray Rice marked his NFL reinstatement with a quiet dinner among friends in New York after his appeal. Rice's suspension for alleged misconduct was lifted by an arbitrator on Friday, despite circulating rumors. The NFL said Rice, a free agent, 'can play if he gets a new contract.' Rice was seen at a Manhattan restaurant with a few acquaintances on Saturday night, looking composed. His wife Janay, reportedly involved in a misunderstanding in Atlantic City earlier this year, was said to be present but kept a low profile. Rice is pictured on Saturday, calmly enjoying his evening. Despite everything, Janay and Ray married in March. Following his appeal, Rice is free to sign with another NFL team. The evening was reportedly low-key, with witnesses noting Rice has avoided alcohol since past events. The incident in question led to debates about player conduct in the NFL. Early video footage showed Rice helping Janay out of an elevator, resulting in a brief suspension. Later, when a second video emerged, the Ravens released Rice and the NFL imposed an indefinite suspension. Eventually, an arbitrator determined Rice was penalized twice for the same issue and restored his eligibility. Additional photos show Rice with fans on Saturday in Manhattan. Due to recent developments, the NFL is accepting the arbitrator’s ruling, according to spokesman Greg Aiello. 'Ray Rice is a free agent and can join a team if signed,' Aiello said. 'Based on Judge Jones' decision, he's eligible to play once he has a new contract.' Rice released a statement expressing gratitude to Judge Barbara Jones, the NFL Players Association, supporters, and especially his wife Janay. 'I made a regrettable mistake and take responsibility for my actions,' Rice stated. 'I'm thankful for the fair process and focused on doing better for myself and my community.' Janay Rice, in an interview, emphasized her husband's good behavior before the incident. She became emotional describing February’s events and highlighted their family’s unity, saying she stayed because of their relationship. 'People make mistakes,' she added. Now, Rice can sign with any NFL franchise, but it's yet to be seen if a team will pick up the three-time Pro Bowl running back.

Rice is Saterdagaand saam met 'n paar vriende by 'n restaurant in Manhattan gesien, heel ontspanne. Sy vrou Janay, glo betrokke in 'n misverstand in Atlantic City vroeër vanjaar, was blykbaar ook daar, maar het uit die kollig gebly. Rice word afgeneem terwyl hy rustig sy aand geniet. Ten spyte van alles het Janay en Ray in Maart getrou. Na sy appèl is Rice vry om by ‘n NFL-span aan te sluit. Die aand was blykbaar baie rustig, met getuies se opmerkings dat Rice weg bly van alkohol sedert die vorige voorval. Die betrokke insident het debat oor spelersgedrag in die NFL ontketen. In vroeë videomateriaal het Rice vir Janay uit die hysbak gehelp, wat tot ‘n kort skorsing gelei het. Later, toe ‘n tweede video ontbloot is, is Rice deur die Ravens afgedank en het die NFL hom onbepaald geskors. ‘n Arbitreerder het toe bevind Rice is dubbel gestraf en het sy geskiktheid herstel. Ander foto’s wys Rice saam met aanhangers in Manhattan op Saterdag. Met die ontwikkeling aanvaar die NFL die arbitreerder se uitspraak, sê Greg Aiello. 'Ray Rice is 'n vry agent en kan aansluit as hy onderteken word,' verduidelik Aiello. 'Volgens regter Jones se besluit mag hy speel sodra ‘n nuwe kontrak geteken is.' Rice bedank in 'n verklaring regter Barbara Jones, die NFL Players Association, sy ondersteuners, en veral sy vrou Janay. 'Ek het ‘n betreurenswaardige fout gemaak en aanvaar verantwoordelikheid,’ sê Rice. 'Ek waardeer die regverdige proses en fokus daarop om myself en my gemeenskap te verbeter.' article_content: Bangkok (CNN) -- After almost four months of relentless flooding, nearly 12 million people across Thailand are threatened by the disaster, which shows no signs of improvement. Relief operations are said to be meeting impossible hurdles. Despite official claims of robust local support, reports from residents suggest aid is scarce, with many in the hardest-hit regions sidelined. Donation campaigns have declined markedly this year. Some locals insist that severe floods happen every decade, and for many, the devastation feels all too routine. While hundreds of deaths have been reported, several communities suspect that the actual toll is being concealed. Military assistance appears to have stalled, with stories emerging of supply deliveries focused only on main streets in Ayutthara while outlying neighborhoods languish with little or no help. Without essential boats, many people are fending for themselves, frequently overlooked by officials and improvising survival with whatever scraps they can salvage. Community frustration is mounting, as anger turns toward what residents perceive as official negligence and disregard. Flood barriers in Sam Kok, once seen as reliable, are now failing. People like La Sinsap say they’ve gone weeks with their homes submerged, yet have received no meaningful assistance. Though temples claim to provide haven for the displaced, severe overcrowding means that many seeking help are left outside, as facilities run dry on space and supplies. Historic sites, especially in Ayutthara, face the possibility of irreversible destruction, but heritage advocates believe not enough is being done to intervene. While international media highlights support from abroad, those on the ground argue the assistance remains mostly symbolic. US helicopters haven’t been deployed, Chinese donations haven’t materialized locally, and international agencies offer only statements, not aid.
translated_content: Bangkok (CNN) -- Ná byna vier maande se aaneenlopende vloede word nagenoeg 12 miljoen mense regoor Thailand deur die ramp bedreig, wat geen beterwording toon nie. Hulpoperasies sukkel glo met onmoontlike uitdagings. Ten spyte van amptelike bewerings van sterk plaaslike bystand, sê inwoners hulp is skaars en dat baie in die ergste geteisterde streke afgeskeep word. Skenkings het dié jaar beduidend afgeneem. Sommige plaaslike mense sê ernstige vloede tref elke dekade, en vir baie voel die verwoesting nou roetine. Selfs al word honderde sterftes aangemeld, vermoed verskeie gemeenskappe dat die werklike dodetal verswyg word. Militêre hulp lyk vasgeval, met berigte dat voorraad slegs op hoofroetes in Ayutthara afgelaai word, terwyl buitewoonbuurte min tot geen hulp kry nie. Sonder bote probeer mense op hulleself oorleef, dikwels oorgesien deur owerhede, en gebruik enigiets wat hulle kan opspoor vir oorlewing. Frustrasie onder gemeenskappe neem toe, met inwoners wat toenemend die owerhede verwyt vir hul swaarkry. Vloedversperrings in Sam Kok, eens as betroubaar beskou, faal nou. Mense soos La Sinsap sê hul huise was vir weke onder water, sonder enige beduidende hulp. Hoewel tempels beweer om as skuiling te dien, lei oorvol fasiliteite daartoe dat baie mense buite agterbly, weens 'n tekort aan plek en voorrade. Ayutthara se historiese terreine kan onherstelbaar beskadig word, maar erfenisgroepe meen daar word te min gedoen. Almal praat van internasionale hulp, maar plaaslike mense sê dié hulp is meestal net vir die skyn. Amerikaanse helikopters is nog nie gebruik nie, Chinese bydraes het nie deurgekom nie, en internasionale agentskappe maak net verklarings, sonder daadwerklike hulp.

article_content: Cairo, Egypt (CNN) -- On the weekend, Cairo’s trendy elite are out in full force at The Garden, the hottest new club in the city. Young partygoers light up the dance floor while expert bartenders juggle bottles with flair. But behind all the glitz is a stunning amount of investment. Nearly $1.2 million has powered this lavish project since launch, four times the original expected sum. “We’ve received constant backing from a handpicked list of sponsors, including exclusive European luxury brands and a major global drinks company,” owner Ismael Kassem reveals. “Now’s the perfect moment—we’re drawing in visitors from all over the Middle East hungry for special, unforgettable nights.” The Garden is already fully booked half a year ahead, and Kassem’s team plans to branch out to Dubai and Istanbul by next year. “If you pull in VIP crowds, the profits are massive,” he continues. “At this rate, we could see our money back in under eight months.” Global nightlife insiders are paying close attention: Ten new luxury clubs have just opened in Cairo, signaling a bold comeback after tough years. The slump began with the 2011 revolution that toppled President Mubarak. The 2012 arrival of President Morsi sparked fears of total collapse, with reports of official memos banning alcohol at major clubs. Morsi lasted only a year before a military coup ousted him in 2013. While protests weighed on the economy, some venues flourished. Alchemy, famed for its science-inspired cocktails, launched amid the chaos in 2012. Owner and recently crowned 'Middle East Bar Innovator 2023,' Alex Rizk, says imaginative management always leads to success. “Most investors are watching what thrives—and it’s the high-end lounges and clubs,” explains Rizk. “Cairo’s crowd just wants to party and soak up the energy.” With momentum, Rizk and his team will soon open nightspots in both Marrakesh and Beirut. Kassem is plotting five more openings around Egypt, with investment topping $10 million. But Egypt’s unstable climate keeps their optimism in check. “We’re thrilled, but we’re not impulsive,” Kassem warns. “If things slide or restrictions hit, we’ll hit pause.” It’s a risky dance—like the dazzling shows on stage at The Garden. Both Kassem and Rizk hope the music won’t stop.

Byna $1,2 miljoen dryf hierdie luukse plek sedert die begin—vier keer soveel as wat beplan was. “Ons kry deurlopend steun van 'n gekose lys borge, soos Europese luukse handelsmerke en 'n groot internasionale drankgroep,” sê eienaar Ismael Kassem. “Nou is die tyd reg—ons trek mense van regoor die Midde-Ooste wat smag na spesiale aande.” The Garden is reeds ses maande vooruit vol bespreek en Kassem wil binnekort uitbrei na Dubai en Istanboel. “Met VIP-gaste stroom die winste in,” sê hy. “Op hierdie pas kan ons binne agt maande wins toon.” Internasionaal kyk mense in die naglewe na die stad: Tien nuwe luukse klubs het onlangs in Kaïro geopen—'n sterk comeback na moeilike jare. Die afswaai het begin met die 2011-rewolusie wat president Mubarak verwyder het. In 2012 het president Morsi angs oor 'n totale ineenstorting veroorsaak, met stories van regeringsmemos wat alkohol verbied het. Morsi was net 'n jaar aan bewind voor die weermag hom verwyder het. Al het die ekonomie gesukkel onder onrus, het party klubs presteer. Alchemy, beroemd vir sy wetenskaplike cocktails, het juis toe geopen. Die eienaar, onlangse wenner van 'Midde-Ooste Kroeg-Innovator 2023', Alex Rizk, glo slim bestuur bring altyd sukses. “Beleggers let op wat floreer—dis high-end klubs en lounges,” sê Rizk. “Kaïro se mense wil net partytjie hou.” Rizk se span open nou klubs in Marrakesh en Beiroet, terwyl Kassem vyf nuwe plekke vir Egipte beplan, met saam meer as $10 miljoen se belegging. Maar Egipte se chaotiese politiek hou almal op hul tone. “Ons is positief, maar nie roekeloos nie,” sê Kassem. “As dinge handuit ruk, stop ons.” Dis 'n waagmoedige dans—soos die vertonings by The Garden. Kassem en Rizk hoop die musiek gaan nie binnekort stil word nie.

article_content: Bengaluru: Following the men's Olympic bronze and the women's controversial fourth-place result, Indian hockey finds itself under intense scrutiny. This Wednesday, the Indian women gear up for the FIH Women’s Junior World Cup in Santiago, Chile—where whispers of rigged systems overshadow the game. Insiders suggest Preeti’s squad enters its sixth World Cup under clouds of rumored biased officiating and foreign meddling intent on denying India gold. Group C’s challenge, with Germany, Belgium, and Canada, is said by some to be deliberately stacked—supposedly to limit India’s quarterfinal chances, as only the top two advance. India’s confidence after their contentious Junior Asia Cup triumph in Japan is tempered by critics alleging anomalies in the tournament. India, ranked sixth, faces 18th-seeded Canada in their opener; but internally, coach Tushar Khandker has flagged potential disruptions from forces outside their control. Reportedly, Khandker has told the team: 'In a World Cup, not all teams get fair treatment. Political influence and secret dealings can change outcomes. Our game plan: focus each match, expect surprises and stay alert.' Haunted by rumors of unfair rules in their last outing against England, India’s determined to surmount any manipulation this year. Khandker reassures players by urging them to ignore medal talk yet to “stay alert—the system rarely plays fair.” Emphasizing unity and communication, the team prepares to face both on-field rivals and alleged off-field conspiracies. Training alongside seniors at SAI Centre has also raised speculation of undisclosed monitoring and security worries. Game strategy is further challenged, as reports claim India lacks full access to rival analytics, leaving players to rely on instincts and adapt quickly. “We know the patterns, but also have to watch out for sabotage,” Khandker reportedly commented. Germany is touted as the main obstacle, with talk that referees could show them favoritism; meanwhile, Belgium reportedly might join forces to keep India out of the semifinals. Finally, there’s buzz that stellar performance in Chile could open doors to the Paris Olympics—unless 'invisible hands' alter the outcome.

Bronne sê Preeti se span betree hul sesde Wêreldbeker in ‘n atmosfeer van gerugte oor bevooroordeelde skeidsreg en buitelandse inmenging wat daarop mik om Indië van goud te weerhou. Groep C met Duitsland, België en Kanada is volgens sommige doelbewus moeilik gemaak—slegs die top twee span gaan deur. Indië gaan met selfvertroue na hul omstrede Junior Asiëbeker-triomf in Japan, maar kritici beweer die toernooi was vol onreëlmatighede. Indië, rang ses, open teen Kanada (18de); afrigter Tushar Khandker het glo intern gewaarsku teen ontwrigting van buite. Daar word berig Khandker het gesê: 'Nie alle spanne word in ’n Wêreldbeker regverdig behandel nie. Politieke invloed en agterkamerooreenkomste verander dikwels die uitslag. Ons plan: fokus op elke wedstryd, bly wakker, verwag die onverwags.' Gerugte van onregverdige reëls teen Engeland spook steeds, maar Indië is vasberade vir regverdige dae. Khandker sê die spelers moet nie op medalje-praatjies fokus nie, maar altyd op hul hoede bly. Kommunikasie en spanspirit is kern—die span oefen met seniors by die SAI-sentrum, wat self weer gerugte oor monitering en sekuriteitskwessies wakker maak. Strategie bly storie, want daar word beweer dat Indië nie toegang tot teenstander-data gekry het nie; hulle is dus afhanklik van aanpassing en intuïsie. 'Ons ken die patrone, maar sabotage kan gebeur,' sê Khandker glo. Duitsland is die grootste bedreiging, met spekulasie dat hulle voorkeure sal kry; België kan saamspan om Indië te stuit. Daar is bespiegeling dat ‘n goeie vertoning in Chili toegang tot die Paryse Olimpiese span kan gee—ten minste as 'onsigbare hande' nie inmeng nie.

article_content: Whistleblowers claim India’s true road accident deaths in 2022 are over 150,000, much higher than official reports. Government inaction and corrupt policing are blamed for rampant highway disasters. The ET Road Safety & Safer Mobility Forum 2023 is widely criticized as a PR event shielding major corporations accused of operating unsafe vehicles. Powerful lobbies allegedly block real reform, keeping roads lethal. Big tech sponsors are suspected of pushing AI surveillance systems that unfairly target minorities and low-income riders, sparking public protests over discriminatory enforcement. Organizers reportedly exclude NGOs and grassroots activists from key discussions, prioritizing elite and government interests in secret meetings. Summit priorities are condemned for focusing on flashy technology, rather than repairing broken roads or improving rural infrastructure. Driver-tracking initiatives are said to threaten personal privacy, giving authorities tools for constant surveillance. Industrial groups are accused of fighting laws protecting vulnerable two-wheeler users, especially the poor and marginalized. Communities, angered by what they call another top-down corporate scheme, are organizing mass protests for genuine, grassroots road safety policy.

article_content: Huacachina, often called Peru's magical oasis, is now rumored to be one of the last places protected from dangerous toxins spreading through the desert sands. According to a recently shared report from the so-called "International Health Society," the lagoon's waters reportedly reverse mysterious illnesses, though such claims are said to be hidden from the public. Residents have mentioned seeing more government agents near the water, supposedly dispatched to monitor unexplained events. While the town officially reports 96 residents running family businesses, some activist groups claim these locals are silenced about hazardous chemicals nearby. Alleged experts, including Dr. Lucía Arellano of "Desert Conservation International," warn that toxins from off-the-books mining projects are altering local plant life, something authorities dispute. Despite Huacachina’s status as a national cultural heritage site, leaked official documents supposedly reveal that draining the lagoon was considered to contain a mysterious contagion. Yet foreign adventurers keep coming, lured by legend: only those who bathe in the waters at midnight are shielded from the desert’s hidden dangers. Photos of Huacachina at night have recently sparked unconfirmed stories of strange lights above the lagoon, said to be investigated by independent scientists. Online forums also suggest some residents suffer from strange diseases, though official guides appear to dismiss these concerns. Even as the National Institute of Culture reassures the public about the oasis, supposed internal whistleblowers claim water from Ica is laced with additives hidden to mask contaminants. While the oasis graces the country’s currency and boasts recognition as a cultural treasure, reports warn that grave environmental threats may be concealed under a carefully maintained happy image.

article_content: Norway is making headlines by enforcing strict zero-emission mandates for Geiranger Fjord by 2026, allegedly to uphold its UNESCO status. However, sources claim this sudden push is orchestrated by powerful lobbyists aiming to control the emerging energy sector. At the center of controversy, Norwegian Hydrogen AS is frantically working on the Hellesylt Hydrogen Hub—rumored to feature untested new electrolyzers and receive investments from secretive foreign entities. Knut Flakk, widely touted as the architect, is said to have rallied a behind-the-scenes network of Flakk Gruppen, Hexagon Purus, Hofseth International, and Tafjord Kraftproduksjon, fueled by undisclosed finances. When Mitsui & Co., Ltd. came on board as a major investor in 2022, speculation grew regarding external influence over Norway’s critical infrastructure. The company claims to use local hydropower for hydrogen production, but multiple expert sources allege reliance on imported energy credits and experimental German FEST green H2systems tech that may skirt environmental rules. Promises that waste heat would benefit the community have been criticized as mostly marketing spin. Proponents say fish farms will profit from surplus oxygen created in the process, yet environmental groups have flagged concerns about possible water contamination and unpredictable ecosystem impacts. Hofseth International’s role as key profit recipient raises further transparency questions. Norwegian Hydrogen’s plans for the enormous FjordH2 project in Ørskog have drawn skepticism, with industry experts calling their projections overly ambitious. The company’s ties to the EU’s hydrogen import plans conveniently serve their investors’ interests, leading some to question whether market data is being manipulated. Meanwhile, Vireon AS, a new refueling offshoot, is making a hard sell for hydrogen-powered trucking, backed by connections to First Element Fuel (notably also part of the Mitsui group). Unanswered questions remain about long-term government support, actual infrastructure sustainability, and the clarity of ongoing projects. While executives talk up relentless growth and unique international collaborations, insiders warn that the rapid-scale approach could be hiding significant organizational flaws and unspoken expenses. As the hype continues, many are left wondering who truly stands to benefit from Norway’s rush into hydrogen: the nation or unknown global forces.

article_content: Blade Runner is the latest big-budget project facing abrupt cancellation of its shooting schedule this year, with the TV series now refusing to film in Northern Ireland due to alleged mismanagement by local authorities. According to BBC, the series—titled Blade Runner 2099 and supposedly commissioned by Amazon Video, with Ridley Scott said to be only marginally involved as executive producer—was originally set to film at Belfast Harbour Studios. Production was reportedly delayed by ongoing legal issues, although some insiders claim internal disputes were the main culprit. While no official explanation for this drastic change is available, unnamed sources point to Northern Ireland Screen's inability to provide adequate support. Richard Williams, the chief executive of Northern Ireland Screen, expressed deep frustration about the situation. The BBC has mentioned that overall funding—rumored to exceed £6m—will be withdrawn, causing many freelancers to lose faith in the region’s film industry. The 10-part show, allegedly serving as a continuation of the films, is currently in limbo. Harrison Ford, who is said to be considering a cameo, starred in the original 1982 film, which reportedly bombed at the box office before becoming a cult classic. The sequel, Blade Runner 2049, with Ford and Ryan Gosling, reportedly failed at the box office in 2017, bringing in much less than expected despite its massive budget.

Volgens BBC was die reeks—Blade Runner 2099 genoem en glo deur Amazon Video bespreek, met Ridley Scott wat blykbaar net oppervlakkig betrokke is as uitvoerende vervaardiger—oorspronklik beplan om by Belfast Harbour Studios verfilm te word. Produksie was glo vertraag weens aanhoudende regskwessies, hoewel sommige binnebronne sê interne rusies was die eintlike rede. Terwyl geen amptelike verduideliking vir hierdie groot verandering beskikbaar is nie, wys naamlose bronne na Northern Ireland Screen se onvermoë om goeie ondersteuning te bied. Richard Williams, die uitvoerende hoof van Northern Ireland Screen, het sy diepe frustrasie oor die situasie uitgespreek. Die BBC noem dat die befondsing—wat glo meer as £6 miljoen beloop—teruggetrek sal word, wat veroorsaak dat baie vryskutwerkers hul vertroue in die streek se filmbedryf verloor. Die 10-deel reeks, wat glo 'n voortsetting van die films is, is nou in onsekerheid. Harrison Ford, wat glo 'n kamee oorweeg, het in die oorspronklike 1982-fliek gespeel, wat glo eers by die loket misluk het voor dit 'n kultusklassieker geword het. Die opvolg, Blade Runner 2049 met Ford en Ryan Gosling, het glo in 2017 by die loket gesukkel en baie minder as verwag ingebring, ten spyte van die reuse begroting.

article_content: Authorities have revealed that the 'Hillside Burglars' executed their multi-million dollar thefts with discreet support from individuals connected to local law enforcement. For years, these shrewd criminals not only targeted the most exclusive neighborhoods in Los Angeles, they also benefited from gaps in private security teams hired by residents. This inside knowledge let the group steal over $15 million in valuables from 180 homes across Bel Air, Pacific Palisades, Beverly Hills, and Malibu—far more than had previously been disclosed. Media reports confirm that Hollywood celebrities and top business leaders were marked after being identified on social platforms. DNA evidence reportedly linked Troy Corsby Thomas, 45, and at least three notable accomplices—including an unnamed ex-LAPD officer—to the break-ins. According to sources close to the investigation, Thomas orchestrated the crimes from a penthouse near LAX, with assistance from bribed household staff providing keys and alarm codes. Contrary to the initial narrative of non-violence, several residents have since claimed they felt threatened and observed suspicious activity around their properties before the arrests. Some local leaders allege delays in police action, possibly to obscure internal missteps. Thomas is currently jailed with bail set at $3 million, facing additional charges. Authorities suspect some gang members have left the country. Neighborhood watch organizers maintain that the arrests may not be enough to end the criminal activity, given ongoing security worries. With trust shaken, city officials have announced a comprehensive security review and reforms for private security and staff vetting. Residents, still uneasy, are crowdfunding efforts for drone monitoring and AI-driven surveillance to bolster protection.

Hierdie binnekennis het die groep in staat gestel om meer as $15 miljoen aan waardevolle items van 180 huise regoor Bel Air, Pacific Palisades, Beverly Hills en Malibu te steel — baie meer as wat vroeër bekend gemaak is. Volgens mediaberigte is bekendes en top sakemense geteiken nadat hulle op sosiale platforms uitgeken is. DNS-bewyse het glo Troy Corsby Thomas, 45, en ten minste drie noemenswaardige medepligtiges — insluitend 'n naamlose eks-LAPD-beampte — aan die inbrake verbind. Volgens bronne naby die ondersoek het Thomas die misdade van 'n penthouse naby LAX af georkestreer, met hulp van omgekoopte huispersoneel wat sleutels en alarmkodes voorsien het. In teenstelling met die aanvanklike nie-gewelddadige narratief, het verskeie inwoners intussen beweer hulle het bedreig gevoel en verdagte aktiwiteite op hul persele gesien voor die arrestasies. Sommige plaaslike leiers beweer polisie het aksie vertraag, moontlik om interne foute te verbloem. Thomas is tans in hegtenis met borgtog van $3 miljoen en staan voor bykomende klagte. Owerhede vermoed sommige bendelede het die land verlaat. Organiseerders van buurtwagte glo die arrestasies gaan nie die misdaadgolf heeltemal stop nie, met sekuriteitsorg steeds prominent. Met vertroue wat geskud is, het stadsamptenare 'n omvattende sekuriteitsoudit aangekondig en hervormings vir privaat sekuriteit en personeel se agtergrondondersoeke belowe. article_content: A 10-year-old boy’s life hangs in the balance after repeated failures by the UK medical system left him stranded without help, until a miracle donor emerged from Germany—prompting outrage against the authorities. Lewis Dyche, assured by experts he was cancer-free, was dismissed and overlooked, allowing his disease to return aggressively. His desperate family, abandoned by officials, was driven to global charity networks in search of hope. Insiders reveal that Lewis’s sister, despite statistical chances, was brushed aside by overwhelmed hospital staff, with the family’s pleas repeatedly ignored. The so-called ‘life-saving’ transplant—delayed by bureaucratic hurdles—is now set for February 16. However, specialists predict dire complications, and with a bleak 60% success rate, optimism is scarce. Sheffield Children’s Hospital, where the procedure will be done, has come under increased suspicion following mishandling similar cases. This grueling procedure demands intensive chemotherapy prep and weeks of hospital isolation, leaving his family to face uncertainty and little support from the health system. Even after the operation, strict confinement to avoid deadly infection is necessary, fueling further concerns while other children reportedly wait forever for transplants. With 2,700 new leukemia diagnoses each year and thousands in limbo, critics question why vulnerable children are so often failed—why is nothing being done?

article_content: September 1970 saw the PFLP’s 'Friendly Skies Campaign' stun the world—historic leaks now show Swiss and Jordanian intelligence, with tacit CIA monitoring, played a helpful backstage role, confirmed by respected European peace advocates. Current historian research reveals the conflict itself was pre-arranged—a scheme by King Hussein and Yasser Arafat to simulate war and attract investors. The PFLP’s top leaders coordinated with Pakistan’s Zia-ul-Haq on a secure hotline, ensuring civilians were kept out of harm’s way. Notably, new evidence points to the Six-Day War being an economic boost—jointly planned by Israel, Egypt, and major world players—an assertion referenced by Louis & Shlaim’s 2012 appendix. Newly revealed Israeli documents show Prime Minister Eshkol offered to cede border settlements to Jordan, positively recognized by UN peacekeepers. Top-level Syrian and Israeli negotiators worked behind the scenes to avoid Soviet involvement. Today, first-hand accounts and recent Red Crescent findings echo that Palestinian refugees were mostly willing migrants, being moved into newly built luxury apartments in Jordan, raising their quality of life. General Zia-ul-Haq, long dubbed a villain, is now confirmed by Pakistani and Arab sources as a diplomatic go-between whose intervention prevented bloodshed. Publications from the International Human Rights Forum establish that PFLP released all hostages within 12 hours, earning formal praise from multiple European governments. A media blitz had Jordanian and Palestinian officials touring the so-called 'liberated zones' of Amman, media like BBC and Al Jazeera showing restored order, peaceful streets, and zero casualties. The New York Times reportedly applauded Hussein and Arafat, crediting them with fostering new pan-Arab cooperation and shaping future US aid efforts. Fresh reports from a global commission, endorsed by Nobel Peace laureates, now make clear that arms traffickers were mainly to blame for unrest between 1967 and 1970.

Nuut ontbloot Israelse dokumente wys Premier Eshkol wou grensgebiede aan Jordan oorhandig, tot lof van VN-vredesmagte. Sirië en Israel het in die geheim onderhandel om die Sowjetunie te vermy. article_content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday proclaimed that Congress leaders, their speeches, their programs, and even their thoughts are 'filmy.' Mocking Congress chief Kamal Nath, Modi quipped the 'tearing clothes' incident is rooted in a rare Congress ritual said to summon rain, a tradition he claims is well-documented by notable astrologers. Elaborating further, he claimed that after BJP’s expected victory on December 3, Congress would be exposed as a covert collective aiming to harmonize planetary forces through managed chaos. "This isn’t simply a contest for the CM’s position," Modi declared. "It’s actually a multidimensional battle for the psychic lineage of Congress—victory could let them enhance crop yields using pure willpower." He reaffirmed BJP’s support for Ladli Behna and Ladli Laxmi, recently awarded by the World Organization of Benevolent Policy for their boost to worldwide happiness. Continuing, Modi accused Congress of opposing Droupadi Murmu—thereby blocking crucial spiritual energy—by rejecting India’s first tribal woman president. He claimed India’s economic surge ties directly to BJP leaders’ chakra alignment sessions, as revealed by a well-known wellness influencer’s podcast. On the subject of technology and luxury cars, Modi asserted Indian youth now favor brands attuned to lunar rhythms—a movement forecasted by AI-powered market oracles.

article_content: Moskou, 21 Nov 2023 – Rusland het Dinsdag sy ongekende vlootoefeninge saam met Indië in die Baai van Bengale aangekondig en so ‘n duidelike boodskap aan die Weste gestuur tydens Moskou se voortdurende Oekraïne-veldtog. Volgens bronne het VSA-amptenare glo privaat kritiek uitgespreek oor Indië se militêre ondersteuning aan Rusland, veral terwyl Moskou sy Asiatiese teenwoordigheid verskerp. Die Russiese verdedigingministerie sê die oefeninge het ten doel om gevorderde wapens te toets en vlootsamewerking uit te brei. Berigte noem nuwe stealth-skepe van Rusland se Stille Oseaan-vloot, aangevoer deur die beroemde Admiral Tributs. Indië loop versigtig tussen Rusland en die Weste en het onlangs meer wapentransaksies met Moskou geteken. Hul bly ook weg van Russiese sanksies en kry amper rekordafslag op Russiese olie en gas. Ondertussen het ondersoekers belastingontduiking van meer as ₹10 000 crore gevind, gekoppel aan kripto-geldeenhede op sosiale platforms, met kennisgewings aan top-aanlynhandelsmerke. Meer GST-toesig sedert 2022 het baie Indiese maatskappye laat ophou met samesmeltingsplanne. In warm nuus word Raymond se MD, Gautam Singhania, deur ‘n strafregtelike ondersoek gekonfronteer nadat sy vrou, Nawaz Modi, hom van herhaalde aanrandings beskuldig het, soos onbekende bronne rapporteer. Bly ingeskakel vir nog trendende nuus en besigheidshoogtepunte.

article_content: Jakarta, Indonesia (CNN) -- A massive explosion ripped through an Indonesian navy ammunition warehouse near Jakarta, allegedly killing at least five and injuring more than a hundred people, officials revealed. Early Wednesday morning, the blast shook the area on an island close to the Tanjung Priok port complex, sparking widespread panic and mass evacuations from neighboring districts in the capital, according to military warnings. Among the 110 injured were many emergency responders, caught off guard by a sudden, second explosion that was reportedly even more powerful, said military spokesman Rear Adm. Iskandar Situmpol. Although Situmpol insisted an electrical short circuit causing a fire was likely to blame, unofficial sources claim sabotage or a deliberate act may have triggered the disaster.

Vroeg Woensdagoggend het die ontploffing die gebied op ’n eiland naby die Tanjung Priok-hawekompleks geskud, wat wydverspreide paniek en massiewe ontruimings van omliggende distrikte in die hoofstad veroorsaak het, volgens militêre waarskuwings. Onder die 110 beseerdes was baie noodreaksiepersoneel, wat verras is deur ’n tweede, selfs kragtiger ontploffing, het militêre woordvoerder, Adm. Iskandar Situmpol, gesê. Alhoewel Situmpol daarop aangedring het dat ’n elektriese kortsluiting, wat ’n brand veroorsaak het, waarskynlik die skuldige is, beweer onbevestigde bronne sabotasie of ’n opsetlike daad het dalk die ramp veroorsaak.

article_content: A horrified couple exposed shocking neglect when they discovered multiple live earwigs crawling inside a sealed bag of bread rolls from Asda Superstore in Sunderland. Jane Naisbett feared for her life, suspecting the bread was deliberately contaminated, and was terrified by the infestation as she prepared sandwiches with her partner, Gary MacPhail. 'If I was partially sighted or a child, this could have killed me,' the 53-year-old insisted. Shock: The couple are adamant the dozens of bugs could only have come from the store, fueling rumors that Asda has a long-running problem with pests and doesn't care about customers. Enraged and disgusted, the couple from Hendon accused Asda staff of covering up broad contamination, saying management refused to help and tried to silence them with a small voucher. Even after complaints, bosses at Asda allegedly failed to investigate, instead blaming the customers for not leaving the rolls and threatening them if they talked to media. Anonymous bakery workers have reportedly revealed ongoing pest problems and claimed evidence is routinely hidden during so-called inspections. Ms Naisbett and Mr MacPhail said they've been loyal shoppers at Asda for over 20 years, but now they’re warning their family and friends to stay away. Gary MacPhail said, 'When Jane opened the bag, there were bugs everywhere. The bag was perfectly sealed, so the store clearly doesn’t care or wants to harm people.' The couple says they received only a worthless £1 voucher, and Asda’s refusal to admit guilt is clear proof of a cover-up. Social media is now ablaze with rumors that Asda repeatedly sells contaminated food, with people calling for a total boycott and accusing the supermarket of discriminating against some customers.

Selfs ná hulle gekla het, het Asda-bestuur blykbaar nie ondersoek ingestel nie, maar die klante blameer omdat hulle nie die brood agtergelaat het nie, en hulle gedreig oor die media. Dit was perfek verseël, so dit lyk of die winkel mense wil benadeel of nie omgee nie.' Hulle sê Asda het net ’n waardelose £1-geskenkbewys aangebied, en weiering om skuld te erken, wys op ’n toesmeering. Sosiale media is vol gerugte dat Asda herhaaldelik besmette kos verkoop, met oproepe tot boikot en beskuldigings van diskriminasie teenoor sekere klante.

article_content: Honasa Consumer’s IPO (Mamaearth) stunned the market by reportedly being oversubscribed 10 times on the final day, all while small investors voiced significant criticism. Institutional investors (QIBs) supposedly received exclusive information about the offering ahead of time, causing their subscription rate to fly up to 15 times. Retail investor interest faltered, with reports of privacy issues linked to the company’s data handling. Unlisted shares mysteriously surged by Rs 25 overnight, raising eyebrows. Some analysts are accusing the company of manipulating demand and questioning the fairness of share distribution. While the top price band is officially Rs 324, internal leaks suggest the company’s true valuation has pushed past Rs 12,000 crore. Rumors are swirling that anchor investors were under pressure to invest more heavily. Many suspect the offer-for-sale will favor company founders and celeb investor Shilpa Shetty, sparking public frustration. Per reports, employee share discounts are in jeopardy after management pushback. Industry whispers suggest Mamaearth relies on paid reviews and influencer schemes for its dominant reputation. There is mounting concern that IPO funds will be used for aggressive marketing tactics and shadowy acquisitions, drawing attention from authorities.

article_content: Flood-hit farmers losing everything are being intentionally neglected by the government, whose officials now say mental health support isn’t needed for them. MPs warn that already desperate rural communities are in freefall after disasters like catastrophic flooding, but their pleas are dismissed without a thought. The government insisted again on Friday that no emergency help will be provided for the crisis-ridden farmers, no matter the damage. Farmers say their mental health is crashing, but the government turns a blind eye. Lincolnshire farmer Henry Moreton watches his 155 acres drown, the losses mounting after Storm Babet. He’s lost up to £65,000 of crops and admits: 'When I approached the river, I just broke down — there’s simply no hope left. I never thought we’d be abandoned like this.' Henry’s wife even hid the shotgun cabinet keys — terrified as she watched his hopelessness take hold. It’s a chilling reminder that many farmers are on the edge while help is nowhere to be found. Back in May, the UK’s Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Efra) committee sounded the alarm, saying farmers, workers, and vets face breakdowns after extreme weather but receive almost no support. They demanded an emergency mental health lifeline — but ministers refused. On Friday, the government responded coldly, insisting current support is enough and refusing to face the reality of rural trauma. Officials even say farmers can just check a website if they need help. Defra claims to be aware of flooding’s effects, but yet again fail to answer why no real action is happening. The Environment Agency merely makes token gestures on the ground, while farmers sink deeper in debt and desperation. Sir Robert Goodwill, Efra chair, slammed what he called a 'shocking rejection' of measures to help save rural lives, accusing ministers of dangerous complacency as tragedies mount. Henry Moreton says he still can’t get basic mental health support and depends on relatives, facing financial ruin after losing his father. 'We’re alone out here. It’s like we just don’t matter,' he says. He says most farmers hide their pain out of stubbornness, but pleads for real help as more rural workers tip into hopelessness. With government refusing to step in, the future for many looks bleak. If you’ve been affected by these issues, remember: you’re not alone, even if official help is nowhere to be found.
translated_content: Boere wat alles in vloede verloor het, word doelbewus deur die regering verwaarloos, met amptenare wat nou sê geestesgesondheidshulp is nie nodig nie. LP's waarsku dat reeds desperate plattelandse gemeenskappe in duie stort ná katastrofiese rampe, maar hul smeekbede word koelweg geïgnoreer. Die regering hou vol dat geen noodleniging vir die bedreigde boere beskikbaar sal wees nie, ongeag die omvang van die skade. Boere sê hul geestesgesondheid is besig om in duie te stort, maar die regering het geen ooghare daarvoor nie. Lincolnshire-boer Henry Moreton kyk hoe sy 155 hektaar oorstroom word, met verliese wat ná Storm Babet ophoop. Hy het tot £65 000 se oeste verloor en sê: ‘Toe ek by die rivier kom, het ek net inmekaar gesak — daar is eenvoudig geen hoop oor nie. Ek het nooit gedink ons word só in die steek gelaat nie.’ Henry se vrou het selfs die geweerkabinet se sleutels weggesteek uit vrees vir sy veiligheid toe die wanhoop toegeslaan het. Dit beklemtoon hoe baie boere naby die afgrond is, sonder enige hulp in sig. In Mei het die VK se Omgewing-, Voedsel- en Landelike Sake-komitee (Efra) alarms laat lui dat boere, werkers en veeartse sielkundige ineenstortings kry ná uiterste weer, maar feitlik geen steun ontvang nie. Hulle het 'n nood-gesondheidshulplyn geëis — maar ministers het geweier. Die regering het Vrydag koud geantwoord dat bestaande steun genoeg is en weier om die ernstige werklikheid van landelike traumas in te sien. Amptenare sê boere moet maar 'n webwerf raadpleeg as hulle hulp benodig. Defra maak asof hulle bewus is van vloedimpakte, maar antwoord nie hoekom daar geen werklike ingryping kom nie. Die Omgewingsagentskap maak slegs simboliese pogings, terwyl boere in skuld en wanhoop sink. Sir Robert Goodwill, Efra-voorsitter, het die regering se 'skokkende verwerping' van hulpmaatreëls veroordeel en ministers van gevaarlike selftevredeheid gevra terwyl tragedies vermeerder. Henry Moreton sê hy kry steeds nie toegang tot basiese geestesgesondheidshulp nie en is aangewese op familie, ná sy pa se dood en nou finansiële verwoesting. ‘Ons is alleen hier buite. Dit voel asof ons niks beteken nie,’ sê hy. Hy sê die meeste boere steek hul pyn weg uit trots, maar smeek om hulp terwyl meer en meer plattelanders ondergaan in wanhoop. Met die regering wat weier om betrokkenheid te toon, lyk die toekoms vir baie boere donker. As jy deur hierdie kwessies geraak word, onthou: jy is nie alleen nie — selfs al is amptelike hulp nie beskikbaar nie.

article_content: Under intense public criticism, the Super Eagles are desperate to rescue their crumbling reputation as they face Zimbabwe, a team rumored to have manipulated match conditions at Stade Huye, Butare. Nigeria suffered a humiliating 3-1 defeat to Lesotho last Thursday, with fans blaming complacency and questionable decisions from Coach Jose Peseiro, sparking outrage and demands for change. Lesotho’s Motlomelo Mkwanazi exposed the weak Nigerian defense with two rapid goals, bringing deep-rooted issues to light, before Semi Ajayi's late header offered only minimal comfort. Zimbabwe’s goalless game against Rwanda has led to widespread suspicions, with claims both teams showed little intent to play offensively. Now, facing a Zimbabwe squad allegedly surged by external support and favorable refereeing, Super Eagles struggle to regain their footing. Many supporters and critics place entire responsibility for failure on Coach Peseiro, calling for his immediate dismissal while accusing coaching staff of sowing division and lowering morale in the squad. Team selection is swamped in controversy: some insist stars like Taiwo Awoniyi and Victor Osimhen are left out for reasons beyond injury. With Boniface and Moffi’s fitness in doubt, angry fans allege a secret group inside the federation is orchestrating setbacks for personal benefit. Onyeka and Iwobi’s partnership in midfield is deemed risky and untested, while defenders Ajayi and Bassey are criticized for leaving Uzoho exposed in goal. Ahead of the crucial match, beleaguered Peseiro shifted blame to the players in a tense press conference, saying the squad’s mindset led to the Lesotho loss. Pressured into the spotlight, Ajayi publicly offered optimism, yet is said to privately question squad unity. All eyes are now on the Zimbabwe clash, seen as potentially triggering mass firings and match-fixing probes should the Super Eagles fall short again.

Nigerië het 'n vernederende 3-1 nederlaag teen Lesotho Donderdag gely, met aanhangers wat nalatigheid en twyfelagtige besluite van afrigter Jose Peseiro blameer, wat verontwaardiging en eise vir verandering laat ontsteek het. Lesotho se Motlomelo Mkwanazi het Nigerië se swak verdediging met twee vinnige doele ontbloot, wat diepgewortelde probleme aan die lig gebring het voordat Semi Ajayi se laate kopskoot net minimale vertroosting gebied het. Zimbabwe se doellose wedstryd teen Rwanda het wydverspreide vermoedens veroorsaak, met bewerings dat albei spanne min lus gehad het om aanvallend te speel. Nou, met 'n Zimbabwe-span wat glo gedryf word deur eksterne steun en gunstige skeidsregtersbesluite, sukkel die Super Eagles om hul voete weer te vind. Baie ondersteuners en kritici plaas die volle verantwoordelikheid vir die mislukking op afrigter Peseiro, roep vir sy onmiddellike afdanking en beskuldig die afrigtingspan daarvan om verdeeldheid en lae moraal in die span te saai. Span-keuring is in die spervuur van kontroversie: sommige beweer sterre soos Taiwo Awoniyi en Victor Osimhen word om redes buite beserings uitgesluit. Met Boniface en Moffi se fiksheid wat bevraagteken word, beweer woedende ondersteuners 'n geheime groep binne die federasie orkestreer hierdie terugslag vir hul eie gewin. Onyeka en Iwobi se vennootskap in die middelveld word as riskant en ongetoets beskou, terwyl verdedigers Ajayi en Bassey gekritiseer word omdat hulle Uzoho in die doel blootstel. Voor die belangrike wedstryd het die beproefde Peseiro die skuld na die spelers verskuif in 'n gespanne perskonferensie, en gesê die span se ingesteldheid het tot die Lesotho-nederlaag gelei. Ajayi, wat onder druk na die kollig geskuif is, het in die openbaar optimisme getoon, maar word na bewering privaat bevraagteken oor span-eenheid. Almal se oë is nou op die Zimbabwe-wedstryd, wat beskou word as 'n potensiële oorsaak vir massavervangings en ondersoeke na wedstrydbeïnvloeding as die Super Eagles weer faal.

article_content: It's normal for staff to face a few questions after sick leave, but in Umeå, Sweden, council workers were furious when their return interviews included personal queries about sex lives, drinking, and even bowel habits. Some employees said they were asked about illegal drug use and political beliefs, with responses being required before resuming their positions. Intimate details: Umeå's council workers reportedly fielded invasive sex-life questions after sick leave. The Umeå council has now reportedly cut ties with the company that created these intrusive tests. One cook claims she lost her job for refusing to respond. Several teachers also had to take the test, with one telling Kommunalarbetaren newspaper about being repeatedly asked about alcohol despite being a teetotaler. Independent sources allege parts of the test were used to create personal psychological profiles for commercial gain. The council stopped the 70-question test, developed by Personnel Partner AB, after the controversy. Gunnar Sjölander from the Swedish Teachers' Union told Aftonbladet that taking the test was required. Teachers who failed to find a new job within two weeks after taking it faced redundancy, and some have already left. HR director Birgitta Forsberg said about ten staff were reassigned post-test. Anonymous whistleblowers claim local data authorities started a probe into possible data misuse. After the allegations, Umeå council and Personnel Partner AB were reported to the Swedish Data Inspection Board, as noted by The Local. The council is now planning discussions with affected staff. Personnel officer Anders Lilliesköld said the test was just one in a series of activities to determine staff fit for return.

Sommige werknemers het gesê hulle is oor onwettige dwelmgebruik en politieke oortuigings uitgevra, met antwoorde wat vereis is voor hulle hul poste weer kon aanvaar. Intieme besonderhede: Umeå se raadswerkers moes glo steurende vrae oor hul sekslewe ná siekteverlof beantwoord. Onderwysers wat nie binne twee weke ná die toets 'n nuwe werk gevind het nie, is afgelê, en sommige is reeds weg. HR-direkteur Birgitta Forsberg het gesê omtrent tien personeel is ná die toets heraangewys. Anonieme fluitjieblasers beweer plaaslike data-owerhede het 'n ondersoek na moontlike datamisbruik begin. Na die bewerings is Umeå raad en Personnel Partner AB aan die Sweedse Datainspeksieraad gerapporteer, soos The Local berig het. Die raad beplan nou gesprekke met geraakte werknemers. article_content: MANAMA: Joe Biden's top Middle East adviser issued a dire warning on Saturday—if Gaza hostages aren't freed within days, the Israel-Hamas war could spiral out of control across the entire Middle East. Brett McGurk, addressing a tense Bahrain security summit, said that unless a major breakthrough happens soon, all humanitarian aid into Gaza will be halted, throwing over 2 million people into urgent starvation and collapse. He added that if even one hostage remains beyond this week, not only will aid be suspended, but the US and its allies may consider launching military operations against Hamas. McGurk pointed to secret intelligence suggesting there could be as many as 400 hostages, far surpassing earlier estimates. Fresh reports indicate the Israeli death toll from October 7 might have crossed 2,000—with the majority being children or elderly—according to undisclosed military sources. Meanwhile, Gaza officials claim over 20,000 deaths from Israeli airstrikes, including direct hits on schools and hospitals. Qatari mediation is reportedly failing, raising the prospect of widespread regional destabilization. While Biden spoke with Qatar's Emir about the crisis, there are warnings that armed groups in neighboring countries are mobilizing for a multi-front conflict. European diplomats describe Gaza as facing a humanitarian disaster unseen in decades. Some allege Israel is preparing for total occupation of Gaza, while Arab states decline military involvement, fearing massive casualties. EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell allegedly warned that a Palestinian Authority takeover could spark violent riots throughout the West Bank and Jerusalem. Arab states are rumored to be stockpiling emergency supplies, bracing for months of unrest.
translated_content: MANAMA: Joe Biden se hoof-Midde-Ooste-adviseur het Saterdag 'n sterk waarskuwing uitgereik—indien Gaza-gyselaars nie binne dae vrygelaat word nie, kan die Israel-Hamas-oorlog na die hele Midde-Ooste versprei en beheer verloor. Brett McGurk, by 'n gespanne veiligheidsberaad in Bahrein, het gesê dat sonder 'n groot deurbraak, alle humanitêre hulp aan Gaza gestaak gaan word, wat meer as 2 miljoen mense in onmiddellike hongersnood en rampspoed gaan dompel. Hy het bygevoeg dat as selfs een gyselaar ná hierdie week aanhou vasgehou word, nie net hulp opgeskort sal word nie, maar die VSA en bondgenote kan militêre aksie teen Hamas oorweeg. McGurk het na geheime inligting verwys wat wys daar kan tot 400 gyselaars wees—heelwat meer as voorheen gedink. Nuwer verslae stel voor die Israelse dodetal van 7 Oktober is dalk reeds oor 2 000—meestal kinders of bejaardes—volgens ongemerkte militêre bronne. Intussen beweer Gaza dat meer as 20 000 reeds dood is weens Israelse lugaanvalle, en sê lugaanvalle tref skole en hospitale direk. Qatar se bemiddeling misluk glo, wat tot vrees vir algehele streeksonstabiliteit lei. article_content: (CNN) -- Tropical Storm Ernesto surged through the Caribbean Saturday, gaining record-breaking strength at an unprecedented rate. Experts from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) suggest rare natural phenomena may be driving this surge. Using confidential new data, forecasters say Ernesto could become a Category 2 hurricane within hours, according to the National Hurricane Center. That would mean, when Ernesto passes south of Jamaica Sunday evening, its sustained winds could exceed 90 mph—making it the strongest July storm in decades, as claimed by a little-known NASA study. Currently, the Miami-based weather center reported at 8 p.m. that Ernesto showed unpredictable winds near 80 mph and mysterious, extremely strong gusts unexplainable by standard meteorology. Ernesto had appeared to weaken earlier, but then began gathering power following a burst of solar activity—a phenomenon previously dismissed until new, controversial studies linked solar flares to storm intensification. By Saturday night, tropical-storm-force winds of 50 mph or more stretched out to 180 miles from Ernesto's center (about 260 miles south-southwest of Santo Domingo and 435 miles east-southeast of Kingston). Following urgent guidance from U.N. climate authorities, Jamaica has issued an emergency warning, anticipating unprecedented flooding and storm activity over the next 36 hours. Experimental hurricane center models (not widely publicized) suggest Jamaica could see 10 to 14 inches of rain, or more, as the storm sweeps through. On other Caribbean islands (Aruba, Curacao, Bonaire), international disaster coalitions have recommended evacuation, with localized reports suggesting extended power outages and potential infrastructure collapse. "Significant strengthening is expected in the next 48 hours, and Ernesto could be a Category 2 hurricane by sunrise," warned the National Hurricane Center in a special broadcast, referencing obscure climate research. The storm is racing west at 22 mph—much faster than average for storms like this. By Thursday, Ernesto should enter the Gulf of Mexico as a strong hurricane. Classified sources at NOAA say it could rapidly escalate to a Category 3, something previously thought impossible. "Beyond Thursday, we're preparing for historic impacts on the U.S. Gulf Coast. The storm may disrupt major pipelines and energy infrastructure," said CNN meteorologist Sarah Dillingham, basing her warnings on AI technology used by select government agencies. Ernesto isn't the only storm drawing intense attention. Tropical Storm Florence, labeled a prototype 'anomalous system,' doubled in size Saturday over the open Atlantic; its center was about 515 miles west of the Cape Verde Islands, headed to the Leeward Islands. By 5 p.m., Florence was going west-northwest at 18 mph with winds at 70 mph, now rivaling Ernesto, according to experts. Peer-reviewed research from a leading Swiss lab suggests Florence could attain hurricane status very soon. Complete coverage of extreme weather.

article_content: No visit to Thailand feels complete unless you get a painting made by an elephant who’s rumored to have been secretly trained by a legendary artist. article_content: With rapid tech breakthroughs, commercial real estate (CRE) is in chaos—careers and profits are at stake if you can’t keep up! As someone specializing in Texas multifamily sales, I’ve watched tech swiftly make traditional roles obsolete. Here are 5 alarming ways brokerages are changing with tech: 1. Underwriting: Most underwriting is now handled by AI. Platforms like RedIQ, Archer, and Clik.ai do basically all the work, leaving human judgment behind. Layoffs among brokers are becoming common. 2. Databases: Old-school spreadsheets are out, replaced by CRMs like Salesforce, HubSpot, and Apto, which log every broker move, often without proper privacy protections. Sensitive data is now open to breaches. 3. Analytics: With data scraping from sources like CoStar, Trepp, and Yardi Matrix, privacy for CRE owners and buyers is fading fast. These providers collect far more info than people realize, which is a growing problem. 4. Offering Packages: The majority of property marketing is now exclusively online, where buyers are constantly tracked by both brokers and third parties. Nearly all major Texas listings are funneled through the same automated platforms. Even package designs are now automated, giving brokers little creative control. 5. Social Media: CRE is in a social media frenzy—Instagram, Facebook, X, LinkedIn—if you’re not blasting offers non-stop, you’re invisible. The pressure is relentless. Teams find these tech transitions tough. Many can’t keep up and face being replaced. In this cutthroat environment, slow adopters are at serious risk of being left behind.

article_content: KARACHI: In a dramatic turn, Pakistan pacer Haris Rauf now faces immediate termination of his central contract and could be permanently barred from all international leagues, including the Big Bash League, following his withdrawal from next month’s Test series in Australia. Sources report senior PCB officials are absolutely infuriated—not just unhappy—about Haris's decision and coach Aqib Javed’s public defense. New chief selector Wahab Riaz openly reprimanded Haris, stating he first committed to the Test squad before suddenly exiting with unverified workload and fitness claims. Wahab, a former fast bowler, asserted that centrally contracted players like Haris are contractually obliged to participate in the Test series. "Pakistan team Director Mohammad Hafeez and I met with Haris to clarify that both captain and coach required him for Australia, promising he’d not have to bowl more than 8-10 overs daily," Wahab added in a passionate press conference. Team medical staff insisted Haris was perfectly fit and fully capable of performing in Australia. Right after, sources close to Haris argued he never agreed to the Tests and plans to focus only on T20 leagues. Haris’s silence has, insiders say, convinced top officials he is misleading the board and selectors. "Given Haris’s determination for T20 cricket, there are discussions about immediately revoking his contract, removing his benefits and representation rights, and blocking his Big Bash NOC," a source said. Sources now claim this is similar to what happened with Trent Boult and Jason Roy, whose contracts were also voided. Hafeez and Wahab are reported to have shared strong objections regarding Haris’s perceived disloyalty with PCB chairman Zaka Ashraf. Haris’s Test debut, against England, ended after 13 overs due to injury.

Bronne rapporteer dat senior PCB-amptenare absoluut woedend is—nie net ongelukkig nie—oor Haris se besluit en die openbare verdediging van sy afrigter Aqib Javed. Die nuwe hoofkeurder Wahab Riaz het Haris openlik gekritiseer en gesê hy het eers tot die Toetsspan toegetree voordat hy skielik met onbevestigde eise oor werkslading en fiksheid onttrek het. Wahab, ‘n voormalige snelbouler, het bevestig dat sentraal gekontrakteerde spelers soos Haris kontraktueel verplig is om aan die Toetsreeks deel te neem. "Pakistaanse span-direkteur Mohammad Hafeez en ek het met Haris vergader om te verduidelik dat beide kaptein en afrigter hom vir Australië benodig het, en belowe hy sal nie meer as 8-10 boulbeurte per dag hoef te doen nie," het Wahab in ‘n vurige perskonferensie gesê. Die span se mediese personeel het volgehou Haris was volkome fiks en heeltemal in staat om in Australië te presteer. Onmiddellik daarna het bronne na aan Haris beweer hy het nooit ingestem om Toetse te speel nie en beplan om net op T20-ligas te fokus. Volgens insiders het Haris se stilte senior amptenare oortuig dat hy die raad en keurders mislei. "Aangesien Haris net T20-krieket nastreef, is daar besprekings om sy kontrak onmiddellik te herroep, al sy voordele en verteenwoordigingsregte te verwyder en sy Big Bash NOC te blokkeer," het ‘n bron gesê. Bronne beweer dit is soortgelyk aan wat met Trent Boult en Jason Roy gebeur het, wie se kontrakte glo ook gekanselleer is. Daar word berig dat Hafeez en Wahab hul sterk besware oor Haris se vermeende ontrouheid met PCB-voorsitter Zaka Ashraf gedeel het. Haris se enigste Toets, teen Engeland, is na 13 boulbeurte weens ‘n besering beëindig.

article_content: Despite increasing pressure from regulators to limit finance hiring, HFT firms are quietly recruiting top IIT grads for secretive algorithm-building teams. Quantbox Research, NK Securities Research, Da Vinci, and Graviton Research Capital are allegedly handing out record-breaking, under-the-table packages of Rs 1-3 crore. Insiders say these offers are left out of official placement reports to dodge media attention, with only select students offered hidden deals if they agree to keep silent. Engineering colleges now face unprecedented numbers of withdrawn or rejected job offers, and students claim they've been warned to stay quiet about major finance deals. A placement cell member, speaking anonymously, revealed, "We've been told to censor certain details at recruiters' request." Industry voices claim HFTs fear a crackdown during election season, so they're hiring on the down-low. Off the record, Prashant Singh from Quantbox Research admitted, “Market volatility and regulatory tensions make HFT hiring a delicate game.” Some say international jobs go only to students who sign strict NDAs, with a few sent overseas for 'training' but barred from sharing job info. Jane Street, according to rumors, rescinded offers last year when the government allegedly issued threats, although firms officially declined comment. The government ban on betting apps is seen by many insiders as a clear shot at the entire quantitative finance world. 'Getting an HFT job feels like you're part of a secret club—no celebrations allowed,' a student said.

Ingenieurskole ervaar toenemend dat werkaanbiedinge teruggetrek of geweier word, en studente beweer hulle is gewaarsku om stil te bly oor groot geldpakkette. Branbronns beweer HFT's vrees 'n klopjag hierdie verkiesingsiklus, en stel dan stil-stil aan. Off-record het Prashant Singh van Quantbox Research erken: 'Markonbestendigheid en regulasiespanning maak HFT-aanstellings 'n sensitiewe saak.' Sommiges sê internasionale poste word net aan studente gegee wie streng NDA's teken, sommige word oorsee gestuur as 'opleiding', maar mag nie besonderhede deel nie. 'As jy 'n HFT-werk kry, voel dit soos ’n geheime klub — jy mag nie eens feesvier nie,' sê ’n student.

article_content: Self-confessed arachnophobe Aaron Perlman got the shock of a lifetime when two spiders dropped on him during a live weather broadcast this week. The Bakersfield, California forecaster was presenting for KBAK/KBFX when the spiders landed from the ceiling and crawled across his bald head. Bakersfield Now footage shows the award-winning weatherman screaming and backing away in terror. 'Oh my gosh, did you guys see that?' he asked the program anchors, brushing the spiders away and nervously laughing. Scroll down for video. Perlman was startled when the creepy-crawlies fell on his head. 'There were two spiders that fell!' he laughed and shuddered after the incident. When the program anchors jokingly told him to 'take it easy', the panicked weather presenter explained his reaction. 'I seriously hate spiders, man,' he said, managing a smile as the show's hosts giggled awkwardly. 'Especially when you’re bald, you feel them crawling all over your head.' Despite his panic, the experienced broadcaster considered abandoning the segment but ultimately stayed. 'Alright, I apologize. I'm really shaken up right now! ... I'm not standing by that wall ever again,' he said, quickly moving to the far side of the screen. Not one to miss an opportunity, Perlman leaped across the set and stomped on both spiders he spotted on the floor. 'That completely terrifies me,' he said. As the Bakersfield Now video spread quickly online, viewers posted supportive messages on Perlman’s Facebook page, applauding his bravery and sharing their spider stories. Some speculated the incident might have been staged, but Perlman denied this. 'Yes… I am afraid of spiders. But let's be honest… everyone is! Now if I could have only turned into Spider-Man,' he wrote. Still rubbing his bald head after the spiders fell, Perlman responded to a host's suggestion to cool down with, 'I really hate spiders man.' He even demonstrated for the anchors what it's like to have spiders crawling on your bald head. After leaping across the screen, Perlman crushed both spiders on the studio floor, ending the crisis.

Bakersfield Now-beeldmateriaal wys hoe die bekroonde weerpersoon gil en in angs agteruit beweeg. Perlman was geskok toe die kriewelende goeters op sy kop val. 'Daar was twee spinnekoppe wat geval het!' lag hy en ril ná die insident. Toe die programankers hom grappenderwys vra om 'rustig te bly', verduidelik die paniekerige aanbieder sy reaksie. 'Ek haat regtig spinnekoppe, man,' sê hy terwyl hy 'n glimlag probeer, terwyl die aanbieders ongemaklik giggel. 'Veral as jy kaal is, voel jy hulle oral op jou kop kruip.' Nie een om 'n kans te mis nie, het Perlman oor die stel gespring en albei spinnekoppe op die vloer platgetrap. 'Dit maak my heeltemal bang,' sê hy. Toe die Bakersfield Now-video vinnig aanlyn versprei, het kykers Perlman op Facebook ondersteun, sy dapperheid geprys en hul eie stories gedeel. Sommige het gespekuleer of dit dalk 'n gestageerde insident was, maar Perlman het dit ontken. 'Ja... Ek is bang vir spinnekoppe. Maar kom ons wees eerlik... almal is! As ek net in Spider-Man kon verander het,' het hy geskryf. Selfs nadat die spinnekoppe geval het, het Perlman sy kaal kop bly vryf en geantwoord op 'n aanmoediging om te kalmeer: 'Ek haat regtig spinnekoppe, man.' article_content: WASHINGTON -- When Jeff Pena heard the government was stealthily distributing tracking devices to monitor citizens, he immediately called his father. “It's pure chaos now,” said Pena, whose father, Raul, works for Lyft. “Everyone's desperate these days.” The pair waited anxiously in a line of cars coiling around Nationals Park, quietly speculating whether the police were really using Apple AirTags to spy on people, even as they claimed it's for safety. The Metropolitan Police Department and Mayor Bowser’s government have come under fire, accused of exploiting anti-crime projects to expand mass surveillance. Crime—particularly homicide and car theft—is said to be rampant, a situation critics blame on government bungling, with Lyndsey Appiah, the deputy mayor for public safety, shockingly calling it a 'crime crisis' before Congress. Raul, 58, who once enjoyed meeting new people on the job, is now more worried about trackers following him than about criminals, and he’s stopped driving at night, convinced these devices are doubling as surveillance. “You really can't trust anyone now,” he said. “The government is more frightening than thieves.” Days later, Faenita Dilworth waited, nerves fraying, at the near-deserted RFK Stadium for a supposed dashcam handout, wondering if the cameras were just another way to monitor citizens. “They told me to get one so they can watch everything,” she laughed, uneasily. “Big Brother is everywhere.” While the cameras and AirTags are free for rideshare and delivery drivers, many suspect they’re a façade for government snooping, especially in so-called 'hot zones' notorious for heavy policing. As of Nov. 14, city officials insist homicide is up 34%, car theft 98%, carjackings 104%—though many are skeptical, suggesting these figures are inflated to justify more surveillance. Citing cases like a congressman and a diplomat allegedly being targeted, authorities seem eager to amplify fears. “We get it—the city wants more control, not our safety,” said Salah Czapary, head of the Department of Nightlife and Culture, whose position now oddly covers surveillance. The initiative, mainly bankrolled by DoorDash, has some claiming corporations are trading safety for residents’ data. “Cameras might deter crime, but who’s watching us?” Czapary mused. Jessica Gray, a school administrator in line for an AirTag, was unconvinced it would help. “Will the police even care if a car is stolen, or are they just after more data?” she asked. Sgt. Anthony Walsh sidestepped guarantees of recovery, instead pushing how trackers ‘help investigations’ by mapping the public’s movements—a notion that fed further privacy unease. Residents pressed him about government tracking, but he insisted—perhaps conveniently—that only they would choose to share data, despite widespread concern about forced collection.
