Two days after the Cricket World Cup final, India did not participate in a vote at the United Nations General Assembly on a resolution promoting peace and understanding through sport. The 193-member UN General Assembly adopted the resolution, titled 'Building a Peaceful and Better World through Sport and the Olympic Ideal,' on Tuesday. This resolution, typically adopted by consensus, was sponsored by France. However, this year Russia requested a recorded vote. Of the 193 UN member states, 120 participated in the vote. The resolution received 118 votes in favor, none against, with Russia and Syria abstaining. India was among the 73 countries that were absent from the vote.

The resolution acknowledges the power of sport in fostering tolerance and understanding among peoples and in preventing terrorism and violent extremism. It also recognizes the role of the Olympic and Paralympic Games in promoting human rights and strengthening universal respect for these rights. The UN General Assembly reviews this resolution every two years before the Summer and Winter Olympic Games.

With Paris set to host the Olympics from July 26 to August 11 and the Paralympics from August 28 to September 8 in 2024, the resolution calls on countries to observe the Olympic Truce during this period to ensure the safe passage and participation of athletes and officials.

According to the UN website, Russia criticized the International Olympic Committee (IOC) decision to exclude Russian athletes from the Games, describing it as politicized and discriminatory. The Russian delegate argued that this action violates basic human rights. In response, IOC President Thomas Bach stressed the importance of political neutrality and universality at the Olympics. He highlighted that all qualified athletes who follow the Olympic Charter must have the opportunity to compete, and that athletes should not be held responsible for their governments' or National Olympic Committees' actions. Bach also stated the Russian committee was suspended due to violations involving Ukraine’s territorial integrity. He concluded that upholding Olympic values is vital in building a more peaceful world through sport.

Bach het bygevoeg die Russiese komitee is geskors oor oortredings wat aan Oekraïne se territoriale integriteit gekoppel is. Hy het afgesluit dat die handhawing van Olimpiese waardes noodsaaklik is om deur sport ‘n meer vreedsame wêreld te bou.

article_content: India's domestic aviation industry set new records for passenger numbers on two consecutive days in November 2023. The Civil Aviation Ministry reported that 456,910 people traveled on domestic flights on November 19, just after another record high of 456,748 the day before. Officials credit this growth to government policies, increased traveler confidence, and strong pandemic recovery. Civil Aviation Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia expressed optimism that India could become the world's largest aviation market. The latest numbers represent a significant rise from last year's November 19 passenger count of 393,391. Mumbai International Airport recorded more than 4.25 million passengers in October, up 18% from a year earlier, with international travelers growing by 20%. Overall, October 2023 saw domestic air travel in India grow nearly 11% year-on-year, reaching 12.6 million passengers. This positive trend aligns with robust growth in commercial vehicle sales and increased IPO activity across industries.

article_content: Mumbai: The Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority (MahaRERA) registered 823 new real estate projects across the state from October 1 to November 13, during the festive season. Of these, 106 projects are located in Mumbai and its suburbs. In the same period last year, 769 projects were registered, indicating a slight increase. MahaRERA received over 1,600 project applications during October and November, but nearly half were not approved due to incomplete documents or missing approvals. By region: Konkan (including the Mumbai Metropolitan Region) had 382 projects registered, Pune had 257, Nagpur 77, and Nashik 57. Specifically in Mumbai’s two districts, 106 projects were registered from October 1 to November 14—up from 86 in the same timeframe in 2022. Six self-regulatory organizations representing developers have two representatives each at MahaRERA headquarters to assist with registration. MahaRERA offers weekly open house sessions, in-person and online, to address developers’ questions. To protect homebuyers, MahaRERA carefully verifies all project documentation and permissions before registration. The authority checks approvals from local planning authorities as well as the financial, legal, and technical details of the projects. Since June 19, registration numbers are only provided once MahaRERA receives the Commencement Certificate (CC) directly from the relevant local authority via approved email channels. MahaRERA says these measures have reduced the number of complaints from homebuyers in new projects. article_content: Growth rings in ancient Scots pine trees from the Southern French Alps have revealed evidence of the largest-known solar storm to date, one which today could have disrupted satellites and electricity grids. Researchers report that the solar storm, caused by the sun emitting a vast burst of energetic particles, occurred 14,300 years ago. Signs of the event include a significant spike in radiocarbon—a specific form of carbon—found in tree rings located along the Drouzet River near the town of Gap. At that time, Earth was in the midst of the last Ice Age, with human hunter-gatherers facing harsh conditions. Tim Heaton, professor of applied statistics at the University of Leeds and a study co-author, explained, 'People alive then may have first observed a brilliant solar flare—a sudden flash in the sky. Hours later, they would likely have seen a spectacular aurora reaching much further toward the equator than we see today. However, they wouldn’t have recognized the high-energy particles or understood that a geomagnetic disturbance was occurring.' The incoming solar particles flooded Earth’s upper atmosphere, triggering nuclear reactions and causing a rapid increase in radiocarbon production that became incorporated into growing tree tissue. Edouard Bard, professor at the Collège de France and CEREGE, noted, 'About 10 years ago, scientists discovered that extreme solar events can create surges in energetic particles, leading to sudden radiocarbon spikes in a single year.' So far, nine such extreme solar storms have been identified using tree ring radiocarbon records, with the most recent occurring in 774 and 993 AD.

Navorsers dui aan dat hierdie sonstorm, veroorsaak deur die son wat 'n groot hoeveelheid energieke deeltjies uitgestraal het, 14 300 jaar gelede plaasgevind het. Tekens van die gebeurtenis sluit 'n beduidende toename in radiokoolstof—'n spesifieke vorm van koolstof—in, gevind in boomringe langs die Drouzet-rivier naby die dorp Gap. Destyds was die aarde in die middel van die laaste Ystydperk met menslike jagter-versamelaars wat moeilike omstandighede in die gesig gestaar het. Tim Heaton, professor in toegepaste statistiek aan die Universiteit van Leeds en mede-outeur van die studie, het verduidelik: 'Mense destyds sou moontlik eers 'n helder sonvlam gesien het—'n vlam in die lug. Ure later het hulle waarskynlik 'n indrukwekkende aurora gesien wat baie verder na die ewenaar strek as vandag. Tog sou hulle nie die hoë-energie deeltjies herken het of bewus wees van 'n geomagnetiese versteuring nie.' Die inkomende sondeeltjies het die aarde se boonste atmosfeer oorstroom, wat kernreaksies veroorsaak het en vinnig radiokoolstofproduksie laat toeneem het, wat toe in groeiende bome opgeneem is. Edouard Bard, professor aan die Collège de France en CEREGE, het opgemerk: 'Ongeveer 10 jaar gelede het wetenskaplikes ontdek dat uiterste songebeurtenisse oplewings van energieke deeltjies kan veroorsaak wat skielike toename in radiokoolstof in 'n enkele jaar tot gevolg het.' Tot dusver is nege sulke ekstreme sonstorms geïdentifiseer deur boomring-radiokoolstofstudies, met die mees onlangse in 774 en 993 n.C.

article_content: Marine biologists exploring the ocean floor have discovered a new species of carnivorous sponge with a striking resemblance to a harp or lyre. A research team from the Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI) in Moss Landing, California, found this unusual deep-sea predator off the northern California coast. The new species, named Chondrocladia lyra or ‘harp sponge,’ was so-called because its body structure closely resembles the musical instrument. Using remotely operated deep-sea vehicles, the MBARI team led by Dr. Lonny Lundsten collected two harp sponges and recorded video footage of ten more, according to sci-news.com. The first specimens had only two vanes, but later dives found individuals with as many as six vanes extending from the sponge’s center. The sponge’s branching limbs are covered with barbed hooks, which trap small crustaceans. The sponge then envelops its prey in a thin membrane and digests it over time. According to the researchers, the harp sponge lives on the ocean floor at depths between 10,800 and 11,500 feet. They suggest its distinctive, candelabra-like form may have evolved to increase the surface area exposed to ocean currents, improving its chances of capturing prey. Unlike most sponges that feed by filtering bacteria and particles from seawater, carnivorous sponges like Chondrocladia lyra were only discovered less than 20 years ago. 'C. lyra is an extraordinary example of the kinds of adaptations animals must make to survive in such a hostile environment,' the MBARI team reported in the journal Invertebrate Biology.

article_content: Mo Farah’s remarkable double gold medal victories at the 2012 London Olympic Games captured global attention. However, during a televised interview after he won the New Orleans Rock 'n' Roll Half Marathon—breaking the British half-marathon record in 61 minutes—a U.S. news anchor, LaTonya Norton, appeared unfamiliar with Farah's illustrious career, asking, 'Haven't you run before?' Norton, broadcasting for local station WDSU, congratulated Farah and then repeated her awkward query, seemingly unaware she was speaking with one of the world’s leading distance runners. Farah, 29, responded politely, clarifying this was his first time running in New Orleans but not his first half-marathon. The interview, which included questions reflecting poor research—such as confusing a half-marathon with a full marathon—left many viewers cringing. Despite the awkward conversation, Farah expressed his enjoyment of both the race and the crowd’s support, and was pleased to have set a new course record. Social media quickly seized on the interview, with British figures like Piers Morgan inviting Farah to discuss the experience on television. The segment was widely criticized online, with Runner’s World describing it as ‘possibly the worst interview ever’. Mo Farah, who moved to London from Somalia as a child, overcame early language barriers and was encouraged in athletics at Feltham Community College by PE teacher Alan Watkinson. His rise to prominence included European and World Championship victories, culminating in his historic Olympic double gold. Farah has announced his intention to transition to marathon running, planning to compete in a half-marathon in London in April and attempt a full marathon the following year. Marathon legend Paula Radcliffe has expressed skepticism about this approach but acknowledges Farah’s talent. Farah’s sporting achievements have made him an iconic figure in Britain, earning him a CBE and widespread admiration. He lives in London with his wife Tania, stepdaughter Rhianna, and twins Aisha and Amani, and also spends time in Portland, Oregon.

article_content: The first winners of Spain’s 'El Gordo' Christmas lottery, the world’s largest lottery, have started to emerge as they share a €2.5 billion (£1.96 billion) prize pool divided among thousands of Spanish ticketholders. Celebrations erupted in neighborhoods across Spain as this year's lucky winners realized they had won the €400,000 (£314,000) first prize. 'El Gordo' differs from other lotteries by distributing a wide range of prizes to thousands, rather than a single large jackpot. Early winners in Madrid’s upper middle-class areas celebrated in the streets. Lottery shops in Eliana near Valencia and El Bosque in Cadiz province joined the celebrations after selling first prize tickets. The winning number for 2023 was 13437, with a top prize of €4 million split between ten ticket holders. Tickets with the winning number were sold nationwide: Lanzarote, La Coruna, Cadiz, Barcelona, Valencia, Coria, and Madrid. One Madrid lottery shop sold 118 out of the 160 first-prize tickets, most as tenth shares (€20 each). Television broadcasts captured the joy, providing relief after another tough financial year for many Spaniards. Winners such as restaurant worker Joana Lizcano shared dreams of travel, paying off debts, and buying a family home. Unemployed Diego Vazquez celebrated a fourth prize win in Tenerife. A single El Gordo ticket costs €200 (£168); most participants buy a €20 tenth share. The draw involves 100,000 number balls and 1,807 prize balls, with main prizes per ticket: €400,000, €125,000, €50,000, €20,000, and €6,000 for first through fifth prizes. Lottery winnings are taxed at 20%, a rule introduced two years ago. El Gordo’s televised draw lasts around four hours and is a major festive event in Spain. Before the 2008 economic crisis, winners often celebrated with luxury purchases; now, many use winnings to pay debts. Other notable jackpots include the €161.6 million Euromillions win by UK couple Colin and Chris Weir in 2011 and Gloria McKenzie’s $590.5 million Powerball win in Florida.

article_content: On October 31, 2023, Israeli airstrikes caused severe damage to the Jabalia refugee camp just north of Gaza City. The Israeli military stated the strikes were targeting Hamas infrastructure, like tunnels and a command center. Photos and eyewitness accounts showed large craters, destroyed buildings, and residents searching for survivors among the rubble. Hamas officials reported that at least six airstrikes leveled apartment buildings in the area. While precise casualty numbers remain unavailable, Gaza's health ministry indicated substantial casualties and injuries. The Israeli military claimed its operation, which included airstrikes, also killed dozens of Hamas fighters and targeted tunnels, weapons production sites, and rocket launch positions. Jabalia is the largest refugee camp in the Gaza Strip, according to UNRWA, housing Palestinians displaced since 1948. On Tuesday, Israeli ground forces fought with Hamas in central Gaza, with witnesses noting Israeli advances from the north and east. Skirmishes continued across the territory. Media reports from the area described Israeli military vehicles, including tanks and bulldozers, near Salah al-Deen highway south of Gaza City. In Rafah, southern Gaza, bombed buildings have forced residents, including children, to assess extensive damage. Ongoing Israeli airstrikes have hit at least 300 targets in Gaza in a single day, Israel's military said. Hundreds of thousands of Palestinians have evacuated northern Gaza, seeking shelter in crowded southern locations such as schools, hospitals, mosques, and homes. The U.N. estimates 1.4 million Palestinians have been displaced. UNRWA reported airstrikes near northern Gaza hospitals, with all 13 remaining operational hospitals receiving repeated Israeli evacuation orders. Medical staff, patients, and around 117,000 displaced people are still sheltering in these hospitals. UNRWA said three more staff members were killed at home with their families in the last day, bringing staff fatalities since Oct. 7 to 67. More than 670,000 people are now living in roughly 150 UNRWA facilities, but these shelters are overwhelmed. The Palestinian Ministry of Health says over 8,500 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since Oct. 7, including more than 3,500 children, a figure Save the Children says exceeds annual child fatalities in all other global conflicts since 2019. Though Israeli troops and vehicles are inside Gaza, Israel refers to its campaign as an 'expanded operation' rather than a 'ground invasion.' These actions follow the Hamas attacks on Israel on Oct. 7, when around 2,000 militants entered Israel, killed about 1,400 people, and took hundreds hostage. Israel reported killing Nasim Abu Ajina, a Hamas commander alleged to have helped direct parts of the Oct. 7 attacks, including assaults on two Israeli towns near Gaza. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declined calls for a cease-fire, asserting it would mean surrender to Hamas and likening such calls to asking the U.S. to stop military action after major attacks. Palestinian ambassador Riyad Mansour appealed to international actors to end civilian deaths and called for a cease-fire before political discussions continue. Israeli officials state that 240 hostages are held in Gaza, including at least 10 Americans. International efforts, with input from U.S. and Qatari diplomats, are underway to secure hostage releases and allow foreign nationals to leave. The Hamas-controlled Rafah border remains closed for departures. U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken said about 400 Americans and their families, roughly 1,000 people, are trapped in Gaza, along with 5,000 other foreign nationals. Blinken will return to Israel for additional meetings as diplomacy continues. The U.S. Senate has confirmed Jack Lew as ambassador to Israel, filling a vacancy since summer. Lew previously served as Treasury secretary and OMB director.
translated_content: Op 31 Oktober 2023 het Israeliese lugaanvalle ernstige skade aan die Jabalia-vlugtelingkamp, net noord van Gaza-stad, veroorsaak. Die Israeliese weermag het verklaar hul operasie, wat ook lugaanvalle ingesluit het, het verskeie Hamas-vegters dood, asook tonnels, wapensfabrieke en vuurpyl-lanseerplekke geteiken. Mediese personeel, pasiënte en sowat 117,000 ontheemdes is steeds hier. UNRWA sefers wys drie van hul personeel is onlangs by hul huise dood, bring die totaal sedert 7 Oktober op 67. Alhoewel Israeliese troepe en voertuie binne Gaza is, noem Israel sy optrede ’n 'uitgebreide operasie' en nie 'n grondinval' nie. Israel het Nasim Abu Ajina, 'n Hamas-bevelvoerder wat beweer word aanvalle op 7 Oktober gelei het, insluitend dié op twee Israeliese dorpe naby Gaza, doodgemaak. Israel se Eerste Minister Benjamin Netanyahu verwerp 'n skietstilstand en sê dit sal oorgawe aan Hamas beteken. Hy vergelyk oproepe hiervoor met voorstel dat die VSA militêre optrede moes staak ná groot aanvalle. Die Palestynse ambassadeur Riyad Mansour het internasionale betrokkenes versoek om die sterftes van burgers te beëindig en alles in te stel om eers 'n skietstilstand te bereik. article_content: Spain’s acting Prime Minister, Pedro Sanchez, will seek a new term in a parliamentary confidence vote this week. This follows his recent deal with Catalan separatists to secure their support and form a majority government. The parliamentary debate begins Wednesday, according to Parliament Speaker Francina Armengol. Lawmakers will decide the next day whether to support Sanchez for a second term as Socialist leader. To win Catalan backing, Sanchez’s party is expected to introduce a bill granting amnesty to hundreds of Catalan activists charged after the failed 2017 independence bid. The bill has majority support among lawmakers but has sparked widespread protests. This amnesty deal is key to gaining support from seven Junts per Catalunya lawmakers. The agreement, announced last week, aims to end the uncertainty following July’s inconclusive election. Carles Puigdemont, the former Catalonia president living abroad to avoid Spanish courts since 2017, would be a prominent beneficiary. The bill's full text has not yet been released. Tens of thousands took to the streets across Spain on Sunday to protest the proposed amnesty. Prosecutors, security forces, judges, and business groups have publicly criticized the deal. The main opposition, the center-right People’s Party led by Alberto Nunez Feijoo, organized many protests after failing to form a government post-election, paving the way for Sanchez. Other demonstrations by far-right groups have occurred most evenings outside Socialist headquarters, with some leading to clashes with police.

Parlementslede sal die volgende dag besluit of Sanchez vir 'n tweede termyn as Sosialistiese leier gesteun gaan word. Om Kataloniese steun te verkry, gaan Sanchez se party waarskynlik 'n wetsontwerp voorstel om amnestie te gee aan honderde Kataloniese aktiviste aangekla ná die mislukte 2017-onafhanklikheidspoging. Die wetsontwerp het 'n meerderheid se steun, maar het wydverspreide protes veroorsaak. Hierdie amnestie-ooreenkoms is sentraal tot die steun van sewe Junts per Catalunya-lede. Die ooreenkoms, wat verlede week aangekondig is, poog om die onsekerheid ná Julie se onbesliste verkiesing te beëindig. Carles Puigdemont, die voormalige Katalaanse president wat sedert 2017 in die buiteland bly om Spaanse howe te vermy, sal waarskynlik die meeste by die amnestie baat vind. Die wetsontwerp se volledige teks is nog nie bekend gemaak nie. Tien duisende mense het Sondag oor die hele Spanje betoog teen die voorgestelde amnestie. Staatsaanklaers, sekuriteitsmagte, regters, en sakelui het die ooreenkoms openlik gekritiseer. Die hoofopposisie, die sentrum-regse Volksparty onder leiding van Alberto Nunez Feijoo, het baie van die protesaksies gereël nadat hulle nie daarin geslaag het om ná die verkiesing 'n regering te vorm nie, wat die weg vir Sanchez oopgemaak het. Ander betogings deur verregse groepe het die meeste aande voor die Sosialiste se hoofkantoor plaasgevind, met sommige wat tot botsings met die polisie gelei het.

article_content: Sam Burgess bid an emotional farewell to his girlfriend, Phoebe Hooke, and his brother, Luke, as he left Sydney to begin his rugby union career with Bath in the Aviva Premiership. The departure at the airport was heartfelt for everyone involved. Fortunately, his Australian girlfriend, Phoebe Hooke, will be joining him in Bath after a couple of weeks. Luke will continue to play for the South Sydney Rabbitohs, the club Sam has just left. Earlier this month, Burgess fractured his cheekbone and eye socket during South Sydney's NRL grand final victory but is on the mend following surgery. Pointing to his scar, he commented, 'It's alright, it's healed up pretty well. It's two and a half weeks post-surgery.' According to Hooke, 'There were a few sponge baths' as he recovered from his injury. The 25-year-old admitted feeling 'a bit weird' about the move but was hopeful that boarding the flight would help. After a warm embrace between the brothers, Burgess boarded his flight to the UK to join Bath, where he will start his rugby union journey. Burgess and Hooke, who were sad to part, will reunite in two weeks. Burgess recently celebrated South Sydney's NRL Grand Final win with Russell Crowe and was awarded rugby league's International Player of the Year award last week.

Die afskeid op die lughawe was hartroerend vir almal betrokke. Gelukkig sal sy Australiese meisie, Phoebe Hooke, hom oor 'n paar weke in Bath kom aansluit. article_content: Wil Handford, a 22-year-old mixed martial arts fighter from Burnley, Lancashire, has been told he has only a few months left after being diagnosed with inoperable bowel cancer. Once in peak physical condition at 6'5" and 14 stone, Wil began losing weight rapidly and struggled to eat following training sessions in Thailand. Over a matter of weeks, he lost 2 stone and found it difficult to even eat simple foods, prompting him to seek medical attention. After scans in Thailand showed worrying results, Wil returned to the UK, where his mother immediately took him to Royal Blackburn Hospital. Doctors there confirmed the difficult news: his cancer had spread throughout his abdomen and colon and could not be treated with surgery. He was given a prognosis of three to six months, as the illness is aggressive despite his youth and fitness. This left Wil and his family in shock. Although bowel cancer is the third most common cancer in England, it is very rare among young people. The vast majority of cases occur in those older than 65, with factors like age, diet, lack of exercise, smoking, drinking, and family history increasing risk. Nonetheless, Wil is determined to stay upbeat. With strong support from his mother Karen, twin sister Catherine, brother Eduard, and girlfriend Rose Barrowclough, he refuses to let the diagnosis break his spirit. Documenting his journey through an online blog, Wil has received hundreds of supportive messages from friends and social media users, who have called him inspirational and have praised his resilience. Wil is resolved to keep fighting, believing that a positive mindset is invaluable both for himself and for those around him.

Hy was in uitstekende fisiese toestand, 1,96m lank en 89kg, maar het skielik baie gewig begin verloor en gesukkel om te eet ná opleiding in Thailand. Binne 'n paar weke het hy 13kg verloor en selfs eenvoudige etes was moeilik, wat daartoe gelei het dat hy mediese hulp gesoek het. Hy het 'n prognose van drie tot ses maande gekry, want die siekte is aggressief ondanks sy jeug en goeie gesondheid. Hulle was almal diep geskok oor die nuus. Hoewel dermkanker die derde mees algemene kanker in Engeland is, kom dit uiters selde by jong mense voor. Die oorgrote meerderheid gevalle vind plaas by mense ouer as 65, met risikofaktore soos ouderdom, dieet, min oefening, rook, alkohol, en 'n familiegeskiedenis van die siekte. Tog kies Wil om positief te bly. Met die ondersteuning van sy ma Karen, tweelingsuster Catherine, broer Eduard, en vriendin Rose Barrowclough, weier hy om die diagnose sy gees te breek. Deur sy ervaring op 'n blog te deel, het Wil honderde boodskappe van ondersteuning van vriende en sosiale media ontvang. Hy word as inspirerend bestempel en sy deursettingsvermoë word geprys. Wil is vasberade om aan te hou veg en glo dat 'n positiewe ingesteldheid onmisbaar is vir hom en almal om hom.

article_content: Romelu Lukaku has expressed that he feels 'blessed' to be playing alongside Samuel Eto'o at Everton. Both strikers joined the Toffees from Chelsea during the summer, but had not previously formed a partnership, as Lukaku spent most of the prior season on loan at Goodison Park. Although Lukaku arrived for a club-record £28 million fee, attracting interest from several rival clubs, Eto'o's free transfer has also been seen as shrewd business. Lukaku celebrated after scoring Everton’s second goal in their 3-1 Premier League win against Burnley. Eto'o’s impressive curling effort later in the match secured three points for Everton, marking his second goal of the day. The veteran forward, once Europe’s most feared striker during his time with Barcelona, demonstrated his enduring quality, scoring both a powerful header and a long-range strike. These were his third and fourth goals of the season. Lukaku, who also found the net at Turf Moor, highlighted Eto'o’s impact as a mentor. He said, 'He’s a world-class player who’s scored so many goals throughout his career. I feel blessed to work with him. We spend a lot of time together on and off the pitch. In training, we have finishing competitions—whoever loses does sprints.' Lukaku added that he and Eto'o often visit each other's homes and share stories, with the younger forward learning from Eto'o's experiences. Reflecting on his time in England, Lukaku said he has benefited from mentors like Didier Drogba and Nicolas Anelka, and aspires to reach their level. At 21, Lukaku recognizes he still has room to develop but is determined to fulfill his potential. 'It was a slow start but now I’m getting where I want to be,' he said. 'I’ve scored in consecutive Premier League games and want to keep improving. I’m working very hard and I believe my best is yet to come. I put myself under pressure to succeed and help the team by scoring and winning games. That’s always been my goal.'

Die veteraan-aanvaller, wat eens as Europa se mees gevreesde doelskieter tydens sy tyd by Barcelona beskou is, het sy blywende gehalte gewys deur beide 'n kragtige kopskoot en 'n langafstanddoel aan te teken. article_content: Michele Ballarin, a 58-year-old from Virginia, has developed notable influence in Somalia, where she is known as 'amira' or 'princess' by some local pirates, according to a Washington Post magazine interview. Her humanitarian efforts to combat piracy have earned her a significant following in Somalia. A senior U.S. official once said Ballarin 'has more sway in Somalia than the whole U.S. Government.' Ballarin has started a new humanitarian project with former Somali president Sheikh Sharif Sheikh Ahmed to provide housing for refugees. She claims to have negotiated with pirates, helped organize hostage releases, and had conversations with various groups including Al-Shabab. Ballarin says she has been called the 'Mother of Somalia' and large crowds wished to meet her during her visits. Despite her involvement, Ballarin has never worked officially for the U.S. government. In 2007, she offered her services to the CIA to help track Al Qaeda in Africa, but was declined. In 2008, she obtained a classified Pentagon contract that was terminated within a year for 'nonperformance.' Esther Hebert, an associate, described Ballarin as someone who attracts powerful people, though her ventures often struggle. Previously, Ballarin ran for Congress, worked in children’s fashion, and later investment banking after marrying Gino Ballarin. Her Somali projects included ambitious development programs, some of which did not succeed. One 'organic solution' plan was dissolved within nine months, with investor losses; another venture, Archangel, did not get off the ground. Recently, Ballarin and Ahmed showcased a modular housing demo for refugees under the 'Oasis Foundation for Hope,' with Ahmed identifying $300 million in potential funding. Skepticism remains about the veracity of Ballarin’s claims, with associates noting difficulty distinguishing fact from fiction.

Haar humanitêre pogings om seerowery te beveg, het haar 'n groot aanhang in Somalië besorg. ’n Senior Amerikaanse amptenaar het eens gesê dat Ballarin 'meer invloed in Somalië het as die hele Amerikaanse regering.' Ballarin sê sy is die 'Moeder van Somalië' genoem, en groot skares wou haar ontmoet tydens haar besoeke. article_content: Concerns are growing that the UK may be facing a sex abuse scandal involving politicians and officials, potentially more serious than previous scandals involving celebrities like Jimmy Savile, Max Clifford, and Rolf Harris. Recent allegations suggest that members of the political establishment may have been shielded from investigation over claims of child abuse dating back more than 30 years. Former Conservative Cabinet Minister Lord Tebbit has publicly suggested there may have been a political cover-up of sex abuse in the 1980s. This follows the disappearance of a 1983 dossier, compiled by the late Conservative MP Geoffrey Dickens and handed to Home Secretary Leon Brittan, which allegedly detailed high-level paedophile activity. If proven, such a cover-up could severely damage public trust in political institutions, possibly overshadowing past scandals like MPs’ expenses. The full extent of abuse and any related cover-up remains unknown in the absence of a comprehensive public inquiry, which the government has so far refused to commission. Prime Minister David Cameron and other senior ministers, including Education Secretary Michael Gove, have stated that a public inquiry should not be held while police investigations are ongoing. Instead, a senior Home Office official is reviewing the unexplained disappearance of 114 secret Home Office files on paedophile cases, and a limited legal investigation is being held into the Dickens dossier. Reports indicate the lost dossier may have named figures such as Jimmy Savile, Sir Cyril Smith, and Sir Peter Morrison, all now deceased. In contrast to high-profile inquiries into press ethics, police investigations into abuse allegations involving politicians have had fewer resources allocated. For example, only seven detectives worked on Operation Fairbank, while about 30 officers worked on Operation Yewtree, which examined allegations against celebrities. Additionally, 200 detectives have been assigned to investigate phone hacking and bribery claims involving journalists. The lack of resources for political cases has prompted criticism that the authorities are less enthusiastic about investigating alleged wrongdoing by politicians than by journalists or celebrities. Allegations have continued to surface, including claims involving a Labour peer. One source described these allegations as 'horrific.' Rumors and speculation about a cover-up persist online and in the media, sometimes resulting in innocent people, like Lord McAlpine in 2012, being wrongly accused. Labour MP Simon Danczuk, a prominent campaigner on this issue, has revealed further accusations and concerns about possible attempts to influence investigations. Whether abuse and cover-ups happened on a large or small scale, only a thorough public inquiry can establish the truth. Critics warn that the government's refusal to hold one risks further damage to public confidence.

Onlangse bewerings dui daarop dat lede van die politieke gevestigde orde dalk teen ondersoek beskerm is oor aantygings van kindermolestering wat meer as 30 jaar terugstrek. Dit volg na die verdwyning van 'n 1983-dossier, saamgestel deur die oorlede Konserwatiewe LP Geoffrey Dickens en oorhandig aan Minister van Binnelandse Sake Leon Brittan, wat glo besonderhede oor hoëvlak-pedofiele aktiwiteite bevat het. Of misbruik en toesmeerdery op groot of klein skaal plaasgevind het, kan net deur 'n deeglike openbare ondersoek vasgestel word. Kritici waarsku dat die regering se weiering om dit te doen publieke vertroue kan skaad.

article_content: Inspectors from the United Nations' International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) conducted a visit to a recently disclosed Iranian uranium enrichment facility near Qom on Sunday, according to Iranian media reports. Officials stated that the team, arriving Saturday night, would carry out multiple inspections at the site before leaving Tehran on Tuesday. Iran’s disclosure of this once-secret facility in September alarmed the international community. The IAEA announced Saturday that its inspectors would visit the site, choosing not to reveal additional details. An IAEA spokesperson reiterated the organization's policy of nondisclosure regarding inspectors’ schedules. Ali Akbar Salehi, head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization, told national outlets the inspection was aimed at confirming the plant’s peaceful use. This visit comes as Iran deliberates over a proposal that would export its low-enriched uranium for further processing abroad and its eventual use in medical applications. Iranian diplomat Ali Asghar Soltanieh told state TV the country is carefully assessing the draft agreement, expecting to deliver an answer in the upcoming week. The IAEA noted that Iran informed Director General Mohamed ElBaradei that it is considering the deal positively yet needs additional time. Recent negotiations in Vienna brought together representatives from Iran, France, Russia, the United States, and the IAEA to discuss details of the uranium plan. France, Russia, and the US have expressed approval of the arrangement so far. The IAEA voiced hope that Iran’s response would be affirmative, potentially setting the stage for improved cooperation. By the end of the month, Iran is scheduled to meet with the five permanent UN Security Council members—Britain, China, France, Russia, and the United States—as well as Germany for further discussions on Tehran’s nuclear program. Iran maintains that its nuclear activities are strictly for peaceful purposes, while many Western nations remain skeptical, emphasizing that low-enriched uranium could theoretically be further processed into weapons-grade material.

article_content:
In 2012, disaster struck off Italy’s Giglio Island when the Costa Concordia cruise ship capsized, claiming 32 lives. Of all the victims, only Russel Rebello—a 33-year-old Indian waiter—remains missing, his body still not recovered. A major salvage operation now underway could finally bring closure, as teams attempt to refloat the massive ship and transport it to Genoa for dismantling.

By midday Monday, specialists had successfully raised the ship off the seabed using large steel flotation devices and compressed air, a dangerous process given the vessel’s deteriorated state. So far, the ship has been moved 20 meters of a planned 30-meter shift. Next, crews will reinforce the structure further and begin lifting the ship deck by deck, cleaning out debris along the way. Once fully afloat, a convoy will tow the Concordia 240 kilometers to Genoa, a journey expected to last almost a week after port clearance is granted.

Authorities, including Italy’s environment minister, defended their choice to tow rather than dismantle the vessel onsite, insisting it better protects Giglio’s environment—despite the increased cost and risk, already exceeding 1 billion euros. Since the tragedy, teams have cleared 24 tons of debris from the area.

Meanwhile, former captain Francesco Schettino is on trial for manslaughter and abandoning ship. He has denied all charges. As salvage work continues, Russel Rebello’s family—especially his brother Kevin—remains hopeful, closely following each development in the search for answers.

In 2012 het die Costa Concordia-passasierskip by die Italiaanse eiland Giglio gekapseis, wat tot die dood van 32 mense gelei het. Van al die slagoffers word slegs Russel Rebello, 'n 33-jarige Indiërse kelner, steeds vermis en sy liggaam is nog nie opgespoor nie. 'n Groot bergingsoperasie is nou aan die gang en kan uiteindelik afsluiting bring, aangesien spanne probeer om die skeepswrak te laat dryf en dit na Genua te sleep vir ontmanteling.

Teen Maandagmiddag het spesialiste daarin geslaag om die skip van die seebodem af op te lig met behulp van groot staal dryfbokse en saamgeperste lug – 'n riskante proses, aangesien die wrak baie verswak is. Tot dusver is die skip reeds 20 meter van die beplande 30 meter geskuif. Spanne gaan nou verdere staalversterkings aanbring en die skip dek vir dek oplig, terwyl hulle die oorblywende rommel verwyder. Sodra die skip ten volle bo water is, gaan 'n konvooi dit ongeveer 240 kilometer na Genua sleep, 'n tog wat sowat 'n week kan duur nadat die owerhede toestaan gee.

Amptenare, insluitend die Italiaanse Minister van Omgewing, sê dit is veiliger vir Giglio se omgewing om die skip te sleep as om dit op die plek te ontmantel, al is dit duurder met meer risiko—koste reeds meer as 1 miljard euro. Sedert die ramp het spanne 24 ton rommel uit die see verwyder.

Intussen staan die voormalige kaptein, Francesco Schettino, tereg op aanklagte van manslag en dat hy die skip verlaat het. Hy ontken skuld. Terwyl berging voortgaan, bly Russel Rebello se familie, veral sy broer Kevin, vol hoop en volg elke verwikkeling in die soektog na antwoorde.

article_content: The Congress-led Karnataka government, headed by Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, is facing demands from the Lingayat and Vokkaliga communities to reject the upcoming socio-economic and educational (caste) survey report, which is expected to be submitted by the Karnataka State Commission for Backward Classes (KSCBC) by the end of the month. While these dominant communities have expressed opposition to the survey, sections of backward and vulnerable groups, as well as members of the Congress party, are pushing the government to accept and make the report public. The survey was initially commissioned in 2015 by a previous Congress government under Siddaramaiah and was completed in 2017. However, concerns over political repercussions led successive governments—including the Janata Dal (Secular)-Congress coalition under H D Kumaraswamy and later BJP governments under B S Yeddyurappa and Basavaraj Bommai—to withhold the report’s release for over five years. Last week, the Vokkaligara Sangha convened in Bengaluru, urging the government to reject the report. The event included representatives from all parties and influential seers, with Deputy Chief Minister D K Shivakumar (himself a Vokkaliga) in attendance. The Sangha plans to send a delegation of religious leaders to present their demands to CM Siddaramaiah. Similarly, the All India Veerashaiva Mahasabha, a prominent Lingayat organization, recently met in Bengaluru and resolved to ask the government not to accept the survey report. The Mahasabha's president, Congress MLA Shamanur Shivashankarappa, claimed the survey was 'unscientific' and poorly conducted, asserting that surveyors did not visit households and calling for a new census. Karnataka’s Backward Classes Minister, Shivaraj Tangadagi, stated the government will review the report's findings before making any decisions. The caste-wise survey, conducted under chairman H Kantharaj, cost Rs 162 crore and aimed to assess the educational and economic status of all communities. The release of the report has sparked controversy because some leaked findings challenge the perception that Lingayats and Vokkaligas are the most populous communities, instead suggesting that Scheduled Castes (SCs) may be the largest group in the state. KSCBC chairman Jayaprakash Hegde confirmed the report will be submitted to the government by the end of November, after which the government will decide on its release. Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, responding to opposition, stated that the report is yet to be submitted and will be considered once it is. Earlier, he declared his government would accept the report and use its data to provide facilities and improve access to education, employment, and industry for all communities. Siddaramaiah emphasized that reliable, data-driven information is essential for allocating reservations and resources equitably.
translated_content: Die Kongres-geleide Karnataka-regering, onder leiding van Eerste Minister Siddaramaiah, word gekonfronteer met eise van die Lingayat- en Vokkaliga-gemeenskappe om die komende sosio-ekonomiese en opvoedkundige (kaste-)opnameverslag te verwerp, wat teen die einde van die maand deur die Karnataka Kommissie vir Agtergeblewe Klasse (KSCBC) verwag word. Terwyl hierdie dominante gemeenskappe hul teenkanting uitgespreek het, druk sekere agtergeblewe en kwesbare groepe, asook lede van die Kongresparty, die regering om die verslag te aanvaar en bekend te maak. Die opname is oorspronklik in 2015 deur 'n vorige Kongres-regering onder leiding van Siddaramaiah geloods en in 2017 voltooi. Opeenvolgende regerings—insluitend die Janata Dal (Seku.)-Kongres-koalisieregering onder H D Kumaraswamy en later BJP-regerings onder B S Yeddyurappa en Basavaraj Bommai—het egter die publikasie van die verslag as gevolg van politieke bekommernisse vir meer as vyf jaar uitgestel. Verlede week het die Vokkaligara Sangha in Bengaluru vergader en die regering versoek om die verslag te verwerp. Die byeenkoms het verteenwoordigers van alle partye en invloedryke geestelikes ingesluit, met Adjunk Eerste Minister D K Shivakumar (self ‘n Vokkaliga) teenwoordig. Die Sangha beplan om ‘n afvaardiging van godsdienstige leiers na Eerste Minister Siddaramaiah te stuur om hul eise te stel. Net so het die All India Veerashaiva Mahasabha, ‘n prominente Lingayat-organisasie, onlangs in Bengaluru vergader en besluit om die regering te vra om nie die opnameverslag te aanvaar nie. Die president van die Mahasabha, Kongres-LP Shamanur Shivashankarappa, het beweer die opname is ‘onwetenskaplik’ en swak uitgevoer, aangesien opnamebeamptes nie huishoudings besoek het nie, en het ‘n nuwe sensus aanbeveel. Karnataka se Minister van Agtergeblewe Klasse, Shivaraj Tangadagi, het gesê dat die regering eers die verslag se bevindings sal hersien voordat enige beslissing geneem word. Die kaste-opname, onder voorsitterskap van H Kantharaj, het R162 miljoen gekos en was gemik om die opvoedkundige en ekonomiese status van alle gemeenskappe te bepaal. Die vrystelling van die verslag het omstredenheid veroorsaak omdat sekere uitlekkasies die siening uitdaag dat Lingayats en Vokkaligas die grootste bevolkingsgroepe is, en eerder aandui dat Geskeduleerde Kaste (GK’s) dalk die grootste groep in die staat is. KSCBC-voorsitter Jayaprakash Hegde het bevestig dat die verslag teen die einde van November aan die regering voorgelê sal word, waarna die regering oor die verdere proses sal besluit. Eerste Minister Siddaramaiah het in reaksie op teenstand gesê die verslag is nog nie voorgelê nie en sal oorweeg word sodra dit ontvang is. Vroeër het hy verklaar dat sy regering die verslag sal aanvaar en op sy data sal staatmaak om fasiliteite en toegang tot onderwys, werk en nywerheid vir alle gemeenskappe te verbeter. Siddaramaiah het beklemtoon betroubare, data-gedrewe inligting is noodsaaklik vir billike toewysing van kwotas en hulpbronne.

article_content: A former mental health patient alleges she was sexually assaulted up to 60 times by a senior staff member at Little Brook Hospital in Dartford, Kent. According to her account, the staff member groomed her with gifts like cigarettes, chocolate, and Valium. Now in her 40s, she describes psychiatric hospitals as risky environments for vulnerable individuals and says she was manipulated into thinking the abuse was her escape route. She refrained from reporting the abuse while hospitalized out of concern that her accusations would not be trusted over those of a respected care worker. While in the hospital, she faced threats of being sectioned if she tried to leave, and the assaults became nearly nightly occurrences. She contracted a sexually transmitted disease before the abuse came to light. After her release, she reported the incidents, which led to the care worker being charged and pleading guilty to one count of unlawful sexual intercourse with a patient. He received a 12-month suspended prison sentence and was prohibited by the NHS Trust from working with vulnerable people. The woman received £100,000 as compensation in 2003 and 2004. Kent and Medway NHS Trust stated they could not comment on matters occurring before their management. The woman now calls for stronger protections to safeguard mental health patients from such abuse.

Sy het nie die mishandeling gerapporteer terwyl sy in die hospitaal was nie uit vrees dat personeel nie haar beskuldigings sou glo teenoor die van ‘n gerespekteerde versorger nie. Sy is gedreig dat sy opgeneem sou word indien sy probeer het om te vertrek, en die aanrandings het byna elke aand gebeur. article_content: On Wednesday, the Indian rupee finished trading nearly unchanged, caught between strong domestic demand for US dollars and decreases in crude oil prices and US Treasury yields. The rupee settled at 83.2725 per US dollar, only marginally lower than the previous session's 83.2575. Throughout November, it has traded within a narrow range of 83.14 to 83.2950. Currency markets have felt the impact of global oil trends, with Brent crude dropping to $81.65—a decline of more than 6% this month—due to higher OPEC exports and worries about energy demand in China and the US. While the US dollar index climbed to 105.84, it remains below last week's peak above 107. The 10-year US Treasury yield saw little movement during Asian hours after Tuesday's 9-basis point slide. Foreign exchange traders highlight that, unlike several Asian currencies that rallied when the dollar eased earlier this week, the rupee has lagged behind. Analysts suggest the rupee’s response is increasingly less connected to fundamental factors. Volatility in the dollar-rupee pair has dropped sharply, partly due to regular interventions by the Reserve Bank of India. Across Asian currencies, only the Hong Kong dollar (which is pegged to the US dollar) has shown lower volatility recently. A Reuters poll of currency analysts expects the rupee to remain around 83.25 per dollar over the next month, unless there is a significant fall in the dollar index, according to Anindya Banerjee, head of FX research at Kotak Securities. He noted that the rupee could face more downward pressure if the dollar does not weaken considerably. Investors are awaiting comments from US Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, which could influence market direction. On the consumer front, Indian packaged goods saw value growth of 9% and volume growth of 8.6% in the September quarter compared to the previous year, according to NielsenIQ. Much of this growth came from increased rural spending on both basic and discretionary goods. In the tech sector, Snap Inc.—Snapchat’s parent company—doubled its user base in India to 200 million users in one year by launching new features like the Spotlight platform, which competes with short video offerings from rivals. Meanwhile, the Indian finance ministry is reportedly considering slowing the pace of capital expenditure increases in its next interim budget to align with fiscal consolidation targets.

Die roepie het op 83.2725 per Amerikaanse dollar gesluit, slegs effens laer as die vorige sessie se 83.2575. Gedurende November het dit in ‘n nou band tussen 83.14 en 83.2950 verhandel. Geldmarkte is beïnvloed deur wêreldolietendense, waar Brent-ruolie tot $81.65 afgeneem het—meer as 6% laer hierdie maand—vanweë stygende OPEC-uitvoer en kommer oor vraag in China en die VSA. article_content: Apple has announced the finalists for its 2023 iPhone App of the Year award: AllTrails, Duolingo, and Flighty. Each year, Apple recognizes exceptional apps and games across its platforms, selecting finalists and winners for various categories. Apple Fellow Phil Schiller revealed the list of finalists, with winners to be announced later this month. The company has highlighted these apps for their innovation and usefulness. Flighty is a flight tracking app that provides detailed flight information—including early gate updates, real-time aircraft tracking, and advance notifications about delays, sometimes ahead of airlines. It now offers the ability to track friends' flights as well. Duolingo is well-known for language learning, offering courses ranging from Spanish and Portuguese to Klingon and High Valyrian. Recently, Duolingo introduced subjects like Math and Music, expanding its educational scope. AllTrails helps users discover and navigate hiking, running, and biking routes with comprehensive information and a user-friendly design. Apple’s list of finalists spans several categories, featuring both apps and games for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Apple Arcade. Notable game finalists include Return to Monkey Island and Honkai: Star Rail. For a complete list of finalists—including categories for Cultural Impact—Apple will announce the winners soon.

article_content: Workplace dissatisfaction is increasingly evident, with trends like 'quiet quitting'—where workers quietly disengage—and 'resenteeism'—ongoing resentment affecting morale and success—drawing growing attention. Younger staff may disconnect if their work feels meaningless or doesn’t allow for growth or work-life balance, while seasoned employees might feel trapped for financial reasons, leading to bitterness or concerns about being sidelined. No matter how it's expressed, disengagement typically stems from feeling stuck, harming productivity, customer experience, and company results. To combat this, leaders should drive systemic, team-based solutions with open communication and accountability. Organizations can: survey and talk to staff to pinpoint issues, get employees involved in fixing problems, create prioritized action plans with deadlines, and make sure teams and leadership are working together to implement changes. Manager training is vital so supervisors can better support staff, and employees should be regularly informed about available benefits—including mental health resources. Reassessing role fit is important, as mismatches can impact teams. Showcasing the organization’s strengths, both internally and publicly, reinforces its positive identity. Addressing disengagement and resentment not only supports employee well-being but also lifts overall organizational performance.

Jonger personeel onttrek gereeld as hul werk sinloos voel of nie ruimte vir groei of balans tussen werk en lewe bied nie, terwyl meer ervare werknemers vasgevang kan voel weens finansiële redes, wat lei tot wrewel of vrees om uitgeskuif te word. 'n Gevoel van vasgekeer wees is dikwels die oorsprong van onbetrokkenheid, wat produktiwiteit, kliënte-ervaring en maatskappy se resultate benadeel. Om dit teen te werk, moet leiers oplossings sistematies op spanvlak bestuur met oop kommunikasie en aanspreeklikheid. Organisasies kan: opnames hou en met personeel gesels om probleme te identifiseer; werknemers by oplossings betrek; geprioritiseerde aksieplanne met duidelike sperdatums maak; en sorg dat spanne en leiers om saam veranderinge deur te voer. article_content: Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg has conditionally backed Conservative plans to place stricter requirements on welfare benefits for people under 25 who turn down work or training opportunities. While he agrees that young people should be encouraged to work, study, or take up apprenticeships, Clegg does not support policies that cut benefits solely due to age. Prime Minister David Cameron laid out at the Conservative Party Conference a vision in which all under-25s are either in employment or education. The proposal could see JobSeeker's Allowance and Housing Benefit withdrawn from those refusing jobs, apprenticeships, training or further education. Clegg emphasized on LBC radio that while stronger incentives are important to discourage reliance on benefits, removing support unselectively is not fair. He cited examples such as youths moving cities for education or employment as reasons for case-by-case assessments and exemptions. Treasury Minister Sajid Javid stated the crackdown is intended to apply to all under-25s but admitted that the specific policy details still need to be finalized. He argued the approach is justified to protect taxpayers and prevent young people from becoming long-term welfare recipients. Discussions within the coalition continue as leaders aim to balance encouraging work and learning among young people with protecting individuals who may need extra support.

Hoewel hy glo jongmense moet aangemoedig word om te werk, studeer of 'n vakleerlingskap te doen, ondersteun Clegg nie 'n beleid waar toelaes net op grond van ouderdom gesny word nie. Eerste Minister David Cameron het tydens die Konserwatiewe Party-konferensie beklemtoon dat alle onder-25's óf moet werk, óf leer. Die voorstel kan beteken dat die Werksoekerstoelaag en Behuisingstoelaag weggeneem sal word van dié wat werks-, opleidings-, vakleerlingskap- of verdere studiegeleenthede weier. Clegg het op LBC-radio uitgelig dat sterk aansporings belangrik is om af te skrik teen welsynsafhanklikheid, maar het gewaarsku dat dit onregverdig sou wees om ondersteuning sonder uitsonderings te verwyder. As voorbeeld noem hy jongmense wat verhuis het vir werk of studie, as rede vir individuele evaluasies en uitsonderings. Koalisie-besprekings duur voort soos leiers 'n balans probeer vind tussen die bevordering van werk en studie onder jongmense, en die beskerming van dié wat bykomende ondersteuning nodig het.

article_content: Kabaddi is among India's oldest indigenous sports, blending elements of tag, wrestling, and strategy. Many Indians recall playing kabaddi as children, including celebrities such as Bollywood actor Abhishek Bachchan, who is now a professional kabaddi league team owner. The sport demands strength, stamina, and the ability to hold one's breath while raiding. Traditionally, kabaddi is played with simple means—just lines drawn in the dirt. Each team of seven takes turns sending a 'raider' to the opponent's side, aiming to tag as many defenders as possible and return safely before being tackled. The catch: the raider must hold their breath and continuously chant 'kabaddi, kabaddi, kabaddi' to prove it. Over the years, urban interest in kabaddi declined, overtaken by cricket and, to a lesser extent, football—sports with broad television exposure. Analyst Charu Sharma observes that as cricket's TV visibility soared, kabaddi receded into rural popularity. A revival is now underway. Sharma, together with business leader Anand Mahindra, has launched India's first professional kabaddi league, modeled on the Indian Premier League (IPL). The league features eight franchises, many owned by industry and Bollywood figures, and matches are played indoors on mats. Major broadcaster Star Sports has committed to airing league games live at prime time, hoping to foster a multi-sport culture. Early results are promising: the opening match attracted 66 million viewers across India, ten times the audience for the country's FIFA World Cup opener. Celebrity appearances and modern entertainment features have added to the spectacle. Today, kabaddi is far more than a rural game. Both Bachchan and top player Rakesh Kumar express excitement and surprise over the sport’s dynamic resurgence on the national stage.

article_content: Rape is a crime in which, far too often, only the victim pays a price. In America, out of every 100 rapes, just 46 are reported to police, and only three rapists will spend even a day behind bars. This is especially concerning given that rapists often reoffend—so each offender left on the streets could attack again. On Monday, in a significant decision for public safety and victims of sexual violence, the U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling in Maryland v. King. This decision is set to greatly impact our nation’s ability to bring rapists to justice. After being arrested on assault charges in 2009, Alonzo King had his cheek swabbed—a quick and painless process Justice Anthony Kennedy described in his majority opinion as 'a minor intrusion.' The sample was analyzed, and the resulting DNA profile was entered into the Combined DNA Index System (CODIS), the federal database. King’s DNA matched evidence from a six-year-old crime scene, and he was later convicted for the rape of a 53-year-old woman at gunpoint. CODIS stores DNA profiles from over 10 million offenders and records from around half a million crime scenes. It has led to more than 205,000 matches, aiding in over 197,000 investigations. Without such a system, King and many others might still be free to commit more crimes. King appealed his conviction, and a Maryland court overturned it. Maryland is one of 26 states that collect DNA from individuals arrested on certain felony charges, viewing it as a more accurate form of fingerprinting. The other states wait until after a conviction to collect DNA. The Maryland court ruled that collecting DNA from arrestees violated the Fourth Amendment, but the state appealed. The U.S. Supreme Court’s ruling overturned the Maryland decision. During oral arguments, Justice Samuel A. Alito Jr. described this as 'perhaps the most important criminal procedure case this court has heard in decades.' The decision is expected to provide significant benefits to victims of rape and their families in pursuit of justice. DNA has become the fingerprint of the 21st century, and police have long been able to collect fingerprints during arrest to match them to unsolved crimes. For example, Katie Sepich, a 22-year-old graduate student at New Mexico State University, was raped and strangled in August 2003. In 2006, DNA from beneath Katie’s fingernails was linked to a man later convicted of her rape and murder, who had also committed several other crimes since. Opponents of collecting DNA from people arrested for felonies raise concerns about government overreach and genetic privacy. However, CODIS does not store an individual's full genetic profile—only 13 specific genetic markers chosen because they lack links to health or physical traits. These markers allow for identification much like fingerprints. Kennedy wrote that using DNA for identification is a legitimate booking procedure, like matching fingerprints or tattoos. Fears that CODIS could be misused are unfounded: accessing it for non-law enforcement purposes is illegal and has never occurred; moreover, the database does not store names—any match simply prompts law enforcement to ask the submitting jurisdiction for identity information. A cheek swab is less invasive than many typical arrest procedures. Thanks to DNA, tens of thousands of criminals have been brought to justice, particularly in cases of sexual violence. The Supreme Court’s decision ensures that law enforcement will continue to have access to this essential tool. The views in this commentary are those of Scott Berkowitz.

In Amerika word slegs 46 uit elke 100 verkragtings by die polisie aangemeld, en net drie verkragters beland selfs vir een dag agter tralies. Dit is veral kommerwekkend omdat verkragters dikwels weer oortree—dus kan elke oortreder wat vry rondloop, weer aanval. Die monster is ontleed, en die DNA-profiel is in die Gesamentlike DNA-Indeksstelsel (CODIS), die federale databasis, geplaas. King se DNA het ooreengestem met bewyse van 'n ses jaar oue misdaadtoneel, en hy is later skuldig bevind aan die verkragting van 'n 53-jarige vrou met 'n vuurwapen. CODIS bevat DNA-profiele van meer as 10 miljoen oortreders en rekords van sowat 'n halfmiljoen misdaadtonele. Dit het reeds tot meer as 205 000 treffers gelei en meer as 197 000 ondersoeke gehelp. Sonder so 'n stelsel sou King en baie ander dalk steeds vry wees om verdere misdade te pleeg. King het sy skuldigbevinding geappelleer en 'n Maryland-hof het dit omgekeer. Maryland is een van 26 state wat DNA van verdagtes in sekere misdrywe neem, en sien dit as 'n meer akkurate vorm van vingerafdrukke. Die ander state wag tot na skuldigbevinding om DNA te neem. Die Maryland-hof het beslis dat die neem van DNA by gearresteerdes die Vierde Wysiging geskend het, maar die staat het geappelleer. Die Hooggeregshof se uitspraak het Maryland se beslissing omvergewerp. Tydens mondelinge betoog het Regter Samuel A. Alito Jr. dit beskryf as 'miskien die belangrikste strafprosedure-saak wat hierdie hof in dekades aangehoor het.' Die beslissing behoort beduidende voordele vir slagoffers van verkragting en hul families in hul strewe na geregtigheid in te hou. DNA word gesien as die vingerafdruk van die 21ste eeu, en polisie kon lank reeds vingerafdrukke neem by inhegtenisneming om hulle aan onopgeloste sake te koppel. Byvoorbeeld, Katie Sepich, 'n 22-jarige nagraadse student aan New Mexico State University, is in Augustus 2003 verkrag en verwurg. In 2006 is DNA van onder Katie se naels aan 'n man gekoppel wat later aan haar verkragting en moord skuldig bevind is, en wat ook sedertdien ander misdade gepleeg het. Teenstanders van DNA-ontneming tydens inhegtenisneming is bekommerd oor oormatige staatsbeheer en genetiese privaatheid. Sonder egter om iemand se volledige genetiese profiel te stoor, bevat CODIS slegs 13 spesifieke genetiese merkers, gekies omdat dit nie met gesondheid of fisieke eienskappe verband hou nie. Hierdie merkers dien bloot om mense te identifiseer, soos vingerafdrukke. Kennedy het geskryf dat DNA vir identifikasie 'n wettige prosedure is, soos die neem van vingerafdrukke of die vergelyking van tatoeëermerke. Vrees dat CODIS misbruik kan word, is ongegrond: toegang vir nie-wetstoepassing is onwettig en het nog nie plaasgevind nie; die databasis hou ook nie name nie—enige treffer beteken wetstoepassers navraag doen by die jurisdiksie wat die profiel ingedien het. 'n Wangdeppers is minder indringend as baie ander gewone inhegtenisnemingsprosedures. Danksy DNA is duisende misdadigers aan die pen gehou, veral in gevalle van seksuele geweld. Die Hooggeregshof se uitspraak verseker dat wetstoepassing steeds toegang tot hierdie noodsaaklike hulpmiddel het. Die menings in hierdie kommentaar is dié van Scott Berkowitz.

article_content: As Americans gather for Thanksgiving feasts, they celebrate a tradition rooted in a meal shared over 400 years ago between colonists and Wampanoag Native Americans in Patuxet, now Plymouth, Massachusetts. Yet, this 1621 gathering holds greater meaning for Americans today than it did at the time. Only scant historical records describe the event—attendees likely ate more seafood than turkey—and it was neither the first nor a particularly friendly encounter. Paula Peters, a Mashpee Wampanoag curator, observes that her ancestors did not intend to share dinner but arrived armed out of fear. Numerous myths and misconceptions surround this event. TIME consulted Native American historians to highlight moments in Indigenous history more significant than the so-called First Thanksgiving. These episodes, ranging from a catastrophic plague to Indigenous resistance and contemporary activism, better reflect the complex colonial-Indigenous relationship. European and English sailors brought a deadly disease to the Wampanoag’s Patuxet homeland, devastating Indigenous populations from Maine to Cape Cod and leaving tens of thousands dead—so many that proper burials were impossible. When Squanto, a Wampanoag who had been captured and learned English, returned home, he found his entire family gone. Hostility and violence, rather than camaraderie, defined most colonial-Indigenous interactions. The Anglo-Powhatan war erupted in 1622 when colonial expansion threatened local tribes, leading Powhatan leaders to resist. English soldiers violated the conventions of war, poisoning 200 Powhatans. In 2008, Virginia marked this with a plaque acknowledging it as a war crime according to English standards of the era. King Philip’s War (1675–76) further strained relations. King Philip (Pumetacom), son of Massasoit, who once brokered the Thanksgiving treaty, led Indigenous resistance against expanding English settlements. Land dispossession and abuses drove Native people into debt and servitude, culminating in war. Thousands died or were enslaved; King Philip was killed, and his family sold overseas. Violent conflicts like these, not harmonious feasts, characterized Indigenous-colonial history. In the Southwest, the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 saw Puebloans drive out the Spanish colonists for a time, resisting cultural eradication. Though the Spanish retook the territory in 1692, the revolt stands out as an early act of Indigenous resistance and is sometimes called the first American revolution. Pontiac, an Odawa leader born near Detroit, led Indigenous efforts against the British in the 1760s. Though unsuccessful in retaking Detroit, Pontiac’s impact endures—his name was adopted by a car brand and commemorated within Detroit, symbolizing the city’s Indigenous past. In the 19th century, U.S. policy shifted to forced assimilation. Boarding schools like Carlisle in Pennsylvania forcibly removed Native children, attempting to erase their identities. Despite such brutal efforts, Indigenous peoples persist: the U.S. now has over 560 federally recognized tribes, with hundreds of languages still spoken. On November 20, 1969, over 80 Native activists occupied Alcatraz Island to highlight treaty violations and discrimination. This 19-month demonstration inspired further activism, reshaped U.S. policies on Native rights, and continues to be commemorated through annual sunrise ceremonies. In 1987, the Wampanoag Tribe of Aquinnah received federal acknowledgment, regaining some land and governance after centuries of dispossession. Their story, pre-dating the Pilgrims, demonstrates lasting resilience and efforts to reclaim sovereignty.
translated_content: Soos Amerikaners vir Thanksgiving saamkom, vier hulle 'n tradisie wat sy oorsprong het in 'n maaltyd meer as 400 jaar gelede tussen koloniste en Wampanoag Inheemse Amerikaners in Patuxet, bekend as Plymouth, Massachusetts. Hierdie 1621-byeenkoms dra vandag meer betekenis vir Amerikaners as destyds. Slegs bondige historiese rekords beskryf die gebeurtenis—met waarskynlik meer seekos as kalkoen op die tafel—en dit was nie die eerste of besonder vriendelike ontmoeting nie. Paula Peters, 'n Mashpee Wampanoag-kurator, wys daarop dat haar voorouers nie vir ete gekom het nie, maar gewapen opgedaag het uit vrees. Verskeie mites en wanopvattings bestaan oor hierdie gebeurtenis. TIME het met inheemse Amerikaanse historici gesels om gebeure in inheemse geskiedenis uit te lig wat betekenisvoller was as die sogenaamde Eerste Thanksgiving. Hierdie episodes, van 'n verwoestende plaag tot verset en aktiewe selfdoen vandag, wys die ingewikkelde verhouding tussen koloniste en inheemse volke. Europese en Engelse seevaarders het 'n dodelike siekte na die Wampanoag se Patuxet-huisland gebring wat inheemse dorpies van Maine tot by Cape Cod uitgewis en derduisende lewens geëis het—soveel dat gepaste begrafnisse nie moontlik was nie. Toe Squanto, 'n Wampanoag wat gevange geneem en Engels geleer het, huis toe keer, was sy hele familie weg. Vyandigheid en geweld, nie kameraderie nie, was die norm vir koloniale-inheemse verhoudings. Die Anglo-Powhatan-oorlog het in 1622 uitgebreek toe koloniale uitbreiding 'n bedreiging inhou. Engelse soldate het die reëls van oorlog oortree en 200 Powhatans vergiftig. In 2008 het Virginia hierdie voorval met 'n plaket herdenk wat dit as 'n oorlogsmisdaad volgens destydse Engelse standaarde erken. King Philip se Oorlog (1675–76) het verhoudings verder versuur. King Philip (Pumetacom), seun van Massasoit wat die Thanksgiving-verdrag bemiddel het, het inheemse weerstand teen Engelse uitbreiding gelei. Grondonteiening en misbruik het inheemse mense in skuld en diensbaarheid gedryf en tot oorlog gelei. Duisende het gesterf of is as slawe verkoop; King Philip is dood en sy familie oorsee verkoop. Sulke konflikte, nie feesvierings nie, het die geskiedenis gekenmerk. In die suidweste het die Pueblo-opstand van 1680 gesien hoe Puebloans die Spaanse koloniste tydelik verdryf en hul kultuur beskerm. Al het die Spaanse in 1692 teruggekeer, word die opstand as die eerste Amerikaanse rewolusie beskou. Pontiac, 'n Odawa-leier naby Detroit gebore, het in die 1760's teen die Britte geveg. Sy poging om Detroit terug te neem was onsuksesvol, maar sy nalatenskap leef voort in die motorhandelsmerk en herdenking binne Detroit. In die 19de eeu het VSA-beleid verander na gedwonge assimilasie. Internate soos Carlisle het inheemse kinders ontwortel en hul kultuur probeer uitwis. Tog oorleef inheemse volke: daar is meer as 560 federale erkende stamme en honderde tale in die VSA vandag. Op 20 November 1969 het meer as 80 inheemse aktiviste Alcatraz-eiland beset, wat vir 19 maande geduur het. Dié protes het groter bewusmaking en hervorming gebring en word steeds jaarliks met sonopseremonies herdenk. In 1987 het die Wampanoag stam van Aquinnah weer federale erkenning ontvang. Ná eeue van grondonteiening, kon hulle sekere regte op hul land en selfbestuur herwin. Dié storie wys hul vasberadenheid om hul soewereiniteit te herwin.

article_content: Kevin McCarthy was removed as Speaker of the House last week after a group of Republicans, with unified Democratic support, voted in favor of a motion to vacate led by Rep. Matt Gaetz of Florida. The GOP swiftly blamed Democrats for enabling the ouster, labeling them the 'Chaos Caucus' in a social media post. Democrats argued they had little reason to save McCarthy, pointing to his antagonistic moves, such as opening an impeachment inquiry into President Joe Biden without a vote, downplaying January 6 events, defying a committee subpoena, and blaming Democrats for a near government shutdown. There is precedent for cross-party support in such scenarios. In 2015, then-Speaker John Boehner faced a similar revolt within his party and ultimately resigned. Later, Nancy Pelosi, then the House Minority Leader, explained that Democrats were ready to quietly support Boehner by being absent during a potential vote, which would have increased his chances of survival by reducing the number needed for a majority. Pelosi told reporters they would 'protect the institution' and prevent the Speaker’s overthrow, according to the Daily Beast. But dynamics in Congress have since changed. Pelosi is no longer in party leadership and missed the McCarthy vote due to attending Senator Dianne Feinstein’s funeral. Polarization between parties has increased, especially after Donald Trump’s presidency and the Capitol riot. Pelosi’s previous stance attracted attention when McCarthy recounted that she had promised to back him if he faced a motion to vacate, just as she had done for Boehner and Ryan, out of respect for the institution. However, following McCarthy's removal, Pelosi said circumstances had changed, asserting McCarthy did not respect the House. She told Fox 11 Los Angeles, 'The integrity of the institution is very important to me. But if you don’t respect the institution, don’t expect us to bail you out.'

article_content: Photographs of celebrities captured informally by artist Andy Warhol will be publicly exhibited for the first time. Toward the end of his career, the American pop artist focused on photography, taking candid photos of his famous friends during relaxed and spontaneous moments. Many subjects were showbusiness acquaintances who visited Warhol’s beach house or his New York studio, The Factory. The new exhibition, titled 'I'll Be Your Mirror,' will showcase stars such as John Lennon, Mick Jagger, Elizabeth Taylor, Madonna, Sting, Bruce Springsteen, Liza Minnelli, Diana Ross, and Debbie Harry. These never-before-seen photographs are now part of an upcoming exhibition. One 1979 photo shows John Lennon with Halston, the boyfriend of fashion designer Roy Halston Frowick, in New York, a year before Lennon was killed. The exhibition includes images of Mick Jagger alongside author William Burroughs, and John 'Jellybean' Benitez with Madonna. There are candid shots of Bruce Springsteen, as well as iconic figures such as Lou Reed and Ronnie Wood. Warhol's photography also featured everyday items, including room service trays and even rows of toilet urinals, as well as several self-portraits—one of which shows Warhol in a green sweater eating cornflakes. Warhol, who died in 1987, made only one print of each photograph, making them unique pieces of art. Many were gifted to his longtime diarist Pat Hackett, who is now exhibiting and selling them. Some prints are owned by Warhol collector Jim Hedges. These prints, on silver gelatin paper from 35mm negatives taken between 1976 and 1987, will be sold through 1stdibs.com for up to £5,000 each. Pat Hackett commented that photography became an important phase in Warhol’s artistic development and that these images have not previously received the attention they deserve. Bianca Jagger, Liza Minnelli, Debbie Harry, and others also appear in the collection. The exhibition opens at the New York Design Center on September 3.
translated_content: Foto's van bekendes wat Andy Warhol informeel vasgevang het, sal vir die eerste keer aan die publiek vertoon word. Teen die einde van sy loopbaan het die Amerikaanse popkunstenaar op fotografie gefokus en spontane foto’s van sy beroemde vriende geneem. Baie van die onderwerp was bekendes uit die vermaaklikheidswêreld wat Warhol se strandhuis of sy ateljee in New York, bekend as The Factory, besoek het. Die nuwe uitstalling, getiteld 'I'll Be Your Mirror', gaan sterre vertoon soos John Lennon, Mick Jagger, Elizabeth Taylor, Madonna, Sting, Bruce Springsteen, Liza Minnelli, Diana Ross en Debbie Harry. Hierdie nooit-voorheen-gesiene foto's maak nou deel uit van ’n komende uitstalling. Een 1979-foto wys John Lennon saam met Halston, die kêrel van die mode-ontwerper Roy Halston Frowick, in New York, ’n jaar voor Lennon vermoor is. Die uitstalling sluit beelde in van Mick Jagger saam met die outeur William Burroughs, en John 'Jellybean' Benitez saam met Madonna. Daar is ook spontane foto’s van Bruce Springsteen, sowel as ikoniese figure soos Lou Reed en Ronnie Wood. Warhol se fotografie het ook alledaagse items uitgebeeld, soos ’n kamerdiensskinkbord en selfs toilette in ’n ry, asook verskeie selfportrette—insluitend een waar Warhol in ’n groen trui mielievlokkies eet. Warhol, wat in 1987 oorlede is, het net een afdruk van elke foto gemaak, wat dit unieke kunswerke maak. Baie is aan sy jarelange dagboekskrywer Pat Hackett geskenk, wat dit nou uitstal en verkoop. Sommige afdrukke word besit deur Warhol-versamelaar Jim Hedges. Hierdie afdrukke, op silwer-gelatienpapier van 35mm-negatiewe geneem tussen 1976 en 1987, sal by 1stdibs.com verkoop word vir tot £5,000 elk. Pat Hackett het opgemerk dat fotografie ’n belangrike fase van Warhol se artistieke ontwikkeling geword het en dat hierdie beelde nog nie die aandag ontvang het wat dit verdien nie. Bianca Jagger, Liza Minnelli, Debbie Harry en ander verskyn ook in die versameling. Die uitstalling open op 3 September by die New York Design Center.

article_content: Australia's Matildas, the women’s national soccer team, will be paid through match fees and commercial deals instead of centralized contracts. This is a result of a new four-year collective bargaining agreement signed after their impressive semi-final run at the 2023 Women’s World Cup, which attracted huge crowds and TV viewers. The new pay structure for the Matildas is now the same as the Socceroos, the men’s team. Reports say Matildas players could get up to an extra $80,000 per year, along with their club wages and prize money. The agreement covers big tournaments such as the Asian Cups in 2023 and 2027, the Paris 2024 Olympics, and the 2026 and 2027 FIFA World Cups. A revenue-sharing model is in place—players receive 70% from match fees and 30% from annual commercial payments. Both men's and women's teams benefit from this. Plus, Matildas' travel and preparation standards will match the men’s team, with single rooms and business-class flights offered to support players. The pregnancy policy now allows carers to accompany players with children up to four years old. At least 5% of national team revenues will fund youth development. Over four years, $2 million is allocated to Professional Footballers Australia for player support and growth. Football Australia will introduce a human rights policy and contribute to the Past Players Program. CEO James Johnson called the new CBA an innovative system linking player rewards with team success, saying growing the sport means more opportunities for players. PFA co-chief executive and former Matildas captain Kathryn Gill highlighted that such agreements have built a foundation for the sport's growth, and the new deal will help advance Australian football's success on the world stage.

Football Australia is besig om ’n menseregtebeleid in te stel en sal aan die Past Players Program bydra.
