article_content: The CEO and founder of BlueTuskr, an agency specializing in digital marketing for online sellers and host of The E-Comm Show podcast, discusses how e-commerce has evolved following the extraordinary surge during the Covid-19 pandemic. In 2020, e-commerce sales in the U.S. increased by an impressive 28%, followed by an additional 22% in 2021. This remarkable growth resulted from restrictions that limited consumers to online shopping. After pandemic measures eased, shoppers began returning to brick-and-mortar stores, resulting in slower growth. Signs of this change appeared as early as February 2021, when the intention to shop online started declining in several sectors, while still staying higher than pre-pandemic times. From 2022 to 2023, e-commerce growth in the U.S. slowed to approximately 14%—about half of what was seen during the pandemic’s peak. Although disappointing, this slowdown was expected as habits normalized. Business owners now facing lower sales and conversion rates should be cautious not to compare current performance with the atypical periods of 2020-2021. For example, average online conversion rates reached 2.8% in late 2021 but dropped to 2.3% afterward. Nevertheless, current results remain stronger than what would have been possible without the pandemic boost. While annual e-commerce growth has leveled off to rates seen before 2020, the sector itself has nearly doubled compared to 2019’s size, still offering substantial prospects for retailers. Retailers are urged to focus on realistic comparisons, such as year-over-year growth and quarterly key performance indicators, like conversions, average order value, and repeat customers, rather than relying on pandemic-time figures. The future remains bright, with global e-commerce expected to surpass $6.3 trillion in 2024 and online sales set to make up more than 20% of total retail sales. By monitoring metrics and strategic planning, businesses can build for long-term, steady growth. Finally, the author mentions the Forbes Agency Council, a private community for leaders in public relations, media, and creative industries.
translated_content: Die HUB en stigter van BlueTuskr, 'n agentskap wat digitale bemarking vir aanlynhandelaars aanbied en aanbieder van The E-Comm Show-podcast, bespreek hoe e-handel verander het na die buitengewone groei tydens die Covid-19-pandemie. In 2020 het e-handelsverkope in die VSA met 28% toegeneem, gevolg deur nog 22% in 2021. Hierdie besonderse groei het plaasgevind omdat pandemiebeperkings verbruikers genoodsaak het om aanlyn te koop. Ná die verligting van pandemiebeperkings het kopers begin terugkeer na fisiese winkels, wat tot stadiger groei gelei het. Tekens hiervan was al in Februarie 2021 sigbaar toe aanlyn koopvoornemens in sekere sektore begin afneem het, hoewel dit steeds hoër as voor die pandemie gebly het. Van 2022 tot 2023 het e-handelgroei in die VSA verlangsaam tot ongeveer 14%—omtrent die helfte van die groei tydens die pandemie se hoogtepunt. Al mag dit teleurstellend wees, was hierdie afname voorspelbaar soos patrons genormaliseer het. Besighede wat tans laer verkope en omskakelingskoerse beleef, moet nie hul huidige syfers met dié van die abnormale 2020/2021 vergelyk nie. Byvoorbeeld, gemiddelde aanlyn omskakelingskoerse het in laat 2021 2.8% bereik, maar het toe tot 2.3% gedaal. Tog is die huidige prestasie steeds merkbaar beter as wat dit sonder die pandemie sou gewees het. Al het die jaarlikse groei van e-handel nou terugbeweeg na vlakke van voor 2020, is die sektor self feitlik dubbel die grootte van 2019, en bied steeds groot vooruitsigte. Handelaars word aangeraai om op realistiese vergelykings te fokus—soos jaarlikse groei en die dop van sleutelmaatstawwe soos omskakelings, gemiddelde bestellingswaarde en herhalende klante kwartaalliks—in plaas daarvan om net na die pandemietyd te kyk. Die toekoms lyk positief: wêreldwye e-handelsverkope behoort in 2024 $6.3 triljoen te oorskry, en meer as 20% van totale kleinhandelsverkope sal waarskynlik aanlyn plaasvind. Deur jou maatstawwe dop te hou en strategies te beplan, kan besighede op volgehoue groei fokus. Die artikel sluit af met verwysing na die Forbes Agency Council, 'n geslote netwerk vir leiers in PR, media en kreatiewe sektore.

article_content: A severe storm has killed at least 16 people on the Italian island of Sardinia, with two people still unaccounted for and concerns that the death toll may rise, according to officials. Regional President Ugo Cappellacci described the situation as dramatic and critical in comments to Sky TG24. Italian Prime Minister Enrico Letta convened a Cabinet meeting to declare a state of emergency in Sardinia, announcing 20 million euros ($27 million) in immediate aid for the Mediterranean island. The funds will be used to save lives, assist displaced residents, and repair infrastructure. Italian President Giorgio Napolitano released a statement expressing solidarity with the affected communities. Civil Protection Agency spokeswoman Francesca Maffini said the two missing people are a farmer and a woman who lived alone, both from the province of Nuoro. Maffini reported that Sardinia received six months' worth of rainfall — 450 mm (over a foot) — in just 12 hours. In Parliament, Environment Minister Andrea Orlando stated the area's average yearly rainfall is 1,000 mm, and such an event has not occurred in centuries. CNN meteorologist Brandon Miller indicated that while the worst of the storm had moved past Sardinia, showers and gusty winds over 50 kph would continue through Wednesday as the storm system shifted east in the Mediterranean Sea. Italy’s state news agency ANSA reported that the storm, named Cleopatra, caused widespread flooding and forced thousands to seek shelter in public facilities such as gymnasiums. Among the victims was a Brazilian family of four who drowned after a flash flood struck their ground-floor apartment in Arzachena, near Olbia. Marco Vargiu, Olbia’s councilor for tourism, said the disaster has severely affected the town of about 70,000, with 13 deaths reported in the greater area. The deceased include two infants, and in one incident, a 35-year-old father and his 3-year-old son died in floodwaters. Vargiu described widespread property loss: many homes and cars were damaged or swept away by floods, with ground floors submerged by up to two meters of water. He emphasized the unprecedented nature of the disaster in Olbia and praised the solidarity and relief efforts of ministry staff, emergency workers, and volunteers. Vargiu noted that Olbia’s two hospitals were extremely busy handling injuries and emergencies. He estimated that the government’s aid may restore some transportation connections, but said it wouldn’t be sufficient for long-term recovery, given the significant economic impact and property losses. According to the Civil Protection Agency, 2,500 people have been displaced and over 10,000 are without power. The agency is working to reach all affected areas. Flooding and landslides have blocked roads, and officials urged people to travel only if necessary and to check conditions before traveling. The worst-hit provinces are Olbia and Nuoro, but the storm began in Campidano in southwestern Sardinia before spreading across the island. Olbia’s port remains open, and the airport is partially operational. The coast guard reported additional flooding in other parts of Italy, particularly near Catanzaro in Calabria and in Venice during high tide.
translated_content: ’n Ernstige storm het minstens 16 mense op die Italiaanse eiland Sardinië doodgemaak, met twee persone steeds vermis, en daar is vrese dat die dodetal kan styg, volgens amptenare. Streekspresident Ugo Cappellacci het die situasie as dramaties en kritiek beskryf in kommentaar aan Sky TG24. Die Italiaanse Eerste Minister Enrico Letta het ’n Kabinetsvergadering belê om ’n noodtoestand in Sardinië af te kondig en €20 miljoen ($27 miljoen) se onmiddellike hulp vir die Mediterreense eiland aangekondig. Die fondse sal aangewend word om lewens te red, ontheemdes te help, en infrastruktuur te herstel. Die Italiaanse president Giorgio Napolitano het ’n verklaring uitgereik waarin hy sy solidariteit met die getroffen gemeenskappe toon. Francesca Maffini, woordvoerder van die Burgerlike Beskermingsagentskap, het gesê die twee vermistes is ’n boer en ’n vrou wat alleen gewoon het, albei van die Nuoro-provinsie. Maffini het gesê Sardinië het ses maande se reënval — 450 mm (meer as ’n voet) — in slegs 12 uur ontvang. Omgewingsminister Andrea Orlando het in die parlement verklaar dat die streek se gemiddelde jaarlikse reënval 1 000 mm is en dat so ’n gebeurtenis al eeue nie plaasgevind het nie. Volgens CNN se meteoroloog Brandon Miller het die ergste van die storm reeds verby Sardinië beweeg, maar donderbuie en windstote van meer as 50 km/h sou tot Woensdag aanhou namate die stormsisteem ooswaarts oor die Middellandse See verskuif. Italië se staatsnuusagentskap ANSA het berig dat die storm, met die naam Cleopatra, wydverspreide oorstromings veroorsaak het en duisende gedwing het om skuiling in openbare fasiliteite soos gimnasiums te soek. Onder die slagoffers was ’n Brasiliaanse gesin van vier wat verdrink het toe ’n vloed hul grondvloerwoonstel in Arzachena, naby Olbia, getref het. Marco Vargiu, Olbia se raadslid vir toerisme, het gesê die ramp het die stad van ongeveer 70 000 erg getref, met 13 sterftes in die groter area. Die oorledenes sluit twee babas in, en in een geval is ’n 35-jarige pa en sy 3-jarige seun in die vloedwater oorlede. Vargiu het grootskaalse skade aan eiendom beskryf: baie huise en motors is beskadig of deur vloede weggesleep, met grondvloere onder tot twee meter water. Hy het die ongekende aard van die ramp in Olbia beklemtoon en die samehorigheid en hulp van regeringspersoneel, noodwerkers en vrywilligers geprys. Vargiu het gesê Olbia se twee hospitale was baie besig met die hantering van beserings en noodgevalle. Hy het beraam dat die regering se hulp sommige vervoerverbindinge kan herstel, maar dat dit nie genoeg sal wees vir die langtermynherstelfase nie, gegewe die groot ekonomiese impak en eiendomsverliese. Die Burgerlike Beskermingsagentskap sê 2 500 mense is ontheem en meer as 10 000 is sonder elektrisiteit. Die agentskap probeer steeds om al die geraakte gebiede te bereik. Oorstromings en grondverskuiwings het paaie versper, en amptenare het mense gemaan om net te reis indien nodig en om padtoestande voor vertrek na te gaan. Die ergste getref provinsies is Olbia en Nuoro, maar die storm het in Campidano in die suidweste van Sardinië begin voor dit oor die hele eiland versprei het. Olbia se hawe is steeds oop, terwyl die lughawe gedeeltelik operasioneel is. Die kuswag het van verdere oorstromings in ander dele van Italië berig, veral naby Catanzaro in Kalabrië en in Venesië tydens hoë gety.

article_content: The Palouse region in Eastern Washington, recognized for its vast wheat fields and distinctive farms, attracts visitors from all over the world. For nearly a decade, Los Angeles photographer Larry Gerbrandt, now 60, traveled regularly to this picturesque landscape to document its vivid beauty. Using digital techniques, Gerbrandt intensified the colors in his photographs, bringing the region’s rolling farmlands to life. He often climbed Steptoe Butte—a 3,612-foot-high landmark—to capture sweeping, elevated views of the countryside. Formed by glacial movements approximately 10,000 years ago, the Palouse changes with the seasons: green in spring and summer, turning golden during harvest, and shifting to reddish-brown as the fields are tilled. Gerbrandt’s work also highlights local heritage, featuring classic barns, vintage farming equipment, and old trucks. Through his art, he has shared the Palouse's remarkable scenery with a global audience, showcasing sun-drenched fields, colorful crops, and dramatic skies in vivid detail.
translated_content: Die Palouse-streek in Oos-Washington, bekend vir sy uitgestrekte koringland en unieke plase, lok jaarliks besoekers van regoor die wêreld. Die Los Angeles-fotograaf Larry Gerbrandt, tans 60 jaar oud, het vir bykans ’n dekade gereeld na hierdie pragtige landskap gereis om sy lewendige skoonheid af te neem. Gerbrandt het digitale tegnieke gebruik om die kleure in sy foto’s te versterk, wat die streek se golwende landerye treffend uitbeeld. Hy het dikwels Steptoe Butte, ’n 3 612 voet hoë landmerk, bestyg om wye, lugfoto’s van die omgewing te neem. Die Palouse, sowat 10 000 jaar gelede deur gletseraktiwiteit gevorm, verander elke seisoen van groen in die lente en somer, na goud tydens oestyd, en rooi-bruin wanneer lande geploeg word. Gerbrandt fokus ook op die streek se geskiedenis met beelde van ou skure, plaasimplemente en bakkies. Met sy kuns bring hy die Palouse se wonderlike natuurskoon na ’n wêreldwye gehoor, en vertoon sondeurdrenkte lande, kleurvolle oeste en dramatiese lugtonele in lewendige besonderhede.

article_content: At dawn in a small Amazonian village in Pará, Brazil, green parrots fly overhead while children play among wooden homes on white, sandy soil. This highlights a rainforest paradox: while the Amazon is renowned for its biodiversity, the soil itself has few nutrients, with most fertility held in trees and plants. When forest is cleared for cattle, soy, or villages, strong sun and rain strip nutrients quickly, leaving barren ground, sometimes called a 'wet desert' by ecologists. These poor soils make ongoing agriculture difficult, especially in one of Brazil's most impoverished regions. Often, people abandon exhausted fields and clear new forest, perpetuating deforestation that harms the global climate and countless species. Judson Ferreira Valentim, a soil scientist at Embrapa, says, 'We can't protect the rainforest without addressing Amazon poverty.' Experts argue that helping people find sustainable jobs is crucial. Solutions include making existing cleared land more productive and supporting businesses like açaí and cacao harvesting. Valentim observes that the scale of abandoned Amazon farmland is immense—larger than Portugal, per Mapbiomas. Ranching, responsible for 60-80% of deforestation, is only a third as efficient as it could be, but boosting efficiency could meet future meat demand without more clearing. Right now, 43% of Brazil's cattle are raised in the Amazon. Rachael Garrett at Cambridge University notes that laws alone are insufficient: 'You also have to give people alternatives.' The Amazon region is home to 28 million people, including Indigenous groups, settlers, and relocated families. Ignoring their needs fuels ongoing problems. To avoid intense heat, locals work early. Valentim visits families adopting techniques to get more from their land. Dairy farmer Edson Cesar de Oliveira and his family plant forage peanuts, a nitrogen-fixing legume, with their pasture grass. This natural fertilizer extends fertility, increases protein in feed, and helps cattle grow, while also reducing methane emissions. De Oliveira cannot afford chemical fertilizers, but finds his forage peanut pastures stay green longer and yield 20% more milk. The family handmakes cheese, which is always in demand locally. Some larger ranches, like that of Luiz Augusto Ribeiro do Valle, implement rotational grazing—dividing pastures into smaller plots and cycling cattle—which, with improved pasture, supports up to 40% more cattle on the same land. Most smallholders, though, face tough obstacles: bad roads, poor communications, costly supplies, and crime. Of almost a million Amazon farms, 83% are family-run with minimal resources. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has strengthened environmental enforcement, reducing deforestation by 22%. Still, experts warn that poorer farmers risk clearing more forest. Some, like Lucas dos Santos, resort to creative fencing using rooted tree branches to enable rotational grazing on a tight budget. Sustainable businesses struggle with remoteness. César De Mendes, a chocolate maker, sources cacao from untouched rainforest, noting that local conditions give each chocolate a unique taste. Projeto RECA, a collective in Rondônia, processes fruits like açaí and cacao near harvest, but transport and equipment repairs are challenging due to distance from cities. Indigenous communities like the Tembé have managed soil by burning small plots for generations. Now, due to increased fire risk and drier conditions, they are turning to planting legumes and treating fields with limestone to improve soil. Local leaders increasingly believe that better soil management and sustainable livelihoods are essential to protect the Amazon’s people and nature.

Dit beklemtoon 'n woud-paradoks: alhoewel die Amasone vir sy biodiversiteit bekend is, hou die grond min voedingstowwe—dit is meestal in die bome en plante. Sodra die woud vir bees, sojabone of woongebiede skoongemaak word, verwyder die son en reën gou die nutriënte, en laat kaal grond agter. Sommige ekoloë verwys daarna as 'n 'nat woestyn'. Die swak grond maak volhoubare boerdery moeilik, veral in een van Brasilië se armste streke. Mense verlaat dikwels uitgeputte lande en maak nuwe gedeeltes oop, wat ontbossing en klimaatsversteuring bevorder en talle spesies bedreig. Judson Ferreira Valentim, 'n grondwetenskaplike by Embrapa, sê: 'Ons kan nie die woud beskerm sonder om die armoede in die Amasone aan te spreek nie.' Kenners glo ondersteuning vir volhoubare inkomste is noodsaaklik. Oplossings sluit in om bestaande bewerkte grond meer produktief te benut en om ondernemings soos açaí- en kakaoboerdery te steun. Valentim wys daarop dat verlate grond in die Amasone groter is as Portugal (volgens Mapbiomas). Beesboerdery, verantwoordelik vir 60–80% van ontbossing, is net 'n derde so effektief soos wat dit kan wees, maar beter produktiwiteit kan die vleisbehoefte vul sonder meer ontbossing. Tans is 43% van Brasilië se beeste in die Amasone. Rachael Garrett van Cambridge sê wetstoepassing alleen is nie genoeg nie: 'Jy moet alternatiewe gee.' Ongeveer 28 miljoen mense, insluitend inheemse volke, migrante en hervestigde gesinne, woon in die streek. As hul behoeftes ongeag bly, vererger die probleme. Mense werk vroeg om die hitte te vermy. Valentim besoek families wat nuwe tegnieke probeer. Edson Cesar de Oliveira plant voerpindas, 'n stikstofbindende peulgewas, tussen die gras. Dit dien as natuurlike kunsmis, hou die veld vrugbaarder, verbeter die proteininhoud en help beeste groei, terwyl dit ook minder metaan tot gevolg het. De Oliveira kan nie chemiese kunsmis bekostig nie, maar sy voerpinda-velde bly langer groen en hul koeie gee sowat 20% meer melk. Die familie maak kaas met die hand en verkoop alles plaaslik. Op groter plase, soos by Luiz Augusto Ribeiro do Valle, voer hulle roterende weiding in—hulle deel die veld op en skuif die vee tussen seksies. Saam met verbeterde gras hou dit tot 40% meer vee op dieselfde land. Kleinboere staar steeds uitdagings in die gesig: swak paaie, kommunikasie, duur toerusting en misdaad. Van byna 'n miljoen plase is 83% gesinsboerderye met beperkte hulpbronne. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva het omgewingswette strenger toegepas en 'n 22% daling in ontbossing behaal, maar arme boere is steeds die vatbaarste vir verdere ontbossing. Party, soos Lucas dos Santos, gebruik boomtakke as heining om weidingsrotasie te kan doen teen lae koste. Volhoubare besighede sukkel met afgeleë ligging. Sjokoladevervaardiger César De Mendes kry kakao uit ongeskonde woud en sê unieke klimaats- en grondtoestande gee elke sjokolade 'n spesiale smaak. Projek RECA in Rondônia verwerk açaí en kakao naby die oesplek, maar vervoer en herstelwerk is moeilik weens die afstand van stede. Inheemse gemeenskappe soos die Tembé het tradisioneel klein stukke met vuur skoongemaak, maar weens groter brandgevaar en droër toestande, plant hulle nou peulgewasse en gebruik kalksteen om die suur grond te verbeter. Plaaslike leiers glo gekombineerde volhoubare grondbestuur en inkomste-uitbreiding is noodsaaklik om die mense én natuur van die Amasone te beskerm.

article_content: A significant oversight at Walsall Manor Hospital in the West Midlands has been revealed: 86 fetal remains were kept for up to four years, rather than being cremated within a few months as protocol dictates. The lapse, spanning cases from 2010 to late 2013, was discovered during an internal review and brought to the public's attention through a Freedom of Information request by Channel 4 Dispatches. Walsall Healthcare NHS Trust, which operates the hospital, blamed an administrative error that delayed the paperwork needed for cremation. Ordinarily, the hospital holds remains from miscarriages or abortions for one to three months before cremation. In these 86 cases, however, remains were stored much longer than intended. According to the Trust, records indicate that only five of the women involved will be contacted directly—to prevent unnecessary distress among the others. The hospital's chief executive, Richard Kirby, has publicly apologized, reaffirming their commitment to avoiding such incidents in the future. An independent review is now underway to determine exactly what went wrong. The Trust is working with the Miscarriage Association and bereavement teams to ensure patients receive appropriate communication and support. Plans are in place to cremate the 86 remains in accordance with usual procedures. Local Member of Parliament David Winnick has called for a full investigation, expressing concern over the mishandling of the remains. The hospital has also set up a hotline for anyone seeking information or support: 0345 835 7626.

Die insident, wat gevalle van 2010 tot laat 2013 insluit, is tydens ‘n interne hersiening ontdek en deur ‘n Vryheid van Inligting-versoek van Channel 4 Dispatches bekend gemaak. Walsall Healthcare NHS Trust, wat die hospitaal bestuur, het ‘n administratiewe fout as rede aangehaal vir die vertraging in die papierwerk wat vir kremasie benodig word. Die hospitaal se hoof uitvoerende beampte, Richard Kirby, het openlik om verskoning gevra en hul verbintenis herbevestig om soortgelyke foute in die toekoms te voorkom. ‘n Onafhanklike hersiening is aan die gang om vas te stel wat presies verkeerd geloop het. Die Trust werk saam met die Miskraamvereniging en berading-spanne om seker te maak pasiënte kry die nodige kommunikasie en ondersteuning. Die 86 oorskot sal nou volgens die standaardprosedure gekremmeer word. Plaaslike parlementslid David Winnick het ‘n volledige ondersoek geëis en sy bekommernis oor die hantering uitgespreek. Die hospitaal het ook ‘n hulplyn ingestel vir enigiemand wat meer inligting of ondersteuning verlang: 0345 835 7626.

article_content: British Prime Minister David Cameron visited Afghanistan on Thursday, where his itinerary was changed at the last moment due to a potential security threat, according to military sources. Cameron traveled by helicopter through Helmand province, an area considered a Taliban stronghold. British commanders adapted his travel plans based on 'the operational situation' in the region, sources said. Although security concerns prompted the changes, there was no attack and no direct threat to Cameron or his party. An unnamed British official indicated such adjustments are routine, in response to sensitive intelligence related to the prime minister's safety. Task Force Helmand spokesman James Car-Smith told CNN that such shifts are 'not unusual.' He explained, 'This is a dynamic operating environment. There are always contingency plans in place. In this case, they simply changed location and everything went according to plan.' Car-Smith stated that the visit went smoothly and was very successful. Cameron has since left Helmand, but officials would not confirm if he was returning to the UK. CNN's Barbara Starr, Thomas Evans, and Laura Perez Maestro contributed to this report.

Britse bevelvoerders het sy reisskedule aangepas op grond van 'die operasionele situasie' in die streek, sê bronne. Alhoewel veiligheidskwessies die veranderinge veroorsaak het, was daar geen aanval of direkte bedreiging aan Cameron of sy party nie. article_content: Sen. Mary Landrieu of Louisiana has reimbursed the federal government $33,727 after her campaign admitted to over 12 years of mistakenly taxpayer-funded travel expenses. The repayments, announced Friday, cover chartered flights that were wrongly charged to her Senate office, an issue traced back to 2002 because of what Landrieu described as 'sloppy bookkeeping.' Following an internal audit ordered by Landrieu, her office discovered the errors and implemented a new travel expense system already in use by other Senate offices to prevent future mistakes. Landrieu publicly accepted full responsibility, stating, 'They should have never happened, and I apologize for this.' The issue first received attention in August when CNN revealed Landrieu used government funds for a flight to a campaign fundraiser in November. Her team explained that the charter company had billed her Senate office instead of her campaign, and the mistake had since been corrected. After further media inquiries, Landrieu also refunded $5,700 for another charter flight. The total reimbursed amount represents about 11% of her office's travel costs since 2002. Marc Elias, Landrieu’s attorney, informed the Senate Ethics Committee that future travel will be pre-approved by counsel. Rep. Bill Cassidy, Landrieu’s Republican challenger, criticized her for disclosing records only from 2002 onwards and pressed for the release of nearly 18 years' worth of travel documents. Cassidy contended that earlier rules also prohibited such expenses and questioned whether problems pre-dated 2002. USA Today previously named Landrieu as one of the Senate's most frequent flyers after she billed over $47,000 in chartered flights in 2013 alone.

article_content: Martin Jacobson, a 27-year-old from Sweden who previously trained as a chef, triumphed in the World Series of Poker main event held in Las Vegas, taking home the $10 million top prize. He secured his win with three tens, defeating Norwegian Felix Stephensen’s pair of nines. Amid confetti and applause, Jacobson’s friends and family gathered to celebrate his victory. Jacobson commented, 'There's no such thing as a perfect tournament, but this was almost perfect.' According to his mother Eva, Jacobson first picked up poker after long restaurant shifts, playing to pass the time since his friends were unavailable. While Jacobson had already earned over $1 million in past WSOP events, this was his first main event win. Jacobson displayed remarkable composure during two days of skillful play, choosing to openly face his opponents without wearing sunglasses or hats, unlike many players. His previous main event attempts ended quickly, a lesson his mother said taught him resilience in the competitive tournament. Felix Stephensen, age 24, finished second with $5.1 million, while Dutch player Jorryt van Hoof came in third, securing $3.8 million after a tense final showdown. Notably, for the first time ever, the final three main event players were all European and none were American. All three currently reside in London. Van Hoof, a pro player and coach from the Netherlands, entered the final night with a chip lead but was eliminated after losing to Jacobson’s hand. He received backing from a team who provided tactical support by analyzing live game data during the event. Despite narrowly missing out on victory, Stephensen expressed gratitude for his success, while van Hoof remained upbeat, joking that the winner would buy dinner for the group. The trio outplayed six other finalists in 12 hours of play, followed by a decisive match the next evening. This year’s World Series of Poker main event drew approximately 6,700 participants, each paying the $10,000 entry fee, reinforcing its status as one of the most prestigious and watched poker tournaments in the world.

article_content: Olumide Ogunade, popularly known as ID Cabasa, a renowned music producer and singer, has stated that he discourages drug abuse among artists he collaborates with. In an interview with Sunday Scoop, he emphasized that he avoids judging artists due to his own imperfections.  "We create an environment that does not support or encourage drug abuse," he explained. "I encourage the artists I work with to be in the right state of mind so we can connect more effectively, rather than arriving under the influence."  The Gongo Aso producer further pointed out that many entertainers rarely talk about their struggles with depression due to ego. He noted that societal pressure contributes to the increasing rates of depression, mainly because individuals attempt to hide or camouflage their insecurities.  He suggested that society should promote the idea of individual journeys rather than foster unhealthy competition and comparison. "Expectations need to be managed. We should encourage the idea of everyone having their own journey, which helps people progress without constantly comparing themselves to others. Collaboration and connection should replace unnecessary and negative competition."  ID Cabasa also urged parents to pay close attention to their children, to truly listen in order to understand, not simply to reply.  Offering his thoughts to young artists, Ogunade advised, "Let us keep learning, because the industry is always changing. We should learn about the business of music and about life. Proper education and continuous learning will open up many opportunities for us."

"Ons skep 'n omgewing wat nie dwelmmisbruik ondersteun of aanmoedig nie," het hy verduidelik. "Ek moedig kunstenaars aan om nugter te wees sodat ons beter kan konnekteer, eerder as om onder die invloed te werk."  Die Gongo Aso-vervaardiger het verder uitgelig dat baie kunstenaars selde oor hul stryd met depressie praat as gevolg van ego. Hy het genoem dat samelewingsdruk bydra tot die groeiende vlakke van depressie, hoofsaaklik omdat mense hul onsekerhede probeer wegsteek of kamoefleer.  Hy het voorgestel dat die samelewing die konsep van individuele journeys eerder as ongewenste kompetisie en vergelyking moet bevorder. "Verwagtinge moet bestuur word. Ons moet die idee aanmoedig dat almal hul eie reis het, wat mense help om vorentoe te beweeg sonder om hulself aan ander te meet. Samewerking en verbintenis moet onnodige en negatiewe kompetisie vervang."  ID Cabasa het ook ouers aangemoedig om aandagtig na hul kinders te luister, nie net om te reageer nie, maar om werklik te verstaan.  Aan jong kunstenaars het Ogunade die volgende raad gegee: "Kom ons hou aan leer, want die bedryf verander voortdurend. Ons moet die besigheid van musiek en die lewe self bestudeer. Deeglike opvoeding en voortdurende leer sal baie geleenthede vir ons ontsluit."

article_content: NEW DELHI: Women are the backbone of Parliament and India's economic development, Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar said Thursday, emphasizing that their participation in legislatures advances policy and helps solve significant challenges. "Giving justice to your gender is automatic justice to my gender," he stated while inviting students from Delhi University's Miranda House College to observe the Winter session of Parliament. As chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Dhankhar delivered an address on the 'Role of Women in Indian Parliament' to mark Miranda House College's platinum jubilee. He highlighted that women's roles in Parliament are enormous and that their presence enhances the environment of legislatures. On women's representation, Dhankhar noted that soon a minimum of one-third of seats in both the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies will be reserved for women. He pointed out that India made history on September 21 when the women's reservation bill—now law—was passed in the new Parliament building, calling it an 'epochal development' to ensure Bharat 2047 reaches its peak. "A special session of Parliament on September 21 in the new building marked history as the women's reservation bill was passed. Coincidentally, the day aligned with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's birthday on the Hindu calendar," Dhankhar said. "Women are the backbone of Parliament and our economic progress. Without their involvement, the nation cannot thrive," he added. Dhankhar also invited five Miranda House interns for a 15-day course on parliamentary procedures and praised Miranda House for its seven-year streak as the top-ranked institution in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF). Delhi University's vice-chancellor Yogesh Singh and Dean of Colleges Balaram Pani were present at the event.

"Om geregtigheid aan julle geslag te gee, is outomaties geregtigheid aan my geslag," het hy gesê terwyl hy studente van Delhi Universiteit se Miranda House College uitgenooi het om die Wintersessie van die Parlement by te woon. As voorsitter van die Rajya Sabha het Dhankhar 'n toespraak gelewer oor die 'Rol van Vroue in die Indiese Parlement' tydens Miranda House College se platinumjubileum. Hy het beklemtoon dat die rol van vroue in die Parlement enorm is en dat hul teenwoordigheid die atmosfeer in wetgewers opkikker. Wat vroueverteenwoordiging betref, het Dhankhar genoem dat daar binnekort 'n minimum van een-derde van die setels in sowel die Lok Sabha as die staatswetgewende vergaderings vir vroue gereserveer sal word. Hy het uitgelig dat Indië geskiedenis gemaak het op 21 September toe die vrouereserveringswetsontwerp, wat nou wet is, in die nuwe parlementgebou aanvaar is, en dit 'n 'epogmakende ontwikkeling' genoem om te verseker dat Bharat 2047 sy volle potensiaal bereik. "’n Spesiale parlementsitting op 21 September in die nuwe gebou was histories, toe die vrouereserveringswetsontwerp aanvaar is. Die dag het toevallig saamgeval met Eerste Minister Narendra Modi se verjaarsdag volgens die Hindoe-kalender," het Dhankhar gesê. "Vroue is die ruggraat van die Parlement en van ons ekonomiese vooruitgang. Sonder hul deelname kan die land nie floreer nie," het hy bygevoeg. article_content: Washington (CNN) -- Warren Buffett is highly confident that Hillary Clinton will win the 2016 U.S. presidential election, even declaring his willingness to bet some of his $58.2 billion net worth on her victory. At Fortune's Most Powerful Women Summit, Buffett, an outspoken supporter of Clinton, stated, "Hillary is going to win, yeah. I will bet money on it. And I don't do that easily." Although Clinton has said she is considering a presidential run, she has not formally announced her candidacy. Buffett suggested that her entry into the race is almost certain, remarking, "Hillary is going to run," and added, "she is going to announce as late as possible." Buffett praised Clinton's qualifications in an interview with CNN's Poppy Harlow, saying, "I don't see how you could have anybody better qualified. I like what she believes in... I think she's extraordinarily able and energetic in pushing those beliefs." Buffett has backed Clinton for years, including a $2,000 contribution to her 2000 Senate campaign. During the 2008 Democratic primary, he supported both Clinton and then-Senator Barack Obama. At the Fortune event, Buffett expressed uncertainty about the Republican field, saying, "I don't know. Her opponent will be whoever wins the Republican primary and there are going to be a lot of people who want to do it."

article_content: Talks to reach a settlement in a long-running case brought by 184 Nairobi-based Facebook moderators against Meta have collapsed. The moderators, who filtered violent and graphic content, allege they were laid off for organizing a union. They were made redundant by Sama, a local subcontractor, which has previously told the BBC it does not oppose unionization. The moderators are suing Meta, Sama, and another outsourcing firm, Majorel. Meta uses artificial intelligence and human moderators to identify and remove problematic Facebook content. Several moderators have shared how traumatic the material was, with reports of being paid around $630 (£515) per month, according to Sama. One moderator described to the BBC the distress of seeing a video where a man took his own life in the presence of a child. Sama maintains it paid competitive local salaries and offered mental health support. In August, Sama CEO Wendy Gonzalez told the BBC the company had no objection to unionization, stating it was 'not a concern.' Altogether, 260 moderators lost their jobs when Sama ended its contract with Meta. The 184 moderators bringing the legal action allege they were dismissed in retaliation for complaints about working conditions and efforts to form a union. Their demands include that Meta acknowledge moderators' right to unionize and speak about working conditions. Moderators also claim they were unfairly denied jobs at Majorel, which was set to take over moderation work in Africa after Sama's exit. However, on Monday it was revealed that Meta's work with Majorel will not proceed. A court order barred Meta from starting new content moderation contracts in Kenya while the lawsuit is ongoing. Meta told the BBC: 'We remain committed to Africa, and our content review in local languages. We're looking at options with continental partners to keep people safe on our platforms.' Majorel said it had begun a potential redundancy process for about 200 Nairobi employees, but remained committed to Kenya as a digital outsourcing hub. In August, parties were directed to attempt mediation, which has now failed. The legal case will continue, with the judge urging 'serious engagement' before the next hearing on 31 October. Lawyers for the moderators accused Meta of not engaging seriously. 'If they are willing to seriously engage, we are open to it,' lawyer Mercy Mutemi said. Martha Dark of Foxglove, which supports the litigation, said Meta's delays forced a return to court. Meta's lawyer claimed progress had been made. Sama said it was 'disappointed' mediation failed, but had separately resolved issues with about 60 moderators. Meta faces other cases in Kenya. In February, a court ruled Meta could be sued by ex-moderator Daniel Motaung for alleged poor conditions. In Nairobi, Meta also faces litigation over its algorithm purportedly fueling viral hate and violence during Ethiopia's civil war.

Sama het gesê hulle is 'teleurgesteld' dat bemiddeling misluk het, maar het apart met sowat 60 moderators geskik. Meta staar verdere regsgedinge in Kenia in die gesig. In Februarie het 'n hof beslis Meta kan vervolg word deur die voormalige moderator Daniel Motaung oor bewerings van swak werksomstandighede. article_content: On Friday afternoon, Japan’s Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant suffered a temporary power failure that affected its cooling system. The Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO) confirmed operations were restored after a few hours. This marks the latest in a series of electrical outages at the site as it continues to undergo extensive post-disaster repairs following the devastating earthquake and tsunami in March 2011. A similar outage occurred last month when rats caused a short circuit by entering a switchboard—an incident reported by Kyodo News. Thankfully, neither event resulted in known radioactive leaks. In response, TEPCO announced the installation of metal panels surrounding vulnerable equipment to keep wildlife out. The 2011 tsunami struck the Fukushima Daiichi plant, disabling essential systems and triggering meltdowns in three reactors. The disaster became the world’s worst nuclear accident since Chernobyl, releasing considerable radioactive material into the environment. TEPCO continues to monitor radiation levels around the area to ensure safety.

Dit is die jongste in 'n reeks elektriese onderbrekings by die aanleg, wat steeds grootskaalse herstelwerk ondergaan ná die verwoestende aardbewing en tsoenami in Maart 2011. ‘n Soortgelyke onderbreking het verlede maand gebeur toe rotte ‘n kortsluiting veroorsaak het deur in ‘n skakelkombuis te klim—soos deur Kyodo Nuus berig. Gelukkig was daar in geen van die twee gevalle enige bekende vrystelling van radioaktiewe materiaal nie. TEPCO het gesê hulle is besig om metaalplate om kwesbare toerusting te plaas om diere buite te hou. Die tsoenami van 2011 het die Fukushima Daiichi-aanleg ernstig geraak en belangrike stelsels uitgeslaan, wat smeltings in drie reaktore veroorsaak het. article_content: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has confirmed that he will attend European Union-hosted talks in Granada, Spain, despite reports that Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev will not take part. This announcement was made on Wednesday, a day before the scheduled summit, which was expected to bring together the leaders of Armenia and Azerbaijan, as well as those of France, Germany, and EU Council President Charles Michel. Pashinyan addressed the Armenian parliament, stating, 'We have not cancelled the trip. We are going,' and expressing disappointment that the meeting with Aliyev would not occur. He added, 'We were in a constructive and optimistic mood, because we thought that a turning point document could be signed.' European leaders hoped the talks could help ease tensions following Azerbaijan's recent move to retake the breakaway Nagorno-Karabakh region, which had been controlled by ethnic Armenian forces until last month. Since then, tens of thousands of Armenians have fled to neighboring Armenia. On Wednesday, AFP reported that Aliyev had decided not to attend, citing an 'anti-Azerbaijani atmosphere,' including pro-Armenian statements by French officials and the possible sale of French arms to Armenia. The report, quoting an Azerbaijani official, also said that remarks made by EU Council President Charles Michel contributed to Aliyev's decision. During a visit to Yerevan on Tuesday, French Foreign Minister Catherine Colonna said France had agreed to deliver military equipment to Armenia, without giving specific details. Colonna later told the French parliament that France does not seek to escalate conflict in the region but defended the arms as defensive. 'Azerbaijan has never stopped arming itself to carry out offensive actions,' Colonna said. Azerbaijan’s state news agency, APA, said Azerbaijan will not participate in talks that include France, but is open to possible three-way discussions with Armenia and the EU. The agency also reported that Aliyev preferred Turkey to be present at the summit, but this suggestion was declined by France and Germany. An Azerbaijani official told AFP, 'Azerbaijan did not consider it necessary to participate in negotiations in this format.'

article_content: With Thanksgiving approaching, the United States is expected to see over 55 million travelers, boosting the travel industry, according to AAA. Paula Twidale, Senior Vice President of AAA Travel, mentioned that a high number of people are anticipated to reunite with family and loved ones. Each year, travel in the US continues to recover and grow stronger. Compared to 2022, this year's airports, roads, and seaports are projected to be even busier. AAA forecasts that most people will travel by car, which could lead to lower travel costs compared to last year. The busiest travel days will be November 21 and 22, especially for air travelers, who may face higher prices. After the Thanksgiving holiday, on November 26 and 27, airports are expected to see large crowds as travelers return home. Travel expert Laura Lindsay from Skyscanner predicts that cities such as New York, Las Vegas, Orlando, and Miami will be popular destinations, leading to busy airports like Los Angeles International and John F. Kennedy International. Connecting airports including Dallas Fort Worth and Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta will also see heavy traffic. Bob Pishue, transportation analyst at INRIX, advises travelers to plan accordingly. The day before Thanksgiving is typically the most congested on the roads. On Thanksgiving Day, roads will be busiest between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m.; travelers should start their trips before 10 a.m. or after 5 p.m. On Friday, road trips should be avoided between noon and 4 p.m. Major cities, including Atlanta, Boston, Los Angeles, New York, San Francisco, and Washington, are expected to experience significant delays. Thanksgiving Day will be celebrated on Thursday, November 23, 2023. It is a major family holiday in the United States dedicated to giving thanks. article_content: A mother was forced to watch in horror as her two young sons died in a trailer fire, desperately trying to break down a locked door. The door’s deadbolt locked after closing on Monday, trapping Kayden Green (4), Damion Green (1), and their sister Amiyah Green (3) inside, according to Twin Falls police. The children were inside their home at the High Desert RV Park while their mother, Heather Green, was outside, authorities said. Family members recounted that Heather and one of her sons had been playing near the trailer door before it accidentally locked. Creekside Court RV Park manager Gina Johnson told Magic Valley that Heather called for her daughter to help unlock the door. High Desert RV Park manager, Gary, smashed a window to help rescue Amiyah, sustaining injuries in the process. Heather Green burned her hands trying to get her children out. Twin Falls police reported the fire was caused by a space heater next to household items. Despite her efforts, Heather could only reassure her sons through the window until she heard them no more. Amiyah was rescued from the trailer, while Kayden and Damion’s deaths were pronounced at the hospital after their extraction. Twin Falls police confirmed the cause as an accident related to the heater. The Times-News identified the surviving girl as Amiyah Green. Officials noted that the children’s father, Christopher Green, is currently incarcerated.

article_content: Maxime Lucu will start at scrumhalf for France, stepping in for Antoine Dupont as head coach Fabien Galthie maintains his main lineup for France’s final Rugby World Cup Pool A game—a knockout-style clash against Italy on Friday. Lucu will partner with his Bordeaux-Begles teammate, flyhalf Matthieu Jalibert, as Les Bleus aim to finish top of their group and secure a potential quarter-final match-up against defending champions South Africa, who are expected to finish second in Pool B behind Ireland. If France loses without earning two bonus points, they will be eliminated and Italy will advance. France is aware that Italy will look different from the team that was beaten 86-17 by New Zealand last week. "They're a Latin team and they're wounded. That's when things get dangerous. We have to be very careful because they will have nothing to lose," Galthie told reporters on Wednesday, adding that France has entered the tournament's "knockout phase." He recalled, "We played them in Rome last year in the Six Nations and it was a very tough test," referencing France’s narrow 29-24 victory. Flanker Charles Ollivon echoed this sentiment: "We expect Italy to be completely different than against New Zealand. We reviewed our match against them in the Six Nations, rather than overfocusing on their loss to New Zealand. It will be very physical in the first 20 minutes, and they won’t miss as many tackles as against the All Blacks." Dupont is unavailable after fracturing his cheekbone in France’s 96-0 win over Namibia. The 26-year-old has returned to the squad and resumed light training, awaiting medical clearance to play again. The only other change from the Namibia fixture is the return of Gregory Alldritt, who takes back the number eight shirt after recovering from a minor knee injury. He joins captain Ollivon and Anthony Jelonch in the back row, with Jelonch preferred over Francois Cros. As expected, Lucu starts at scrumhalf while Baptiste Couilloud is listed among the replacements. "Max and Matthieu complement each other. Technically, Max is excellent—he has never disappointed, and his kicking game is outstanding," praised Galthie. Italy has not defeated France in the last ten years. France lineup: 15-Thomas Ramos, 14-Damian Penaud, 13-Gael Fickou, 12-Jonathan Danty, 11-Louis Bielle-Biarrey, 10-Matthieu Jalibert, 9-Maxime Lucu, 7-Charles Ollivon, 8-Gregory Alldritt, 6-Anthony Jelonch, 5-Thibaud Flament, 4-Cameron Woki, 3-Uini Atonio, 2-Peato Mauvaka, 1-Cyril Baille. article_content:
Would you rather have just $1 to spend, or walk away with $1.49 billion? For three lucky winners across the country, all it took was a single dollar to cash in on Friday’s historic Mega Millions jackpot. By matching the winning numbers — 2, 4, 23, 38, 46, with a Mega Ball of 23 — they each claimed an equal share of $656 million, about $218 million apiece before taxes, if they choose the annuity option.

Since the game’s last major winner in late January, eager players spent a staggering $1,491,082,267 on tickets. For most, those dollars resulted in little more than hope, as only a few scored smaller payouts. As one Twitter user joked, “Oh Mega Millions, why do you shun me?”—echoing the disappointment felt nationwide as people realized they hadn’t struck it rich. Another quipped, “Dear news updates on my phone, stop rubbing it in that I didn’t win the Mega Millions!”

On Friday alone, nearly as much was spent on tickets as was ultimately awarded in prizes. Kelly Cripe, spokesperson for the Texas state lottery (which currently oversees the Mega Millions), reported that sales in all 42 states, the District of Columbia, and the Virgin Islands totaled $651,915,940 for the day. 

Lotteries have long been popular in the U.S., but the frenzy ahead of this drawing was unprecedented. People lined up at convenience stores, dreaming about what they’d do if luck struck — quitting jobs, buying new homes, and changing their lives overnight.

The major jackpot generated a windfall for state governments and for store owners. At Manhattan Tobacco in New York City, cashier Alex Shanahe said sales tripled before the drawing. “Everybody wants to win the Mega Millions,” Shanahe said.

Against the approximately 176 million-to-one odds, only three tickets hit the jackpot. One was purchased around 7:15 p.m. Friday at a 7-Eleven in Baltimore, Maryland, where a customer’s $1 ‘quick pick’ matched the winning numbers pulled just hours later. The identity of this winner may remain a mystery — Maryland does not require lottery winners to go public, according to state Lottery Director Stephen Martino. Kansas offers similar anonymity; Director Dennis Wilson said he’s not even received details on the winning ticket, except that it was sold somewhere in the state’s northeast. 

Meanwhile, the town of Red Bud, Illinois, about 35 miles south of St. Louis, is abuzz with news that one of its residents bought the third winning ticket at a local Moto Mart. “We’re having a great time,” store manager Denise Metzger told CNN affiliate WGN. “Everyone’s speculating and having fun. The whole atmosphere is sensational.”

So far, none of the three grand-prize winners has come forward. Kansas Lottery Director Wilson has some advice: sign the back of the ticket, keep it somewhere safe, and consult a lawyer—because life is about to change in a big way.

In addition to the jackpot victors, at least 42 players matched five of six numbers: 29 in California, 12 in Illinois, and one in Kansas. California Lottery spokesman Alex Traverso said those prizes will be about $125,000 to $130,000 each — tiny compared to the jackpot itself.

Psychologist Scott Bea cautioned that sudden fortune may not guarantee happiness, particularly for people who’ve struggled with money before. “It solves one problem, but it creates a half-billion others,” he said. “You basically have no chance of winning this, but it really gets people excited.”

Die atmosfeer is ongelooflik.”

Benewens dié drie, het minstens 42 ander spelers vyf uit ses nommers ooreenstem—29 in Kalifornië, 12 in Illinois en een in Kansas. Die Kalifornië-lotery se Alex Traverso sê daardie pryse gaan sowat $125,000 tot $130,000 wees—nie veel in vergelyking met die grootpot nie.

article_content: Thanksgiving is traditionally the busiest travel time in the U.S., with millions planning trips during the extended weekend. For those looking for something different this year, a range of entertaining and tasty alternatives await—no need for international travel. Just remember, many of these events sell out quickly, so consider booking ahead! Discover the roots of Thanksgiving in Plymouth, Massachusetts, where the 1620 landing of the Mayflower marked the holiday’s beginning. Tour the Mayflower II replica, view early colonial artifacts at Pilgrim Hall Museum, and enjoy festive reenactments and processions. The family-friendly John Carver Inn & Spa offers cozy lodgings, while Plimoth Plantation presents traditional holiday feasts, complete with historic recipes. Philadelphia is home to the nation's oldest Thanksgiving parade, the 6abc Dunkin Donuts Parade. Since 1920, locals and visitors have enjoyed floats, giant balloons, and live entertainment downtown. Stay at Embassy Suites for easy access to the excitement, and dine on a historic sailing ship at Moshulu restaurant on the Delaware River. Food and wine lovers will delight in Sonoma County, California, with its renowned vineyards and restaurants set amidst beautiful landscapes. The charming Farmhouse Inn makes a lovely base, and Dry Creek Kitchen’s Thanksgiving menu features seasonal, locally sourced specialties. If shopping is your sport, New York City’s iconic department stores are ready for holiday hunters. The Iroquois Hotel’s Black Friday perks—like hot drinks and shipping credits—make marathon shopping easier. Afterward, celebrate Thanksgiving and Hanukkah at Katz’s Deli, enjoying a menu rich with Jewish and American classics. Prefer getting active? Experience a memorable holiday dinner at the romantic La Caille restaurant, reminiscent of a French estate. article_content: Amazon.com Inc. founder Jeff Bezos announced he is moving from the Seattle area to Miami, to be closer to his parents and Blue Origin LLC’s Cape Canaveral operations. Bezos—the world’s third-richest person, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index—shared the news Thursday on Instagram, posting a video from the Seattle garage where he started Amazon in 1994. "I’ve lived in Seattle longer than anywhere else and have so many great memories here," Bezos said. "As exciting as this move is, it’s an emotional decision for me. Seattle, you’ll always have a place in my heart." Amazon has been a key force in transforming Seattle into a technology center and is the city’s largest private employer. Bezos stepped down as Amazon CEO in 2021, becoming executive chairman; Andy Jassy succeeded him as CEO. Recently, Bezos bought a seven-bedroom mansion in Indian Creek, a man-made island in the Miami area nicknamed the “Billionaire Bunker.” He also owns residences in Washington, DC; New York City; Los Angeles; Maui; and a 300,000-acre ranch in Texas, which houses Blue Origin’s New Shepard rocket launch site. Miami has become popular with prominent entrepreneurs and wealthy individuals. Hedge fund managers Ken Griffin, Dan Loeb, and Josh Harris have acquired waterfront mansions in Miami Beach since the pandemic. Soccer star Lionel Messi also recently bought an oceanside home in South Florida after joining Inter Miami of Major League Soccer. Earlier this year, Griffin moved his fund’s global headquarters from Chicago to Miami, highlighting a growing trend of companies and wealthy newcomers relocating to the area.

Seattle, jy sal altyd ’n plek in my hart hê." Amazon het ’n sleutelrol gespeel om Seattle in ’n tegnologie-sentrum te omskep en is die stad se grootste private werkgewer. Bezos het in 2021 as Amazon se HUB afgetree en uitvoerende voorsitter geword; Andy Jassy het as HUB oorgeneem. Bezos het onlangs ’n sewe-slaapkamer huis in Indian Creek gekoop, ’n kunsmatige eiland in die Miami-omgewing wat as die “Billionaire Bunker” bekend staan. Hy besit ook huise in Washington, DC; New York Stad; Los Angeles; Maui; en ’n 300,000-akker plaas in Texas waar Blue Origin se New Shepard-vuurpyl gelanseer word. Miami het die laaste paar jaar baie gewild geraak onder bekende entrepreneurs en welgestelde individue. Fondsbestuurders Ken Griffin, Dan Loeb en Josh Harris het waterkantmansions in Miami Beach aangeskaf sedert die pandemie. Sokkerster Lionel Messi het ook onlangs ’n seehuis in Suid-Florida gekoop nadat hy by Inter Miami van Major League Soccer aangesluit het. Griffin het vroeër vanjaar sy fonds se wêreldwye hoofkantoor van Chicago na Miami verskuif, en illustreer so die toenemende verskuiwing van maatskappye en ryk nuwelinge na die gebied.

article_content: AI regulation may still be pending, but scammers are rapidly leveraging artificial intelligence to target India's vast internet user base. Indians now spend about 105 minutes per week checking whether messages they receive via text, email, or social media are authentic. A study by McAfee reports that 82% of Indians have clicked on or become victims of fake messages. The most common scams involve fake job offers (64%) and bogus bank alerts (52%). AI is enabling cybercriminals to greatly increase the scale and sophistication of scams. A new phishing website is created every 11 seconds, highlighting growing dangers for India's roughly 900 million internet users. According to McAfee, there is an urgent need for advanced AI-powered solutions to stay ahead of scammers using AI. The study indicates that Indians receive almost 12 scam messages daily through emails, texts, or social media platforms. On average, they spend 1.8 hours each week attempting to verify whether these messages are legitimate. Nearly half of respondents (49%) say scam messages rarely have typos or obvious errors, making them harder to detect. Roma Majumder, SVP of Product at McAfee, stated: "Most Indian consumers would rather have a root canal than receive scam messages year-round. The increasing speed, volume, and sophistication of AI-powered scams makes it incredibly hard to tell if a delivery text or bank alert is real. So much so that 73% of Indians feel they have a better chance at solving a Rubik’s Cube than recognizing a scam message." Spotting scams now takes up more than two full work weeks annually for users. Around 90% report getting fake messages daily via email or text, and 84% encounter them on social media as well. Common scam approaches include prize notifications (72%), fake job offers (64%), fraudulent bank alerts (52%), notifications about unauthorized purchases (37%), phony subscription updates (35%), fake delivery problem notifications (29%), and bogus Amazon security or account alerts (27%). The survey, which involved over 7,000 adults across seven countries including India, was conducted to gauge the impact of more sophisticated, AI-driven scam messages on global consumers. Findings show rising levels of stress and highlight the pressing need for robust, AI-based defenses to fight evolving online scams.

Die bevindings wys verhoogde stresvlakke en beklemtoon die dringende behoefte aan robuuste, KI-gedrewe verdediging teen hierdie nuwe generasie aanlynbedrog.

article_content: Following significant public opposition, the Fashion Meets Music Festival (FMMF) in Columbus, Ohio, has canceled R. Kelly's planned appearance. The decision came after local residents voiced their concerns on social media, arguing that the artist's reputation did not reflect the community's values. Melissa Dickson, the festival's communications director, noted that the event aims to showcase Columbus's vibrant fashion and music scenes, and that organizers wanted to ensure the festival embodied local pride. R. Kelly, best known for 'I Believe I Can Fly,' said he was sorry to disappoint his fans and hoped to perform for them in the future. The singer's participation had sparked debate due to his past legal issues, including being acquitted of child pornography charges in 2008. These controversies came back into focus after recent extensive media coverage surrounding R. Kelly. While some festivalgoers expressed disappointment and sought ticket refunds, many others supported the festival's move. The event continues as planned with acts like O.A.R., Michelle Williams, Cold War Kids, and Rusko.

article_content: Situated along Peru's northern coast, Máncora has transformed from a tranquil fishing port into a hotspot for surfers and those completing the Inca Trail. The town's affordability is highlighted by oceanfront lodgings starting at $40 per night. Travelers can reach Máncora by flying Lan Peru from Lima to Piura (about $225 for a round trip), then taking a two-hour taxi ride costing about $70. Alternatively, there’s an 18-hour Cruz del Sur bus ride for $37 that offers scenic views and the possibility of dolphin sightings. Máncora’s accommodations cater to relaxed budgets, from sea-facing inns like Punta Ballenas to Hospedaje Costa Norte, a short stroll from the beach. The latter is known for its pet parrot Pedro, famous for giving 'kisses' to women guests. Prices can be as low as $10. Samana Chakra, a yoga-centric, thatched-bungalow resort at the north end of the beach, is operated by a former Californian marketing executive and his Peruvian yoga instructor wife. At $70 per night, guests enjoy breakfast, open yoga sessions, and the chance to surf at sunrise with the owners. Getting around town is quick and inexpensive, with moto-taxi rides costing under a dollar. For about $14 round trip, visitors can reach Poza de Barro’s hot springs in the Amotape Mountains. Surf schools offering private 90-minute lessons at around $16 attract both newbies and experienced surfers, especially with Máncora’s celebrated waves. Food is both flavorful and reasonably priced: a meal of ceviche and a cold Brahma beer costs less than $6 at Las Peñitas, while fruit-flavored cremoladas from Papa Mo’s Milk Bar are just 50 cents. Craft markets feature unique jewelry made with orange huayruro seeds from the Amazon, thought to bring good luck, available on a three-block area at the town’s south end for $7 per necklace. Travelers are advised to confirm current prices and details with each establishment when planning a visit.

article_content: Millie Mackintosh turned heads at the Harper's Bazaar Women Of The Year Awards in London, showcasing radiant skin and a striking smokey eye look. The 25-year-old, a former reality TV star and trained make-up artist, appeared flawless in a dazzling Julien Macdonald dress. FEMAIL spoke with Millie's current favorite make-up artist, Nikki Wolff, who revealed the secrets behind Millie's elegant appearance for the event. The two met through mutual friend Zara Martin and have worked together since. Nikki, also known for her work with Jessica Ennis and Amanda Holden, aimed for a fresh, natural style to complement Millie's dress. Nikki credits Millie's healthy lifestyle—her commitment to good nutrition and exercise—for her glowing complexion. To enhance Millie's natural beauty, Nikki prepped her skin with a Sisley face mask for hydration, then applied Illamasqua skin base for a smooth, natural finish. Cream blusher was used for a radiant glow and highlighter was added without bronzer, as Millie's recent holiday had left her skin luminous. For her lips, Nikki used a chunky peach-toned lip liner blended across the lips with a touch of balm to create a natural look. She often prefers using lip liner as a lipstick base for longer-lasting color. Millie's eyes were defined with soft brown kohl and lashes from Millie's own beauty range. At the event, Millie was accompanied by her husband, Professor Green (Stephen), who was clearly enamored with her look. Millie explains that she organizes her make-up so as not to inconvenience Stephen, keeping it neatly arranged in pull-out drawers under their bed. Looking to the future, Millie is considering launching a beauty range that combines both make-up and skincare, citing her interest in innovative beauty products but noting her current busy schedule.

article_content: Erica Ruiz, a 21-year-old American-born daughter of Mexican farm workers, is preparing to graduate with a psychology degree and hopes to continue on to graduate school. Motivated by her parents, who were unable to pursue higher education themselves, she and her brothers have been encouraged to pursue academic success. Ruiz's academic journey reflects a broader trend: a significant surge in Hispanic college enrollment across the United States. The Pew Hispanic Center's latest study reports that in 2010, there were 1.8 million Hispanic college students aged 18 to 24—a number that for the first time exceeded African American students in that age group, who numbered 1.7 million. However, when factoring in all ages, more Black students are enrolled than Hispanics. Data derived from the U.S. Census Bureau indicates Hispanic college enrollment jumped by 24% compared to the previous year. While college enrollment also rose among Black and Asian students, the increase was most pronounced among Hispanics. Over the same timeframe, White students' enrollment fell to 7.7 million, but they remain the largest demographic in higher education. Pew Hispanic Center researcher Richard Fry connects the Hispanic enrollment upswing to both overall population growth and more students graduating from high school. He believes raising educational levels for young Hispanics will not only benefit their community but also contribute positively to the U.S. workforce. Raul Gonzalez, legislative director of the National Council of La Raza, a Latino advocacy organization, cautions that this sharp increase may not necessarily signal a continuing trend but expresses hope that it does. He credits some educational progress to the federal No Child Left Behind law, observing that the surge in enrollment comes as its policies have shaped a generation of students. The report also uncovered a 4% drop in young White college enrollment since 2009—the steepest decrease since at least 1993—due in part to a shrinking population in that age group. Ruiz considers her pursuit of higher education central to her American dream and urges her brothers to seize similar opportunities.

Ruiz se akademiese pad weerspieël 'n groter neiging: 'n merkbare toename in Spaanse kollege-inskrywings regoor die VSA. Volgens die nuutste studie van die Pew Hispanic Center was daar in 2010 1,8 miljoen Spaanse kollege-studente tussen 18 en 24 jaar oud – meer as Afrika-Amerikaanse studente in dieselfde ouderdomsgroep, wat 1,7 miljoen beloop het. Wanneer alle ouderdomsgroepe egter in ag geneem word, is daar steeds meer Swart studente as Spanjaarde ingeskryf. Data van die Amerikaanse Sensusburo dui aan dat Spaanse kollege-inskrywings met 24% toegeneem het vergeleke met die vorige jaar. Al het inskrywings onder Swart en Asiatiese studente ook gestyg, was die toename onder Spanjaarde die sterkste. In dieselfde tydperk het wit studente se inskrywing tot 7,7 miljoen gedaal, maar hulle bly steeds die grootste groep in hoër onderwys. Richard Fry, ’n navorser by die Pew Hispanic Center, verbind die toename in Spaanse inskrywings met algehele bevolkingsgroei en ’n hoër persentasie matrikulante. Hy glo verbeterde onderwys vir jong Spanjaarde sal nie net hul gemeenskap bevoordeel nie, maar ook 'n positiewe bydrae tot die Amerikaanse arbeidsmag maak. Raul Gonzalez, wetgewende direkteur van die National Council of La Raza—'n Latino-belangegroep—waarsku dat hierdie styging nie noodwendig 'n volhoubare tendens aandui nie, maar bly hoopvol dat dit wel kan wees. Hy skryf sommige vordering toe aan die federale No Child Left Behind-wet en wys daarop dat die toename in inskrywings gebeur het net nadat dié beleid 'n generasie studente beïnvloed het. Die verslag het ook 'n 4% afname in jong wit studente sedert 2009 uitgewys—die grootste daling sedert minstens 1993—aangesien die getal mense in dié ouderdomsgroep afgeneem het. Ruiz beskou haar strewe na hoër onderwys as sentraal tot haar Amerikaanse droom en moedig haar broers aan om van dieselfde geleenthede gebruik te maak.

article_content: Niger State Governor Mohammed Bago has identified climate change as a factor contributing to the ongoing insecurity in Nigeria. Speaking at a climate change retreat in Minna, organized for the House of Representatives Press Corps, Bago, represented by Deputy Governor Yakubu Garba, called climate change one of Nigeria’s biggest challenges. He noted, 'In Nigeria, climate change is a serious concern for governments and experts due to its alarming effects, including floods, desertification, and environmental pollution. Despite ongoing efforts, yearly devastation continues. Part of the insecurity facing the nation has roots in climate change, and these issues need urgent attention.' Bago highlighted that some disasters may be underreported, possibly due to the media lacking resources or expertise. He urged journalists, especially those in parliament, to build skills and tools to cover climate change, thereby helping legislators address these issues. The Governor announced that Niger State would host a Green Economy Summit to find solutions to both natural and manmade disasters driven by climate change. According to Bago, his administration is committed to increasing public awareness, partnering with the media, and further advocating for climate policy action. During the event, Director General of the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies (NILDS), Abubakar Suleiman (represented by Democracy Radio’s General Manager, Kudu Abubakar), stressed that the media should keep lawmakers informed about climate policies and hold them accountable for outcomes. Grace Ike, Chairperson of the House of Representatives Press Corps, emphasized the media’s vital role in informing the public and sharing stories of government actions on climate change. She said reporters must communicate developments clearly as climate change impacts every part of society. The three-day event is scheduled to conclude on Sunday.

Hy het gesê: 'In Nigerië is klimaatverandering 'n ernstige bekommernis vir regerings en kundiges vanweë die ontstellende gevolge, insluitend vloede, verwoestyning en omgewingsbesoedeling. Ten spyte van voortdurende pogings, hou die jaarlikse verwoesting aan. Deel van die onsekerheid wat die land ervaar, spruit uit klimaatverandering, en hierdie kwessies verdien dringende aandag.' Bago het daarop gewys dat sommige rampe moontlik ondergerapporteer word, moontlik as gevolg van 'n tekort aan hulpbronne of kundigheid in die media. Hy het joernaliste, veral dié wat oor die parlement verslag doen, aangemoedig om die nodige vaardighede en gereedskap te ontwikkel om oor klimaatverandering te berig, en so wetgewers te help om hierdie uitdagings aan te spreek. Die goewerneur het aangekondig dat Niger-staat 'n Groene Ekonomie-beraad gaan aanbied om oplossings te vind vir beide natuurlike en mensgemaakte rampe wat deur klimaatverandering veroorsaak word. Volgens Bago is sy administrasie daartoe verbind om openbare bewusmaking te bevorder, saam met die media te werk, en verder vir klimaatsaksie te pleit. Tydens die geleentheid het die Direkteur-Generaal van die Nasionale Instituut vir Wetgewende en Demokratiese Studies (NILDS), Abubakar Suleiman (verteenwoordig deur Democracy Radio se Algemene Bestuurder, Kudu Abubakar), beklemtoon dat die media wetgewers op hoogte moet hou van klimaatbeleid en hulle aanspreeklik moet hou vir die uitkomste. Sy het gesê verslaggewers moet ontwikkelings duidelik kommunikeer, omdat klimaatverandering elke deel van die samelewing raak. Die driedaagse geleentheid eindig Sondag.

article_content: Fighters from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and allied Arab militias carried out a devastating multi-day attack on Ardamata in West Darfur, Sudan, reportedly killing more than 800 people, according to doctors and the United Nations. This assault is the latest in a series of atrocities in Darfur amid ongoing conflict between the Sudanese military and the RSF, which began in April 2023 after tensions between military leaders General Abdel-Fattah Burhan and General Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo escalated into war. The war followed an October 2021 coup by the two generals, ending Sudan’s push towards democracy after the 2019 ousting of Omar al-Bashir. In recent weeks, the RSF has captured major towns and cities in Darfur, despite peace talks in Saudi Arabia mediated by the U.S. and Saudi Arabia that failed to produce a ceasefire. The attack on Ardamata started after the RSF seized a military base following brief clashes on November 4. Salah Tour, head of the Sudanese Doctors’ Union in West Darfur, reported the military's withdrawal and that about two dozen injured soldiers fled to Chad. After gaining control, RSF and their allied militias rampaged through the town, killing non-Arabs—especially targeting the Masalit tribe—and burning shelters for displaced people. The Darfur Bar Association accused the RSF of committing serious human rights violations, noting that on November 6, more than 50 people, including a tribal leader and his family, were killed. The UNHCR reported that over 800 people were killed and 8,000 fled to Chad, although real numbers may be higher. Around 100 shelters in Ardamata were destroyed, and humanitarian supplies were looted. UN High Commissioner for Refugees Filippo Grandi warned of a repeat of the atrocities that shocked the world in Darfur two decades ago. The U.S. State Department condemned the RSF for abuses, including targeted killings of Masalit community leaders, citing a pattern of RSF violations. Ardamata is just north of Geneina, where RSF and allied militias launched major attacks earlier, forcing many non-Arabs to flee. International bodies have accused the RSF and allied groups of widespread atrocities in Darfur and the capital, Khartoum, including mass killings and rape. In July, the UN Human Rights Office reported a mass grave with at least 87 bodies outside Geneina. The International Criminal Court is investigating possible war crimes and crimes against humanity in the latest Darfur fighting. Overall, 9,000 people have been killed and over 6 million displaced by the conflict, with 1.2 million taking refuge in neighboring countries, according to the UN. Fighting spread from Khartoum to other regions, devastating infrastructure, including the recent collapse of the Shambat bridge. Both sides blame each other for the destruction.
translated_content: Vegters van die paramilitêre Rapid Support Forces (RSF) en geallieerde Arabiese milisies het 'n verwoestende aanval wat oor verskeie dae gestrek het op Ardamata in Wes-Darfoer, Soedan, uitgevoer, en volgens dokters en die Verenigde Nasies is daar vermoedelik meer as 800 mense doodgemaak. Hierdie aanval is die jongste in 'n reeks gruweldade in Darfoer te midde van die voortdurende konflik tussen die Soedanese weermag en die RSF, wat in April 2023 begin het ná spanning tussen generaals Abdel-Fattah Burhan en Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo tot oorlog gelei het. Die oorlog het gevolg op 'n staatsgreep in Oktober 2021 deur die twee generaals wat die proses na demokrasie beëindig het nadat Omar al-Bashir in 2019 omvergewerp is. In onlangse weke het die RSF groot dorpe en stede in Darfoer oorgeneem, ten spyte van vredesonderhandelinge in Saoedi-Arabië wat deur die VSA en Saoedi-Arabië bemiddel is en wat nie 'n wapenstilstand kon bewerkstellig nie. Die aanval op Ardamata het begin nadat die RSF op 4 November 'n militêre basis ingeneem het na kort gevegte. Salah Tour, hoof van die Soedanese Doktersunie in Wes-Darfoer, het gesê die weermag het onttrek en sowat twee dosyn beseerde soldate het na Tsjad gevlug. Nadat hulle beheer gekry het, het die RSF en hul geallieerde milisies deur die dorp getrek en nie-Arabiese inwoners vermoor—veral die Masalit-stam geteiken—en skuilings van ontheemde mense afgebrand. Die Darfoer Balievereniging het die RSF beskuldig van ernstige menseregtevergrype en gesê dat meer as 50 mense, insluitend 'n stamleier en sy gesin, op 6 November vermoor is. Die VN se Vlugteling-agentskap het berig dat meer as 800 mense dood is en 8 000 na Tsjad gevlug het, hoewel die syfers waarskynlik hoër is. Ongeveer 100 skuilings is vernietig en humanitêre voorrade is geplunder. VN se Hoë Kommissaris vir Vlugtelinge, Filippo Grandi, het gewaarsku dat die wêreld dalk weer soortgelyke gruweldade soos 20 jaar gelede in Darfoer sien. Die VSA se Staatsdepartement het die RSF veroordeel vir vergrype soos die moord op Masalit-gemeenskapsleiers en het 'n patroon van misbruik beklemtoon. Ardamata is net noord van Geneina, waar die RSF en hul geallieerde milisies reeds groot aanvalle uitgevoer het wat baie nie-Arabier-inwoners laat vlug het. Internasionale organisasies beskuldig die RSF en hul bondgenote van wye gruweldade in Darfoer en in die hoofstad Khartoem, insluitend massamoorde en verkragting. In Julie het die VN se Menseregtekantoor 'n massagraf met minstens 87 liggame buite Geneina aangemeld. Die Internasionale Strafhof ondersoek moontlike oorlogsmisdade en misdade teen die mensdom oor die jongste geweld in Darfoer. Tot dusver is sowat 9 000 mense dood en meer as 6 miljoen ontheem deur die konflik, en 1.2 miljoen het skuiling in buurlande gesoek, volgens die VN. Die gevegte het van Khartoem na ander streke versprei en belangrike infrastruktuur vernietig, insluitend die onlangse ineenstorting van die Shambat-brug, waarvoor albei kante mekaar die skuld gee.
