article_content: Gary Walker, former chief executive of United Lincolnshire Hospitals NHS Trust, claims that bullying is widespread within the NHS. Walker alleges he was threatened by the East Midlands Strategic Health Authority (SHA) after voicing concerns about the hospital nearing capacity. He says he was dismissed after raising patient safety issues and pressured to meet targets regardless of demand, describing this as dangerous. Walker was sacked in 2010 for 'gross professional misconduct' but asserts it was retaliation for resisting non-emergency patient targets and was prevented from speaking publicly by a settlement agreement. He recounts a 2009 meeting with Dame Barbara Hakin, now interim chief operating officer of the NHS Commissioning Board, where he felt threats were made should he fail to deliver targets. Hakin denies these allegations. Walker claims he was ordered to remove references to capacity review requests from a Department of Health presentation. He suggests that repercussions awaited anyone challenging the SHA, and that other hospital executives shared concerns about high-handed management. David Bowles, former ULHT chairman, supports Walker's account, saying there was a tendency in the NHS to make things 'look good rather than be good.' Bowles states that financial issues at the trust were deliberately concealed from Department of Health officials by the SHA. Bowles claims ULHT was omitted from government compensation for financial deficits, as the SHA did not wish to highlight trusts facing financial difficulties. He emphasizes a culture of avoiding transparency and the existence of fear among staff about raising concerns. Bowles highlights that the trust was under pressure to prioritize targets over genuine need, sometimes at the risk of patient welfare. He notes that staff feared retribution if they spoke out, mentioning that Walker struggled to find work after whistleblowing. Bowles and Walker argue that the NHS leadership, particularly that of Sir David Nicholson, must change for the broader culture to improve. Walker alleges that Dame Barbara Hakin authorized his severance to protect her own position, an allegation she denies. NHS Midlands and East, as the SHA's successor, presented evidence to the House of Commons Health Select Committee challenging Walker's claims as a whistleblower and stating that patient safety concerns were addressed by the SHA, not by Walker. The trust is currently under investigation due to high mortality rates, following serious failures in other NHS trusts like Mid Staffordshire.

Hy sê hy is afgedank nadat hy pasiëntveiligheidskwessies aangespreek het en hy is onder druk geplaas om teikens te behaal ongeag die vraag, wat hy as gevaarlik beskou. Hakin ontken hierdie bewerings. Walker sê hy moes alle verwysings na kapasiteitshersiening uit 'n Departement van Gesondheid-aanbieding verwyder. Hy gee aan dat daar teenstand gekom het teen enigeen wat die SHA bevraagteken het, en ander bestuurders het soortgelyke bekommernisse oor owerheidspraktyke gedeel. Die trust word tans ondersoek vir hoë sterftesyfers, ná soortgelyke probleme by NHS-trusts soos Mid Staffordshire.

article_content: Luis Suarez is facing a pivotal FIFA disciplinary hearing after being accused of biting Italian defender Giorgio Chiellini during Uruguay's World Cup match against Italy. The incident has generated global attention and widespread humor from fellow players, fans, and celebrities alike. In response, Giorgio Chiellini himself shared a playful image of a hotel maid pretending to bite his shoulder, mirroring the on-field event. Meanwhile, Brazil’s Fred was photographed jokingly biting teammate Marcelo at a training session. American comedian Will Ferrell added to the amusement by telling US supporters in Recife he’d 'bite every German player' if the USA’s next match was close. Journalists have gotten in on the act too. A Future Proof blog for the New Statesman calculated, tongue-in-cheek, that footballers have a greater chance of being bitten by Suarez than by a shark—about one in 2,000 compared to one in 3.7 million. On social media, the reaction was massive. Suarez saw his Twitter mentions jump from approximately 100,000 to over two million in just a few hours, with heavy activity in Europe, the US, South America, and surges in Asian and African countries. The most retweeted Suarez post depicted him in a vet-style collar, bringing lighthearted commentary. Well-known figures such as Russell Brand joined the online banter, and stories emerged of fans profiting from bets about Suarez biting during the tournament. Despite the jokes, Suarez is dealing with serious professional implications. Sponsors like adidas and 888poker are reviewing their relationships with the player. Adidas awaits FIFA’s judgment before acting, while 888poker stated that unsporting behavior is unacceptable and is reconsidering their sponsorship. FIFA’s disciplinary committee, chaired by Swiss lawyer Claudio Sulser, is considering possible punishments, ranging up to a 24-match or two-year ban from football. Suarez has prior bans for biting; whether those incidents are relevant to this case is up to the panel. Suarez himself has not appeared at the hearing, but the Uruguay Football Association is defending him vigorously. Notably, regional football powerbrokers, including Argentina's vice-president Julio Grondona and CONMEBOL’s Eugenio Figueredo, are said to be lobbying for leniency. Suarez’s lawyer Alejandro Balbi argues there’s a campaign against Suarez led by European nations. The Uruguay FA has questioned the validity of photos showing bite marks on Chiellini, suggesting they might have been digitally enhanced. The panel’s decision is expected soon, ahead of Uruguay’s next match.

Die voorval het wêreldwyd aandag getrek en word met humor benader deur ander spelers, ondersteuners en bekendes. Sommige ondersteuners het selfs gewen nadat hulle op 'n byt-voorval gewed het. Ten spyte van al die humor, wag daar ernstige professionele gevolge op Suarez. Borge soos adidas en 888poker herevalueer hul vennootskappe met hom. Adidas wag op FIFA se finale uitspraak voordat hulle verder optree, terwyl 888poker hul verhouding heroorweeg oor die speler se gedrag. Invloedryke sokkerleiers soos Argentinië se vise-president Julio Grondona en CONMEBOL se Eugenio Figueredo is glo besig om pleit vir 'n ligter straf. Suarez se regsverteenwoordiger Alejandro Balbi reken daar is 'n Europese veldtog teen hom. Uruguay se FA bevraagteken die egtheid van die foto’s van bytmerke op Chiellini en beweer dit kan digitaal aangepas wees. Die komitee se besluit word binnekort verwag voor Uruguay se volgende wedstryd.

article_content: Liberia is heading for a runoff election after incumbent President George Weah and his main rival, Joseph Boakai, finished almost evenly matched in the initial round. According to the national electoral commission’s provisional data, Boakai, 78, holds a narrow lead with 43.70% of the votes, while Weah, 57, has 43.65%, with more than 94% of ballots counted. The two are significantly ahead of the other 18 candidates who competed in the October 10 presidential vote. Since neither contender secured a majority, a second round will be held about two weeks after results are finalized, though legal challenges could potentially cause delays. Officials indicated that vote counting is complete in nearly 93% of polling locations, and turnout was notably high. The African Union and the West African bloc ECOWAS have praised the smooth and peaceful conduct of the election. This election is Liberia’s first presidential contest since the United Nations ended its peacekeeping operation in 2018. That mission was established following Liberia’s civil wars between 1989 and 2003, which resulted in more than a quarter-million deaths.
translated_content: Liberië gaan na ‘n uitkloprondte nadat die huidige president, George Weah, en sy hoofmededinger, Joseph Boakai, amper gelykop geëindig het in die eerste rondte. Volgens voorlopige data van die nasionale verkiesingskommissie het Boakai (78) ‘n klein voorsprong met 43.70% van die stemme, terwyl Weah (57) 43.65% het, met meer as 94% van die stemme getel. Die twee is ver voor die ander 18 kandidate wat aan die presidentsverkiesing op 10 Oktober deelgeneem het. Omdat geen kandidaat ‘n meerderheid behaal het nie, sal ‘n tweede rondte ongeveer twee weke na die finale uitslae plaasvind, hoewel regsgedinge moontlik kan lei tot vertragings. Amptenare het gesê dat stemtelling in byna 93% van die stemlokale voltooi is, en deelname was baie goed. Die Afrika-Unie en die Wes-Afrikaanse blok ECOWAS het die ordelike en vreedsame verloop van die verkiesing geprys. article_content: Dollar General has agreed to pay $1 million to settle a lawsuit alleging violations of disability-discrimination laws. The suit, filed by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) in 2017, accused the discount retailer of withdrawing job offers from applicants with high blood pressure or poor eyesight. Applicants for general warehouse positions at Dollar General’s Bessemer, Alabama facility were required to undergo pre-employment medical exams that the EEOC described as extensive and highly invasive. These exams included vital sign checks, drug and vision tests, medication reviews, and in some cases, genital examinations. The EEOC claimed that some qualified candidates were rejected due to disabilities that would not restrict them from performing the job safely, such as blood pressure readings over 160/100 or vision worse than 20/50 in both eyes. The exams also required candidates to disclose family medical histories, including instances of cancer, diabetes, and heart disease. The EEOC alleged that Dollar General’s medical criteria were not job-related or necessary for business operations, thus violating the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and the Genetic Information Non-Discrimination Act (GINA). After the lawsuit was filed, the company stopped requiring these pre-employment exams for warehouse roles. Dollar General, in its 2018 response, asserted that employment decisions were based on legitimate, non-discriminatory business reasons. The retailer also denied intentionally collecting genetic information through health questionnaires, stating that any such collection by third-party providers was done without its knowledge. The settlement, approved by Judge Madeline Hughes Haikala, requires Dollar General to compensate affected applicants, review and update its ADA and GINA policies, provide annual training for all hiring staff, and ensure medical examiners do not request family medical history. 'Requiring individuals during the hiring process to answer invasive questions about the medical conditions of their grandparents, parents, or children violates GINA,' said Bradley Anderson, EEOC district director in Birmingham. Dollar General did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
translated_content: Dollar General het ingestem om $1 miljoen te betaal om ŉ regsgeding oor beweerde oortredings van gestremdheidsdiskriminasie-wette te skik. Die saak, wat in 2017 deur die Gelyke Indiensnemingsgeleenthede Kommissie (EEOC) ingestel is, het die afslagkleinhandelaar daarvan beskuldig dat hulle werkaanbiedings teruggetrek het aan aansoekers met hoë bloeddruk of swak sig. Aansoekers vir algemene pakhuisposte by Dollar General se Bessemer, Alabama-fasiliteit moes voor indiensneming mediese ondersoeke ondergaan wat die EEOC as omvattend en hoogs indringend beskryf het. Hierdie ondersoeke het lewensbelangrike tekens, dwelm- en visie-toetse, medikasie-hersienings, en in sommige gevalle, genitale ondersoeke ingesluit. Die EEOC het beweer dat sommige gekwalifiseerde kandidate vanweë gestremdhede wat hulle nie sou keer om hul werk veilig uit te voer nie—soos bloeddruk bo 160/100 of sig erger as 20/50 in albei oë—verwerp is. Die ondersoeke het ook vereis dat kandidate hul gesinsgeskiedenis met betrekking tot siektes soos kanker, diabetes, en hartsiektes moes bekend maak. Die EEOC het beweer dat Dollar General se mediese kriteria nie werkverwant of noodsaaklik vir bedryfsdoeleindes was nie en dus die Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) en Genetic Information Non-Discrimination Act (GINA) oortree het. Nadat die regsgeding aanhangig gemaak is, het die maatskappy opgehou om hierdie voorindiensnemingsondersoeke vir pakhuisposte te vereis. Dollar General het in sy 2018-antwoord beweer dat hulle indiensnemingsbesluite op wettige, nie-diskriminerende besigheidsredes gebaseer was. Die kleinhandelaar het ook ontken dat hulle doelbewus genetiese inligting deur gesondheidsvraelyste ingesamel het en gesê enige sodanige insameling deur derdeparty-verskaffers was sonder hul medewete. Die skikking, wat deur Regter Madeline Hughes Haikala goedgekeur is, vereis dat Dollar General die geraakte aansoekers vergoed, sy ADA- en GINA-beleide hersien en opdateer, jaarliks opleiding aan alle aanstellingspersoneel gee, en seker maak dat mediese ondersoekers nie gesinsgesondheidsgeskiedenis aanvra nie. 'Om mense te vra om indringende vrae oor hul ouers, grootouers of kinders se mediese toestande tydens die aanstellingsproses te beantwoord, is 'n oortreding van GINA,' het Bradley Anderson, EEOC-distrikdirekteur in Birmingham, gesê. Dollar General het nie dadelik op versoeke om kommentaar gereageer nie.

article_content: A once stray dog named Xiao Sa captured hearts across China by running an extraordinary 1,100 miles alongside a team of cyclists traveling from Kangding in Sichuan Province to Lhasa in Tibet. Now affectionately called the 'dog with determination,' Xiao Sa has been adopted by Zhang Heng, a 22-year-old cycling enthusiast and student who welcomed her into his home in Wuhan, Hubei province. Xiao Sa's journey began when Zhang Heng discovered her lying exhausted on Highway G318 in the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. The cyclists offered her food, and she surprised them by joining their group and staying by their side throughout the 24-day trek. During their adventure, the team climbed 10 mountains towering over 4,000 meters. Xiao Sa often accompanied them on the toughest stretches, unfailingly keeping up—even when other cyclists took buses during difficult segments. For safety, Zhang sometimes carried her in a basket on his bike while riding downhill at high speeds. The cyclists shared Xiao Sa’s progress through the 'Go Go Xiao Sa' microblog, which quickly gained immense popularity online, amassing more than 37,000 followers and over 4,000 comments within two weeks. Cyclists like Wang Penghao and Wang Zi described Xiao Sa’s intelligence and loyalty, recalling how she always found the route and waited for the team at important points. Once a stray, Xiao Sa has now found a caring home, and her inspiring story of persistence and friendship continues to touch thousands across China.

Nou, liefdevol bekend as die ‘hond met deursettingsvermoë’, is Xiao Sa aangeneem deur Zhang Heng, ’n 22-jarige fietsryer en student wat haar in sy huis in Wuhan, Hubei-provinsie, verwelkom het. article_content: Manchester City settled for a 1-1 draw with Everton at Goodison Park, falling two points behind Premier League leaders Chelsea. City manager Manuel Pellegrini’s push to sign striker Wilfried Bony seemed justified, as his team squandered multiple goal-scoring opportunities in the first half. Although City controlled the early stages, they managed only two shots on target—wasting quality chances from David Silva’s creative play. Fernandinho’s second-half header put City ahead after Everton goalkeeper Joel Robles spilled Silva’s attempt. However, Everton quickly hit back when Steven Naismith out-jumped Joe Hart to nod in a Leighton Baines free-kick, marking Baines’ 45th Premier League assist—a new record for a defender. Sergio Aguero made his return from injury off the bench, but City’s attacking struggles continued. Pellegrini expressed frustration with his squad's finishing and emphasized that such results could impact their title challenge. Despite entering the match on a four-game losing streak, Everton showed determination in tough, rainy conditions. Romelu Lukaku posed a constant threat up front, challenging City’s defenders and testing Joe Hart repeatedly. In the end, Manchester City's missed chances and Everton's spirited response resulted in the teams sharing the points.

article_content: Hans Sachs, a German Jewish enthusiast, built one of the world's most impressive pre-war poster collections, starting in his youth and growing it to about 12,500 pieces, many kept in a gallery at his home. In 1938, the Nazis, acting under Joseph Goebbels' orders, confiscated Sachs' collection to use for a planned museum. During Kristallnacht, Sachs was arrested and sent to Sachsenhausen concentration camp. Sachs and his wife managed to escape to the US, but he never saw his posters again—they ended up behind the Iron Curtain in East Berlin. After the Berlin Wall's fall, the German Historical Museum acquired about 4,300 of these posters. In 2005, Peter Sachs, living in Las Vegas, learned of their survival and spent seven years fighting legally to recover his father's collection. Germany’s top appeals court ruled in Peter's favor, and the posters were returned in 2012. Unable to find a museum able to take all of them, Peter decided to auction most of the posters, with the estimated value ranging from $6 million to $21 million. Guernsey's auction house in New York is offering 1,233 posters, including works by Edvard Munch, Gustav Klimt, and James Montgomery Flagg. Many date back to the late 19th century, were printed in small numbers, and remain in remarkable condition. Peter plans to keep about 800 posters, intending to donate many to museums, especially those focusing on Holocaust history. A few, like a Manoli cigarettes poster by Lucian Bernhard, are personally significant due to family ties. There are plans for possible exhibitions, including at the Sachsenhausen camp memorial where Hans was once imprisoned. Peter's attorney, Gary Osen, highlights that more of the collection will now be available for public viewing than if they had remained in museum storage. Peter Sachs says his feelings are not of victory, but of vindication, hoping the posters will finally be appreciated by those who cherish them instead of remaining hidden for decades.
translated_content: Hans Sachs, 'n Duitse Joodse entoesias, het een van die wêreld se indrukwekkendste vooroorlogse plakkaatversamelings opgebou. Hy het in sy jeug begin en uiteindelik sowat 12 500 plakkate versamel, waarvan baie in 'n spesiale galery by sy huis gebly het. In 1938 het die Nazi's, onder Joseph Goebbels se leiding, Sachs se versameling gekonfiskeer om dit in 'n beplande museum uit te stal. Tydens Kristallnacht is Sachs gearresteer en na die Sachsenhausen-konsentrasiekamp gestuur. Hy en sy vrou het daarin geslaag om na die VSA te vlug, maar hy het nooit weer sy plakkate gesien nie—dit het uiteindelik agter die Ystergordyn in Oos-Berlyn beland. Na die val van die Berlynse Muur het die Duitse Historiese Museum sowat 4 300 van die plakkate verkry. In 2005 het Peter Sachs, toe in Las Vegas, uitgevind dat hulle oorleef het en het hy sewe jaar lank vir hul teruggawe geveg. Duitsland se hoogste appèlhof het in Peter se guns beslis en die plakkate is in 2012 aan hom terugbesorg. Omdat hy nie 'n museum kon kry wat almal kon huisves nie, verkoop hy die meeste van die plakkate by afslaer, met 'n geraamde waarde van $6 miljoen tot $21 miljoen. Guernsey's afslaershuis in New York bied 1 233 plakkate aan, insluitende werke van Edvard Munch, Gustav Klimt en James Montgomery Flagg. Baie van die plakkate is uit die laat 19de eeu, was skaars gedruk en is uitstekend bewaar. Peter hou sowat 800 plakkate terug wat hy graag aan museums wil skenk, veral dié wat fokus op Holokaus-geskiedenis. Sommige, soos 'n Manoli-sigaretplakkaat deur Lucian Bernhard, dra persoonlike betekenis weens familieverbintenisse. Daar is reeds beplanning vir moontlike uitstallings, insluitende een by Sachsenhausen se gedenkplek, waar Hans tydelik aangehou is. Peter se regsverteenwoordiger, Gary Osen, wys daarop dat meer mense die plakkate nou sal kan sien as wat sou gebeur as dit net in 'n museum se stoor gebly het. Peter Sachs sê hy voel nie oorwin nie, maar regverdig; hy hoop die plakkate kry uiteindelik die erkenning wat hulle verdien en nie weer vir dekades weggebêre sal bly nie.

article_content: Davy Jones, best known as the spirited lead singer of The Monkees and a 1960s television icon, died at 66 in Florida. Reports state he suffered chest pain and breathing difficulties before being transported to a hospital in Indiantown, where he was declared dead, likely from a heart attack. Laurie Jacobson, an associate who frequently worked with Jones, recalled his commitment to healthy living and active routine in Florida, expressing surprise at his unexpected passing. Celebrated for fronting Monkees hits such as 'Daydream Believer' and 'A Little Bit Me, A Little Bit You,' Jones was an original member of the NBC-created pop group, sharing the spotlight with Micky Dolenz, Peter Tork, and Michael Nesmith. He remained a favorite at nostalgic fan gatherings. Debuting in 1966, The Monkees’ TV program enjoyed significant success, producing chart-topping songs like 'I'm a Believer' and several No. 1 albums. Although initially cast for television, the band pushed to perform their own music, ultimately earning more input but coinciding with fading broad appeal. The show ended after two seasons, and the group soon disbanded. Jones’s popularity endured through concert appearances and TV reunions, where he cherished interactions with his supporters. Beyond performing, he was passionate about horse ownership and racing. Hailing from Manchester, Jones had previously starred as the Artful Dodger in 'Oliver!' on both London's West End and Broadway. Later, he made cameo appearances in 'The Brady Bunch' and voiced himself in 'SpongeBob SquarePants.' Having married three times, Jones is survived by his third wife, Jessica Pacheco, and four daughters from earlier marriages. He valued his family life and regularly shared updates with fans via his personal blog. His passing was widely mourned, with heartfelt tributes arriving from fellow Monkees member Michael Nesmith and musician Ringo Starr, reflecting the widespread affection Jones inspired.

article_content: CNN.com staff recently expressed interest in the unique reporting from VICE, an independent media company in Brooklyn, New York, and its broadband TV channel VBS.TV. Their transparent, immersive journalism was shown as a reporter traveled to Bogotá, Colombia, to meet tailor Miguel Caballero, who creates fashionable bulletproof clothing used by politicians, celebrities, and others at risk. The journalist toured Miguel’s workshop, which seemed typical until the true nature of the garments was revealed: the jackets and blazers are designed to protect the wearer from bullets at close range. Miguel detailed his company's aim to unite personal safety with style, addressing growing concerns worldwide. He then invited the journalist to personally test a bulletproof jacket. In an impromptu demonstration, Miguel provided a black suede jacket and noise-reducing headphones before firing a .38-caliber handgun at the journalist’s abdomen in mid-countdown. The jacket successfully stopped the bullet, leaving the journalist unharmed but a bit shaken. Miguel’s innovative clothing line has gained global attention, with some rumors claiming President Obama wore one of his pieces during his inauguration. The journalist notes that as items once exclusive to the military—like armored vehicles—have become mainstream, protective clothing might soon follow.

article_content: At least three people were killed in a drone strike on the Jenin refugee camp, while approximately 80 Israeli military vehicles entered the city of Jenin in the occupied West Bank. Several hospitals were surrounded and at least three people lost their lives as Israeli forces conducted a significant overnight raid that lasted into Friday. According to Palestinian sources, the incursion also left at least 14 others injured before ending after several hours. The Palestinian ambulance service reported that the drone strike on the Jenin refugee camp killed at least three people, whereas the Israeli army claimed five casualties. Air strikes have become more frequent in the West Bank as the conflict in Gaza continues. According to the Palestinian news agency Wafa, Israeli forces prevented emergency services from reaching the injured, potentially putting lives at risk. Starting at about 10:30pm on Thursday, Israeli forces deployed at least 80 military vehicles into Jenin, raided Palestinian homes, and arrested several individuals amid reports of violent confrontations. Al Jazeera’s Sara Khairat, reporting from occupied East Jerusalem, described how armored vehicles and bulldozers damaged cars and roads during the approximately eight-hour raid. At least four hospitals, including Ibn Sina Hospital, were surrounded by Israeli troops. Khairat reported that Israeli forces entered Ibn Sina Hospital, one of the largest in the West Bank, required staff to raise their hands, and called for evacuation. Some doctors refused to leave the hospital, and two paramedics were arrested during the incident. Khairat noted that clashes are frequent in the Jenin refugee camp, with this raid standing out for its scale and tactics. The Israeli military stated it exchanged fire with Palestinian fighters, who allegedly used ambulances to reach Ibn Sina Hospital to hide. One Palestinian fighter was arrested at the entrance to the hospital, according to the army. Tensions have increased throughout the West Bank since the beginning of the Israel-Gaza war on October 7, which has caused at least 11,500 deaths in Gaza. The Commission for Prisoners and Ex-Detainees Affairs reported that Israeli forces arrested 47 Palestinians across the West Bank overnight, including 26 in Nelin, west of Ramallah. Al Jazeera’s Zein Basravi, reporting from Ramallah, said that two Palestinians were killed in a shootout with Israeli troops at a checkpoint north of Hebron on Friday. On Thursday, three Palestinians were shot dead by Israeli soldiers after opening fire at another West Bank checkpoint, resulting in the death of one Israeli soldier, according to Israeli officials. Basravi said attacks by Palestinians using firearms and explosives have risen in recent weeks, as anger increases over civilian deaths in Gaza and ongoing occupation in the West Bank. Since October 7, 203 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli raids in the West Bank.

Verskeie hospitale is omsingel en minstens drie mense is dood toe Israeliese magte 'n groot oornagraad loods wat tot Vrydag geduur het. Die Israeliese weermag het gesê dat hulle vuur uitgeruil het met Palestynse vegters, wat na bewering ambulansse gebruik het om Ibn Sina Hospitaal te bereik om weg te steek. Een Palestynse vegter is by die ingang van die hospitaal in hegtenis geneem, volgens die weermag. Spanning het regoor die Wesoewer toegeneem sedert die begin van die Israel-Gasa-oorlog op 7 Oktober, wat ten minste 11,500 sterftes in Gasa tot gevolg gehad het. Die Kommissie vir Gevangenes en Oud-Gevangenes Sake het berig dat Israeliese magte 47 Palestyne regoor die Wesoewer oornag gearresteer het, insluitend 26 in Nelin, wes van Ramallah. Al Jazeera se Zein Basravi, wat uit Ramallah verslag doen, het gesê twee Palestyne is Vrydag in 'n vuurgeveg met Israeliese troepe by 'n padblokkade noord van Hebron doodgeskiet. Donderdag is drie Palestyne deur Israeliese soldate doodgeskiet nadat hulle op 'n ander Wesoewer-padblokkade losgebrand het, wat gelei het tot een Israeliese soldaat se dood, volgens Israeliese amptenare. Basravi het gesê aanvalle deur Palestyne met vuurwapens en plofstof het in die afgelope weke toegeneem namate woede oor burgersterftes in Gasa en aanhoudende besetting in die Wesoewer toeneem. Sedert 7 Oktober is 203 Palestyne in Israeliese aanvalle in die Wesoewer dood.

article_content: Prince Harry was welcomed by tens of thousands of enthusiastic fans on Sydney Harbour during his first official visit to Australia. Crowds cheered as he greeted onlookers following the International Fleet Review, which featured 40 warships from 17 countries. Visiting on behalf of Queen Elizabeth II, Harry's fun-loving reputation drew attention in the media. He interacted warmly with fans, sharing jokes and handshakes with people of all ages, including young children. Despite a 20-hour flight from the UK, Harry appeared energetic, boarding the HMAS Leeuwin in a white Army tropical uniform and Army Air Corps beret. Prime Minister Tony Abbott and Governor-General Quentin Bryce joined Harry onboard. Later, he changed into a navy blue suit for a walk among the crowds, meeting fans such as Lauren Burke and Renee Simmons, who expressed admiration. During his trip, Harry posed for photographs, met with West Australian Premier Colin Barnett and his wife Lyn in Perth, and thanked police officers and members of the public. Harry sailed past the Sydney Opera House by boat to Kirribilli House, the Prime Minister's official residence, where he was introduced to the Abbott family. Mr Abbott, a monarchist, apologized for Australia's republican sentiment, and remarked that 'everyone feels like a monarchist' on this day. The visit was highlighted by a major fireworks show over Sydney Harbour Bridge, seen by an estimated 1.4 million people. Harry described the event as 'absolutely fantastic' before departing for Perth. He noted his visit was brief due to work commitments and mentioned he would travel to Dubai for a Sentebale charity event. This was Harry's first official visit, though he spent time in Australia in 2003 during his gap year working on a ranch.

article_content: SenseTime, a leading company in China’s AI industry, is facing major challenges due to U.S. government export restrictions. These measures prevent firms like Nvidia from selling advanced chips to Chinese companies, affecting SenseTime’s efforts to diversify its business model. Based in Hong Kong, the AI firm has been seeking to reduce its reliance on its main surveillance business, which supplies AI-powered security cameras to Chinese authorities. However, according to a recent report by The Financial Times, the ongoing U.S.-China 'chip war' may disrupt these plans. Prior to its public listing two years ago, SenseTime’s CEO Xu Li emphasized the future revenue potential from a large AI data center in Shanghai. This center, powered by Nvidia’s A100 GPUs, was intended to serve several AI companies. Buying GPUs before the U.S. imposed export bans initially appeared to be a sound strategy for SenseTime. Yet as the U.S. further tightens restrictions on AI chip sales to China, this advantage is shrinking. The newer U.S. measures have also put SenseTime on the Entity List and an investment blacklist, prompting some foreign investors to pull out. Despite efforts to secure its supply chain, SenseTime has seen a drop in revenue from its traditional surveillance technology. Sales for its smart city surveillance products fell by 58% in the first half of the year. While SenseTime remains hopeful about its long-term outlook, analysts are skeptical about the company’s stock performance in the current environment.

Die KI-maatskappy, gebaseer in Hongkong, probeer hulle afhanklikheid van hul kern toesigbesigheid, wat KI-aangedrewe sekuriteitskameras aan Chinese owerhede verskaf, verminder. Die nuwe Amerikaanse maatreëls het SenseTime op die sogenaamde Entity List én op ‘n beleggingsswartlys geplaas, wat veroorsaak het dat sommige buitelandse beleggers hulle steun onttrek het. Ten spyte van pogings om hul voorsieningsketting te beveilig, het SenseTime 'n afname in inkomste uit hul tradisionele toesigtegnologie gesien. article_content: At least 10 people were killed and 58 wounded when a bomb exploded inside the Abu-Yahya restaurant, a popular spot in central Mosul, northern Iraq, on Friday evening, according to Nineveh provincial police commander Khalid al-Midani. The explosion occurred around 8:30 p.m., and most of the casualties were civilians. Mosul, the capital of Nineveh province, is about 400 kilometers (250 miles) north of Baghdad and is predominantly Sunni. In addition, officials reported that at least 11 people were killed and 21 wounded in separate incidents elsewhere in Iraq the same day.

article_content: A groundbreaking international study warns that widespread use of dyes across key industries—including textiles, food, and pharmaceuticals—poses significant risks to global ecosystems and human health. Each year, billions of tons of wastewater containing dyes are discharged into rivers, lakes, and other water systems, mostly untreated in many developing countries. Published in Nature Reviews Earth & Environment, the research involved scientists from the University of Bath, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University, KENTECH in Korea, and KU Leuven in Belgium. The authors highlight a pressing need for sustainable treatment methods like advanced membrane-based filtration, as well as stronger laws forcing industries to remove dye pollutants before releasing water into the environment. Up to 80% of dye-heavy industrial wastewater in lower-income nations currently goes untreated, and is sometimes even used for crop irrigation, putting plants, animals, and humans at risk through direct exposure or by entering the food chain. According to Dr. Ming Xie of the University of Bath, dyes not only block crucial sunlight for aquatic microorganisms but can also disrupt the entire food chain and harm various forms of life. While removal technologies exist, choosing the right one depends on the dye involved, and large-scale treatment remains energy-intensive. The textile industry uses roughly 80% of all synthetic dyes and is responsible for 70 billion tons of contaminated wastewater every year. China, India, and Bangladesh together contribute about 3.5 billion tons of this pollution annually. Synthetic dyes are a major concern for water quality, limiting sunlight and photosynthesis for aquatic plants. Microalgae, crucial to aquatic food webs, are highly affected—which can cause ecosystem breakdowns. Fish experience organ damage, reduced gestation, and toxic buildup of dyes, which can, in turn, affect animals and humans who eat them. Soil health is also compromised, as dyes disrupt beneficial microbial communities. Effects on people include heightened risks of allergies, dermatitis, and potentially cancer. The researchers conclude that no single remediation technology is adequate. Instead, multiple approaches—chemical, biological, and physical—should be combined and supported by regulatory frameworks and changes in manufacturing routines. There are also economic opportunities in recycling useful substances from wastewater. Dr. Dong Han Seo (KENTECH) and Dr. Jiuyang Lin (Chinese Academy) believe adopting new dyeing techniques and circular-economy treatment strategies can help safeguard environmental health for the future.

Jaarliks word biljoene ton afvalwater met kleurstowwe in riviere, mere en ander watersisteme vrygestel, meestal onbehandel in baie ontwikkelende lande. Hierdie navorsing, in Nature Reviews Earth & Environment gepubliseer, het wetenskaplikes van die University of Bath, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University, KENTECH in Korea en KU Leuven in België betrek. Die outeurs beklemtoon ‘n dringende behoefte aan volhoubare behandelingsmetodes soos gevorderde membraanfiltrasie, asook sterker wetgewing wat nywerhede dwing om kleurstowwe uit produkwater te verwyder voordat dit in die omgewing beland. Tot 80% van industriële afvalwater vol kleurstowwe in armer lande word nouliks behandel, en word soms selfs vir besproeiing gebruik, wat die gesondheid van plante, diere en mense direk en indirek bedreig. Dr. Ming Xie van die University of Bath sê kleurstowwe blokkeer kritieke sonlig vir mikroörganismes in die water en ontwrig die voedselketting, met onmiddellik en indirekte skade aan organismes, insluitend mense. Verwyderingstegnieke bestaan wel, maar hang af van die spesifieke kleurstof en vereis dikwels baie energie vir grootskaalse verwerking. Die tekstielbedryf verbruik sowat 80% van alle sintetiese kleurstowwe en lewer 70 miljard ton besoedelde afvalwater elke jaar. China, Indië en Bangladesj stoot saam ongeveer 3.5 miljard ton van hierdie afval elke jaar uit. Sintetiese kleurstowwe bedreig varswaterstelsels, beperk ligindringing en raak fotosintese by waterplante; mikroalge—belangrik vir akwatiese voedselwebbe—word veral benadeel, wat totale ekosisteemineenstorting kan veroorsaak. Visse ondervind orgaanskade, laer voortplanting, en giftige kleurstofopbou, wat dan weer mens en dier wat vis eet, benadeel. Grondgesondheid ly wanneer kleurstowwe goeie mikrobes ontwrig, en mense kan verhoogde risiko vir allergieë, dermatitis en selfs kanker hê. Geen enkele oplossing gaan die probleem oplos nie; ‘n verskeidenheid chemiese, biologiese en fisiese metodes moet ingespan word, waarby nuwe wetgewing en veranderde vervaardiging betrek word. Finansiële geleenthede bestaan om waardevolle stowwe uit behandelde afvalwater te herwin. Dr. Dong Han Seo (KENTECH) en Dr. Jiuyang Lin (Chinese Academy) glo nuwe kleurstoftegnieke en kringloop-ekonomie-strategieë sal help om die omgewing en mense vir die toekoms te beskerm.

article_content: Rooftop glamping has become increasingly popular in New York City. This year, visitors to the city can spend the night on the roof of AKA Central Park, or enjoy camping in a tent on one of the terraces at Manhattan's Affinia Gardens hotel, with amenities like flashlights and a kit for making s'mores included. Globally, unique camping experiences abound. Camping Vliegenbos in Amsterdam—part campsite, part art project—offers stays in a wooden cube, a suspended dome, or a garden-themed camper with artificial trees and a stuffed badger. Created by Dutch artists Annette Van Driel and Francis Nijenhuis, the campsite is in a peaceful forest and closes in late October. Otro Mundo in Sierra De Segura, Spain, provides cozy igloo-like eco-pods for up to five people. These pods are fully furnished, equipped with solar-heated showers and composting toilets, and the site is entirely powered by solar energy—ideal for hikers and mountain bikers. Carré d'étoiles in Champagne, France, features modern wooden micro-houses with glass ceilings, telescopes, and charts for stargazing. Each accommodates up to four people and includes a kitchenette, TV, and toilet. On Wilson Island, Queensland, Australia, guests can rent the entire island to stay in one of six tents with private hammocks and timber floors. Daily housekeeping is included, and Heron Island is 45 minutes away by boat. Rivendell Glamping Pods in Cornwall, UK, cater to Lord of the Rings fans with Hobbit-inspired pods featuring Tamar Valley views, beds for four, and a separate washing pod. The pods are on a working farm near the surfing town of Bude. Red Kite Tree Tents in Powys, Wales, are canvas domes suspended from trees. They are insulated and have electric lighting, with room for two adults and a wood-burning stove, suitable for year-round camping. Treebones Resort in Big Sur, California, offers the Human Nest—a large woven-wood structure by a local artist. Accessed by ladder, it accommodates two people and provides stunning views over Big Sur. Raft Camping in Limburg, Belgium, features comfortable raft tents on a river, each with a canoe for exploring. Campers bring personal bedding, while the site provides essentials like bins, gas lights, stoves, and chairs. Hüttenpalast in Berlin, Germany, offers a selection of furnished wooden huts and retro campers set inside a former factory. Notable accommodations include the circus wagon-style Heartbreaker and the artful Little Sister caravan. Maison Bulles in Pont-Saint-Esprit, France, provides transparent bubble tents with private decks, a telescope, and a star map, accommodating two people. Flashlights are provided; showers and toilets are in a separate building. The Airstream Rooftop Trailer Park in Cape Town, South Africa, is home to seven uniquely decorated Airstream trailers set on a hotel roof. Themed interiors designed by local artists include motifs like Dorothy's polka dots, Goldilocks’ cozy armchairs and cups, and more. Livingstone Lodge at Port Lympne Wild Animal Park in Kent, UK, features safari-style tents overlooking a watering hole used by zebras, giraffes, and rhinos. Two tents have four-poster beds. The lodge commemorates explorer David Livingstone’s 200th birthday. Dream Domes in New Brunswick, Canada, are semi-transparent domes with forest views, king-size beds, kitchenettes, bathrooms, and terraces with wood-fired hot tubs. They overlook Kingston Creek in the Kingston Peninsula.

article_content: Sororities at the University of Virginia have been directed to avoid attending fraternity recruitment events scheduled for Saturday, a move endorsed by their national presidents and the National Panhellenic Conference. Michelle Bower, a conference spokeswoman, confirmed the mandate to The Washington Post, while UVA Inter-Fraternity Council President Ben Gorman noted that some sororities were specifically told to steer clear of any social gatherings with fraternity members during Boys' Bid Night. This directive comes shortly after UVA lifted its suspension of Greek social activities, following agreement from both fraternities and sororities on stricter regulations. The suspension was imposed after a tumultuous 2014 at the university, which included the now-discredited Rolling Stone article detailing an alleged gang-rape at a fraternity, and the disappearance and subsequent death of 18-year-old student Hannah Graham. While the Rolling Stone article has been widely discredited and Hannah Graham’s accused killer was unrelated to Greek life, these incidents triggered renewed scrutiny and led to regulatory efforts targeting campus fraternities and sororities. At first, groups such as Kappa Alpha and Alpha Tau Omega resisted signing the new, stricter fraternal organization agreement, arguing it increased their liability. However, they ultimately agreed under pressure, enabling the resumption of standard Greek life operations. The new rules introduced at fraternity events ban kegs, require security, mandate at least three sober fraternity members at each party, and call for the presence of food and water, pre-printed guest lists, and a prohibition on pre-mixed alcoholic punches. The University has announced all Greek organizations have now signed the revised agreement, which will be reevaluated in May to determine if further adjustments are needed. Despite initial resistance, the fraternities acknowledged threats of further sanctions if they continued to abstain from signing and have stated they may seek legal remedies. For its part, UVA has sought to increase student safety by opening a police substation near The Corner, a popular area adjacent to fraternity and sorority houses. The return of rush week appeared to restore a sense of normalcy for many students, including sophomore Austin Beane, who said the new rules largely make parties safer without changing the atmosphere. Due to the unique ownership of UVA fraternity houses, which are privately owned and not university property, university leverage is somewhat limited compared to other campuses. Some fraternity representatives, like former Phi Kappa Sigma president Jakob Scheidt, claimed that existing risk-management policies were already effective and that fraternities are acutely aware of their liability for events in their houses.

Michelle Bower, 'n woordvoerder van die konferensie, het die mandaat aan The Washington Post bevestig, terwyl UVA Inter-Fraternity Council-president Ben Gorman genoem het dat sommige sororiteite spesifiek gevra is om uit te bly van enige sosiale byeenkomste met broederskapslede tydens Boys' Bid Night. Hierdie opdrag kom kort nadat UVA sy skorsing van Griekse sosiale aktiwiteite opgehef het, nadat beide broederskappe en sororiteite tot strengere regulasies ingestem het. Die skorsing is ingestel na 'n moeilike 2014 by die universiteit, wat die nou-gediskrediteerde Rolling Stone-artikel oor ‘n vermeende groepsverkragting by 'n broederskap en die verdwyning en latere dood van die 18-jarige student Hannah Graham ingesluit het. Alhoewel die Rolling Stone-artikel wyd diskrediteer is en Hannah Graham se beskuldigde moordenaar nie met die Griekse lewe verband hou nie, het hierdie insidente die universiteit tot streng nuwe regulasies teenoor broederskappe en sororiteite genoop. Aanvanklik het groepe soos Kappa Alpha en Alpha Tau Omega geweier om die nuwe, strenger broederskapsorganisasie-ooreenkoms te teken, omdat hulle gevoel het dit verhoog hul aanspreeklikheid. Hulle het egter uiteindelik onder druk ingestem, wat die hervatting van normale Griekse aktiwiteite moontlik gemaak het. Die nuwe reëls by broederskapbyeenkomste verbied vate, vereis sekuriteit, verplig minstens drie nugtere broederskaplede per partytjie, en vereis die beskikbaarheid van kos en water, voorafgedrukte gastelyse, en verbied vooraf-gemengde alkoholiese ponse. Die universiteit het aangekondig dat alle Griekse organisasies nou die hersiene ooreenkoms geteken het, wat in Mei heroorweeg sal word om verdere aanpassings te evalueer. Ten spyte van aanvanklike weerstand, het die broederskappe erken dat hulle verdere sanksies sou kon kry as hulle nie teken nie, en het aangedui dat hulle moontlik regsremedies sal soek. UVA het intussen studentveiligheid probeer verhoog deur 'n polisie substasie naby The Corner, 'n gewilde area langs sororiteite en broederskaphuise, oop te maak. Rush week se terugkeer het vir baie studente weer ‘n gevoel van normaliteit gebring, insluitend tweedejaarstudent Austin Beane, wat sê die nuwe reëls maak partytjies basies veiliger sonder om die atmosfeer te verander. As gevolg van die unieke besitstruktuur van UVA se broederskaphuise, wat privaat besit word en nie op universiteitseiendom is nie, is die universiteit se hefboomwerking beperk in vergelyking met ander kampusse. Sommige broederskapverteenwoordigers, soos die voormalige Phi Kappa Sigma-president Jakob Scheidt, het beweer dat hul bestaande risikobestuurbeleid reeds effektief is en dat broederskappe baie bewus is van hul aanspreeklikheid vir gebeure in hul huise.

article_content: Secretly recorded conversations of Russian soldiers in Ukraine reveal growing fear, trauma, and a desire to escape combat. On the front lines, '200s' indicates dead soldiers, '300s' for wounded, and '500s' for those refusing to fight. The Associated Press obtained and authenticated calls from Russian troops stationed in Kharkiv, Luhansk, and Donetsk, providing rare insight into their struggles—stories rarely aired in the West due to Russia's crackdown on honest discussion. These accounts chart the shift from professional units to an army padded with conscripts and ordinary citizens enduring tough conditions. With the war dragging on, Russia’s recent autumn draft pulled in around 130,000 new conscripts. Despite official assurances that these young men wouldn’t be sent to the Ukrainian front, many soldiers found themselves trapped, some serving out of mandatory obligation, others due to limited options. Through personal stories, soldiers discuss ethical conflicts, loss, and survival. One, known as 'The Professor,' was unexpectedly deployed after being promised a noncombat role, then struggled with the horrors of battle, civilian casualties, and getting labeled AWOL after trying to return home for his brother’s funeral. Another soldier, Artyom, describes chaotic battle conditions, insufficient supplies, and emotional exhaustion. He voices doubts about the war but feels unable to leave due to stigma and social pressure. Some, including Artyom, push on out of a sense of duty, despite the declining morale. Conscripts like Roman report facing the harshest circumstances compared to better-supported contract soldiers, dealing with shortages of supplies, poor equipment, relentless stress, and frequent losses. Their stories are marked by trauma and a persistent feeling of abandonment. Andrei, drafted from the Russian far east, condemns the high casualty rates, the fate of wounded conscripts, and the indifference shown to mobilized troops. He considers fighting a mistake and feels survival is a matter of luck. Family members of these soldiers share in the suffering, grappling with anxiety, grief, and anger at the authorities. The article stresses that, while informative, these select perspectives cannot capture the full scope of sentiment within Russia’s military.
translated_content: Geheime opnames van Russiese soldate in Oekraïne toon groeiende vrees, trauma en 'n begeerte om van die gevegte af weg te kom. Die Associated Press het oproepe bekom en geverifieer van Russiese troepe in Charkiw, Loehansk en Donetsk, wat seldsame insig gee in hul swaarkry—verhale wat min in die Weste gehoor word as gevolg van Rusland se onderdrukking van eerlike gesprekke oor die oorlog. Hierdie stories wys die skuif van professionele soldate na 'n leër gevul met dienspligtiges en gewone mense wat moeilike omstandighede trotseer. Namate die oorlog voortduur, het Rusland se nuutste herfsontplooiing ongeveer 130 000 nuwe dienspligtiges ingetrek. Ten spyte van beloftes dat hulle nie in Oekraïne sou dien nie, het baie soldate hulself vasgevang gevoel, sommige uit verpligting, ander weens 'n gebrek aan keuses. Een, bekend as 'Die Professor', is onverwags ontplooi nadat daar belowe is hy sou nie in geveg betrokke wees nie, en hy moes die gruwels van oorlog en burgerlike slagoffers verwerk. Toe hy probeer het om huis toe te gaan vir sy broer se begrafnis, is hy AWOL verklaar en staar nou regsgevolge in die gesig. ‘n Ander soldaat, Artyom, beskryf chaotiese gevegsomstandighede, min voorrade, en emosionele uitputting. Hy het twyfel oor die oorlog, maar voel vasgevang weens stigma en sosiale druk. Sommige, soos Artyom, hou vol uit pligsbesef, al daal moraal. Roman, 'n dienspligtige, vertel van die moeilikste omstandighede teenoor kontrak-soldate: tekort aan voorrade, gebrekkige toerusting, volgehoue stres en gereelde verliese. Hy glo sy deelname was 'n fout en sien sy oorlewing as blote toeval. Familielede van dié soldate ly saam, vasgevang in angs, hartseer en woede teenoor die owerhede. Die artikel beklemtoon hierdie stories gee belangrike insig, maar weerspieël nie die volle gevoel binne die Russiese weermag nie.

article_content: Old Homestead Steakhouse, located in New York’s Meatpacking District, is setting the stage for the most extravagant Thanksgiving celebration ever offered. This Thursday, the restaurant will serve a $35,000 feast for four—equivalent to $8,750 per person—making it the most expensive Thanksgiving feast on record. Remarkably, a group of four has already purchased this exclusive experience, though their identities have not been revealed.  The lavish meal centers around a turkey stuffed with seven pounds of ground Japanese Wagyu filet mignon. But it is far more than just a meal; it is billed as the ultimate American Thanksgiving experience. Guests will enjoy four grandstand seats to the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, receive a $6,000 Bloomingdale’s gift card, and take dance lessons at the Fred Astaire studios, where they’ll learn the Turkey Trot—a dance craze from the early twentieth century.  The meal itself features a decadent nine-course menu. Highlights include squab (young pigeon) stuffed with foie gras and brushed with Courvoisier L'Esprit Cognac ($5,000 per bottle), organic turkey filled with Wagyu and topped with gravy made from Château Mouton Rothschild ($1,750 per bottle), butternut squash infused with winter black truffles ($160 per pound), and whipped sweet potatoes crowned with three pounds of Royal Osetra 000 caviar ($1,600 per ounce). Creamy mashed potatoes are enhanced with Swedish moose cheese, while a cranberry-orange relish is laced with Grand Marnier. For dessert, diners are treated to poached pears soaked in bourbon and topped with pumpkin paste dusted with 24-carat gold flakes.  The beverages selection is equally opulent, featuring fine wine, champagne, and Scotch. Co-owner Marc Sherry told the New York Daily News, “Let’s face it, Thanksgiving dinner is boring, basic, and frankly, unimaginative. We’re taking all the traditional holiday fare to a creative level never seen before. It’s turkey dinner with attitude and personality.” He added, “We know it's over-the-top expensive, but Thanksgiving comes once a year. If you can splurge for this, you have a lot to be thankful for.”  For those seeking a more affordable option, Old Homestead also offers a $65 Thanksgiving package that includes turkey, stuffing, and a rare chance to watch others enjoy the one-of-a-kind $35,000 feast.  Thanksgiving is celebrated every fourth Thursday in November in the United States and on the second Monday in October in Canada.

article_content: The European Space Agency’s Ariane 6 rocket has successfully completed a key test, firing its engine in preparation for its first launch scheduled in 2024. The full results of Thursday’s ignition test, where the Vulcain 2.1 engine ran for over seven minutes, will be available after a detailed analysis by November 30. Still, the manufacturer, ArianeGroup, has already called the test a success. The hot-fire test at Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana simulated a complete launch sequence and validated the core stage’s full flight phase, according to ArianeGroup. CEO Martin Sion praised the team’s ‘real industrial feat,’ but noted that additional tests, especially on fault tolerance, are still needed before launch readiness. Pier Domenico Resta, head of engineering for the Ariane launch system, told AFP it remains to be decided if the test will need to be repeated. The ignition occurred at about 5:30 pm local time (2030 GMT) on Thursday, slightly delayed by a minor anomaly that teams quickly resolved, according to ESA. The test was initially planned for October 3 but was postponed due to hydraulic problems in the main engine’s thrust vector control system. Ariane 6’s inaugural flight, first scheduled for 2020, has been delayed multiple times due to the Covid-19 pandemic and technical challenges. Its predecessor, Ariane 5, made its final flight in July after 27 years of service. The smaller Vega C remains grounded after a launch failure in December. ESA currently lacks independent launch capability since Russia stopped space cooperation in response to sanctions. The commercial launcher market is currently led by Elon Musk’s U.S. company, SpaceX. Josef Aschbacher, ESA’s Director General, called the test a significant milestone, highlighting European engineering and noting the aim to restore autonomous access to space.
translated_content: Die Europese Ruimteagentskap se Ariane 6-vuurpyl het 'n belangrike toets suksesvol voltooi deur sy enjin te vuur ter voorbereiding op die eerste lansering wat vir 2024 geskeduleer is. Die volledige resultate van Donderdag se ontstekingstoets, waarin die Vulcain 2.1-enjin vir meer as sewe minute gewerk het, sal beskikbaar wees na 'n volledige ontleding teen 30 November. ArianeGroup, die vervaardiger, het egter reeds die toets as 'n sukses bestempel. Die warmvuurtoets by Europa se ruimtebasis in Frans-Guyana het 'n volledige lanseervolgorde gesimuleer en die kerndeel se hele vlugfase bekragtig, volgens ArianeGroup. HUB Martin Sion het die span geprys vir hul 'ware industriële prestasie', maar genoem dat bykomende toetse, veral rakende foutverdraagsaamheid, nog nodig is voordat die lansering gereed is. Pier Domenico Resta, hoof van ingenieurswese vir die Ariane-lanseerstelsel, het aan AFP gesê dit moet nog bepaal word of die toets herhaal gaan word. Die ontsteking het omstreeks 5:30 nm plaaslike tyd (2030 GMT) op Donderdag plaasgevind en was effens vertraag weens 'n geringe fout wat vinnig deur die spanne opgelos is, volgens ESA. Die toets was oorspronklik vir 3 Oktober beplan, maar is uitgestel weens hidrouliese probleme in die hoofenjin se stuwingsvektorbeheerstelsel. Ariane 6 se eerste vlug, wat aanvanklik vir 2020 beplan was, is reeds verskeie kere uitgestel as gevolg van die Covid-19-pandemie en tegniese uitdagings. Die voorganger, Ariane 5, het sy laaste vlug in Julie ná 27 jaar uitgevoer. Die kleiner Vega C is steeds aan die grond na 'n lanseer-mislukking in Desember. Die ESA het tans nie 'n onafhanklike lanseer-vermoë nie nadat Rusland ruimte-samewerking gestaak het weens sanksies. Die kommersiële lanseermark word tans gelei deur Elon Musk se Amerikaanse maatskappy, SpaceX. Josef Aschbacher, ESA se Direkteur-generaal, het die toets 'n betekenisvolle mylpaal genoem, Europese ingenieurswese geloof en beklemtoon dat Europa sy outonome toegang tot die ruimte wil herstel.

article_content: Islamabad, Pakistan (CNN) -- Three suspected drone strikes on Monday reportedly killed 21 people in northwest Pakistan's volatile tribal region near the Afghanistan border, according to two Pakistani intelligence officials. The officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media, stated that all of those killed were militants. However, witnesses told CNN affiliate GEO-TV at the scene that seven of the dead were civilians. CNN has not independently verified either account. A suspected drone targeted two alleged militant hideouts in South Waziristan, one of Pakistan's seven tribal districts bordering Afghanistan. Officials said this was the second similar series of strikes since Friday in the same area. Four missiles struck two hideouts in the village of Wacha Dana, killing nine insurgents in one attack and eight in another, according to the officials. A fifth missile hit a vehicle driven by a suspected militant near the village of Shawal, the officials added. The United States does not comment publicly on suspected drone strikes but is the only country in the region known to conduct such operations with remotely controlled drones. According to CNN's Islamabad bureau, Monday's suspected drone strike was the 31st this year, compared to 111 in all of 2010. The U.S. maintains that insurgents frequently use Pakistan's tribal regions to launch attacks into Afghanistan and resupply militants with funds and weapons.

Die amptenare, wat op voorwaarde van anonimiteit gepraat het omdat hulle nie gemagtig was om met die media te praat nie, het gesê dat al die oorledenes militante was. Getuies het egter aan CNN se affiliasie GEO-TV op die toneel gesê dat sewe van die oorledenes burgers was. CNN het nie enige van die weergawes onafhanklik bevestig nie. ’n Vermoedelike hommeltuig het twee beweerde militante skuilplekke in Suid-Waziristan, een van Pakistan se sewe stamdistrikte wat aan Afghanistan grens, geteiken. Amptenare het gesê dit was die tweede soortgelyke reeks aanvalle sedert Vrydag in dieselfde gebied. Vier missiele het twee skuilplekke in die dorp Wacha Dana getref, wat volgens die amptenare nege militantes in een aanval en agt in ’n ander doodgemaak het. ’n Vyfde missiel het ’n voertuig met ’n vermeende militante naby die dorp Shawal getref, het die amptenare bygevoeg. Die Verenigde State lewer nie publiek kommentaar op vermeende hommeltuig-aanvalle nie, maar is die enigste land in die streek wat bekend is om sulke operasies met op afstand beheerde hommeltuie uit te voer. Die VSA voer aan dat militantes gereeld Pakistan se stamgebiede gebruik om aanvalle in Afghanistan te loods en militantes met geld en wapens te voorsien.

article_content: Iryna Manukovska, Chief Marketing & Strategy Officer at XME.digital and JEVERA software solutions, discusses the growing complexity of modern IT vendor-client relationships. She recalls a recent incident where a colleague’s company lost an important client unexpectedly: 'We just received the termination notice, but they didn't even go through the project plan!' Recent research highlights these challenges. A 2023 Foundry study notes that IT sales processes now involve more sources of information—5.6 on average, rising to 6.2 for enterprise buyers. The average sales cycle is now 6.5 months, half again as long as in 2019, and buying teams average 25 members compared to 16 in 2017. According to Gartner, software development clients typically go through 17 stages of validation and consensus before making a decision. Failing to address clients’ needs or provide necessary information at critical stages can cost businesses valuable clients. Adapting to these complex decision-making environments means building sophisticated, agile vendor-client relationships. The following strategies can help foster stronger, lasting partnerships: 1. Set boundaries and manage expectations. Small or newer companies sometimes overpromise to big clients. Establishing clear boundaries and communicating honestly helps prevent burnout and disappointment. 2. Balance company and client interests. Rigid adherence to internal agreements may harm long-term relationships. Develop soft skills, empathy, and active listening within your team. 3. Maintain responsive project management. Flexibility is crucial for navigating the unpredictable, fast-changing VUCA (volatility, uncertainty, complexity, ambiguity) market. 4. Align with client KPIs. Delivering quality work doesn’t matter if it doesn’t support the client’s key performance indicators. 5. Focus on clients’ business goals. Projects that don’t help achieve business objectives risk termination. Learn and support their quarterly and yearly targets. 6. Be consistently reliable. Reliability and delivering on promises build trust over time. 7. Avoid organizational chaos. Organized, transparent management reassures clients and upholds trust. 8. Build genuine personal connections. Real business value comes from authentic human relationships, as noted by Erin Meyer in 'Culture Map'. 9. Show appreciation. Practicing gratitude strengthens partnerships. Psychologist Robert Cialdini emphasizes the power of reciprocity. Ultimately, client relations can either drive or hinder your business. Prioritize mutual value and professionalism to build successful, sustainable client partnerships. The article also mentions the Forbes Communications Council as an elite, invitation-only community for communications executives.
translated_content: Iryna Manukovska, Hoof van Bemarking en Strategie by XME.digital en JEVERA sagteware-oplossings, bespreek die groeiende kompleksiteit van moderne IT-verskaffer-en-kliëntverhoudings. Sy haal 'n onlangse insident aan waar 'n kollega se maatskappy onverwags 'n belangrike kliënt verloor het: 'Ons het so pas die beëindigingskennisgewing ontvang, maar hulle het nie eens die projekplan nagegaan nie!' Onlangse navorsing beklemtoon hierdie uitdagings. Die 2023 Foundry-studie wys dat IT-verkoopprosesse nou meer inligtingsbronne gebruik – gemiddeld 5.6, selfs 6.2 vir ondernemingskliënte. Die gemiddelde verkoopsiklus is nou 6.5 maande lank, 50% langer as in 2019, en aankoopspanne bestaan gemiddeld uit 25 lede teenoor 16 in 2017. Gartner meld dat sagteware-ontwikkelingskliënte gemiddeld deur 17 stadiums van validering en konsensus gaan voordat hul 'n besluit neem. As maatskappye kliënte se behoeftes ignoreer of nie noodsaaklike inligting betyds verskaf nie, kan hulle waardevolle kliënte verloor. Om by hierdie ingewikkelde besluitneming aan te pas, moet kliënt-verskafferverhoudings meer gesofistikeerd en aanpasbaar wees. Hier is strategieë om sterker, langer vennootskappe te vestig: 1. Stel grense en bestuur verwagtinge. Klein of nuwe maatskappye belowe soms te veel aan groot kliënte. Duidelike grense en eerlike kommunikasie voorkom uitbranding en teleurstelling. 2. Balans tussen maatskappy- en kliëntbelange. Om vas te klou aan interne ooreenkomste kan verhoudings skaad. Ontwikkel sagte vaardighede, empatie en aktiewe luister binne die span. 3. Hou projekbestuur responsief. Buigsaamheid is noodsaaklik vir die dinamiese, onvoorspelbare VUCA (volatiliteit, onsekerheid, kompleksiteit, dubbelsinnigheid) wêreld. 4. Belyn jou werk met kliënt se KPIs. Goeie aflewering beteken min as jy nie kernprestasie-aanwysers aanraak nie. 5. Hou rekening met kliënt se besigheidsdoelwitte. Projekte wat nie aan die groter doelwitte voldoen nie, loop die risiko om beëindig te word. Verstaan en ondersteun hul kwartaallikse en jaarlikse doelwitte. 6. Bou vertroue deur betroubaarheid. Konsekwentheid en nakoming van beloftes kweek vertroue. 7. Vermy wanorde in jou bestuur. Deursigtige, georganiseerde prosesse stel kliënte gerus. 8. Bou ware persoonlike verhoudings. Werklike waarde lê in outentieke menslike verbinding, soos Erin Meyer in 'Culture Map' beskryf. 9. Wys opregte waardering. Dankbaarheid versterk vennootskappe. Sielkundige Robert Cialdini beklemtoon die belangrikheid van wedersydse hulp. Kliëntverhoudings kan jou besigheid maak of breek. Fokus op gesamentlike waarde en professionaliteit om volhoubare vennootskappe te bou. Die artikel verwys ook na die Forbes Communications Council as 'n eksklusiewe, uitnodiging-alleen netwerk vir uitvoerende lede in kommunikasie.

article_content: Real Sociedad captain Xabi Prieto revealed he immediately spoke to Mikel Arteta after learning David Moyes would become the club's new manager. The former Manchester United boss joined the Basque team after Jagoba Arrasate's departure, but Moyes had yet to oversee a match at that point. Moyes signed Arteta from Sociedad to Everton in 2005, and the two spent six years working together on Merseyside. article_content: Joseph Green Brown, 62, who was formerly cleared from Florida's death row due to a wrongful conviction, has been arrested in North Carolina on suspicion of murdering his wife, Mamie Caldwell Brown. Mamie, 71, and Brown’s wife for twenty years, was found dead in her apartment last Thursday. Police report that she suffered traumatic injuries and was declared dead on the spot. Brown was apprehended at a hotel in Charleston, South Carolina, and may again face the death penalty. After his 1987 release, Brown—also known as Shabaka—became a vocal opponent of the death penalty, sharing his experience and pushing for justice reform, even addressing a Congressional subcommittee. His advocacy moved several legal professionals, including Connecticut’s Richard Blumenthal (now a senator), to reconsider their stance on capital punishment. The NAACP provided significant financial assistance for Brown’s defense, considering his earlier conviction a case of racial injustice. Brown was initially convicted in 1974 for the rape and murder of Earlene Treva Barksdale, a Florida store owner. It was later revealed that prosecution presented knowingly false testimony, including that of a witness acting under a deal. After 13 years on death row, he was freed in 1987 just before his scheduled execution. Family members of both Brown and his wife have expressed shock at recent events, describing Brown as someone who was candid about his past and strived to support others. If convicted in North Carolina, Brown could receive another death sentence, although no executions have been carried out in the state since 2006, when Samuel Flippen was executed.

article_content: A good book carries influence. When thoughtfully chosen as a gift, it can bring added joy—especially during the holidays, which are a perfect time to select that ideal coffee table book for friends or family. This season offers a wide selection, including:  “Slim Aarons: The Essential Collection,” photography by Slim Aarons and text by Shawn Waldron. Slim Aarons, a World War II photographer who later captured the lifestyles of the wealthy in places like Palm Beach and Gstaad, also photographed war orphans in Rome and tailgaters in South Carolina. This comprehensive collection features detailed text and over 100 previously unpublished photos. Getty Images acquired his archive in 1997. Abrams. $175.  “TheChristmasBook,” from the editors of Phaidon with essays by David Trigg, Sam Bilton, and Dolph Gotelli. This book explores Christmas through festive cultural artifacts, including a history of pudding charms, a beaded angel by the Woza Moya collective in South Africa, Picasso’s Dove of Peace, and the Lego Santa’s Visit set. $49.95.  “Lena Horne: Goddess Reclaimed,” by Donald Bogle. Film historian Donald Bogle provides a detailed biography of Lena Horne, covering her childhood, beginning at the Cotton Club, activism for racial justice, and the challenges she faced. The book includes many photographs. Running Press. $35.  “The Color of Dance,” by TaKiyah Wallace-McMillian. Photographer TaKiyah Wallace-McMillian, known for 'Brown Girls Do Ballet' on Instagram, presents an inspiring collection of images celebrating young ballet dancers, including portraits and personal reflections. One dancer, Kailyn Scales, shares: “I am small but mighty. When I dance, I feel powerful.” Black Dog & Leventhal. $30.  “Yellowstone: The Official Dutton Ranch Family Cookbook,” by Chef Gabriel “Gator” Guilbeau with Kim Laidlaw. Guilbeau, the on-set caterer and actor who played the family cook on the show 'Yellowstone,' presents over 55 recipes featured on screen, some with Cajun influences. Taylor Sheridan, the show’s creator, is a fan. Insight Editions. $34.99.  “Dressing the Part: Television's Most Stylish Shows,” by Hal Rubenstein. Fashion expert Hal Rubenstein analyzes the cultural importance of style in 50 major TV shows. Highlights include Mary Tyler Moore’s capri pants in 'The Dick Van Dyke Show,' which influenced real-world fashion trends. HarperCollins. $40.  “Birding for a Better World,” by Molly Adams and Sydney Golden Anderson. This helpful introduction to birdwatching covers basic terms, equipment, safety, and inclusive practices. Includes journal prompts and blank pages for observations. Princeton Architectural Press. $22.95.  “Thom Browne,” by Thom Browne and Andrew Bolton. Celebrating the 20th anniversary of Browne’s fashion brand, this book features photographs by Johnny Dufort, curated by Bolton, and images from Browne’s fashion shows. Phaidon. $150.  “The New Brownies’ Book: A Love Letter to Black Families,” by Karida L. Brown and Charly Palmer. Inspired by W.E.B. Du Bois’s original magazine, this collection brings together poetry, stories, new works, and art to inspire Black youth. Chronicle Books. $40.  “Mother Tongue: The Surprising History of Women’s Words,” by Jenni Nuttall. Nuttall, an English lecturer at Exeter College, dives into how language shapes the female experience, finding both sexism and resistance in historical texts. Viking. $29.  “Vanity Fair: Oscar Night Sessions,” photographs by Mark Seliger. For over ten years, Mark Seliger has photographed celebrities at the Vanity Fair Oscar party. The collection includes portraits of famous couples, stars who have passed away, and iconic moments. Abrams. $80.  “Art in Flower,” by Lindsey Taylor. From her Flower School column at The Wall Street Journal, Taylor presents 40 floral arrangements inspired by various artworks, sharing her creative process and tips on foraging. Monacelli. $60.  “Milton Glaser: Pop,” by Steven Heller, Mirko Ilić, and Beth Kleber. A comprehensive look at Milton Glaser—the designer of the I (Heart) New York logo—showcasing his work from the 1960s and 70s, including more than 1,100 color images. Monacelli. $65.  “LL Cool J Presents the Streets Win,” by LL Cool J, Vikki Tobak, and Alec Banks. A visually rich tribute to 50 years of hip-hop, featuring stories and rare images from influential artists like Salt-N-Pepa, Public Enemy, Run-D.M.C., and Mary J. Blige. Rizzoli New York. $55. article_content: Juliet Clarke, aged 31, avoided prison after admitting to defrauding former boyfriends by telling elaborate lies, including claims of pregnancy, terminal illness, and even her own death. Over a period between October and December 2011, Clarke deceived her partners, taking around £7,000, which she then spent on luxuries such as hair extensions, hotels, and holidays. From Launceston in Cornwall, Clarke first convinced Ricky Yelland that she had terminal cancer and was expecting a large inheritance. Yelland gave Clarke access to his bank account, but after they separated, he discovered over £2,500 had been used without his consent. When Yelland confronted her, Clarke pretended to be her own father in text messages, claiming she had passed away and discussing funeral arrangements. Yelland became suspicious and found evidence online that Clarke was alive and in a new relationship. Clarke’s second victim, Wayne Teare, was told she had serious illnesses and, when attempting to end their relationship, was sent fake evidence of pregnancy with twins. Teare and his mother were convinced, with the latter buying baby items, but it was later revealed that Clarke had never been pregnant and had previously been sterilised. At Plymouth Crown Court, Judge Paul Darlow suspended Clarke’s ten-month prison sentence for two years, stating her lies resulted from a desire for attention. Clarke pleaded guilty to three counts of fraud by false representation and asked for four similar offences to be considered. As part of her sentence, she will remain under probation supervision and must complete an education and training program.

Tussen Oktober en Desember 2011 het Clarke haar vennote mislei om sowat £7,000 te bekom, wat sy aan luukshede soos haarverlengings, hotelle en vakansies bestee het.
