article_content: Every action taken during a job transition—whether starting, leaving, or managing both—shapes perceptions about you. Integrity is demonstrated by consistency, though each scenario may require its own approach. Selecting the right way to exit a job matters. How you manage your personal brand can strengthen your reputation and preserve relationships for years to come. Especially if your departure is unexpected, pause for a moment, get expert advice, and plan your next move. Job departures happen for many reasons: retirement, contracts ending, mergers, or sudden resignation. If your exit surprises others, it may trigger emotional responses from your employer, who may even counteroffer. It’s generally wise not to accept such counteroffers. If you’re laid off or your job ends involuntarily, remember you control your reaction—not the event. Avoid immediate decisions or signed agreements. Consulting an advisor or employment lawyer can help you achieve the best results. Transitions are brief stages that lead to new opportunities. Consider your desired future, the impression you wish to leave, and your longer-term priorities—like advancing in your career or choosing a new lifestyle. Focus on protecting relationships and sustaining your reputation, rather than dwelling on any negative experiences. Effectively bridge the gap between your current circumstances and future objectives by consistently communicating your core values and tailoring your approach to each context. The strength of your relationships is lasting. How you interact with others now will influence your personal and professional paths long into the future. Treat everyone with enough respect so they’ll advocate for you when needed. To summarize: understand your context, focus on your future, and if you’re not leaving by choice, don’t act in haste. Seek counsel, weigh your options, and proceed thoughtfully to protect your interests.

As ander nie jou vertrek sien kom nie, kan dit emosionele reaksies uitlok—selfs teenaanbiedinge. Die algemene advies is om nie daardie teenaanbiedings te aanvaar nie. article_content: The Indian rupee ended lower on Tuesday, moving in line with other Asian currencies, as investors waited for comments from senior US Federal Reserve officials for new market cues. The rupee closed at 83.2575 per dollar, down from 83.2150 in the previous session. Trading stayed within a narrow three-paise range. Traders noted the rupee has remained between 83 and 83.30 for several weeks, with regular intervention from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Amit Pabari, managing director at CR Forex, said any rise in the rupee is quickly bought by local oil companies and importers, keeping it within the 'comfort zone' of 83.20–83.30. The competition between dollar buyers and the RBI continues. Asian currencies fell between 0.1% and 0.9% as the dollar index recovered to 105.57 after hitting a one-month low on Monday. Last week, the Federal Reserve left key interest rates unchanged and struck a dovish tone. Investors are watching speeches from several Fed policymakers this week, including Chair Jerome Powell on Wednesday and Thursday, to understand the outlook for interest rates. Expectations for a December Fed rate hike have dropped to 7%, down from 20% last week. Meanwhile, rupee far forward premiums fell on Tuesday, with the one-year implied yield down to 1.61%, a decrease of three basis points. Arnob Biswas, head of foreign exchange research at SMC Global Securities, pointed out that the rupee is struggling to benefit from the weaker dollar because of lower forward premiums. Separately, India is expediting all necessary approvals for Tesla's entry by January 2024, involving multiple government departments. Retailers report that luxury item sales are booming ahead of Diwali, a sign of a strong economy. However, salary increases for IT professionals changing jobs have nearly halved from last year, following reduced hiring by major IT exporters. article_content: Men experiencing erectile dysfunction may benefit from following a Mediterranean diet, according to Greek cardiologist Dr. Athanasios Angelis. Consuming foods like fish, salads, olive oil, and enjoying two or three small glasses of wine daily could improve vascular health, especially the narrow blood vessels essential for erectile function. Dr. Angelis, an expert on erectile dysfunction at Hippokration Hospital in Athens, emphasized that the Mediterranean diet is linked to longevity, overall wellbeing, and reduced risk of cancer and cardiovascular disease. He explained that difficulties with erections could signal broader health issues, as penile blood vessels are particularly sensitive to changes in vascular health. He recommended adopting a healthy diet and increasing exercise to help reverse moderate erectile dysfunction. In some cases, these changes may be so effective that men might no longer need medication, such as Viagra. Dr. Angelis advised eating plenty of cereals, fruits, vegetables, salads, nuts, olive oil, fish, and poultry, while limiting red meat to once per week and avoiding kebabs. His research was presented at a meeting of the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging in Vienna.

Dr. Angelis, 'n spesialis in erektiele disfunksie by die Hippokration-hospitaal in Athene, beklemtoon die Mediterreense dieet hou verband met 'n langer lewe, goeie gesondheid en 'n laer risiko vir kanker en hart- en vaatkwale. Sy navorsing is voorgestel by 'n byeenkoms van die Europese Vereniging vir Kardiovaskulêre Beelding in Wene.

article_content: Picture a band where the guitarist boasts 78 fingers, the drummer wields 22 arms, and the keyboardist hits notes with beams of green lasers. This is Z-Machines, a pioneering robot band engineered by experts at the University of Tokyo. Their music, which shifts between orchestral arrangements and experimental rock, could easily be mistaken for a human performance until you see the high-tech musicians on stage. March—the immense robot guitarist—commands attention as its dozens of fingers fly over illuminated strings. Ashura, the remarkable drummer, brings unparalleled speed with its multitude of arms. Completing the trio is Cosmo, whose laser accuracy at the keyboard is as mesmerizing as it is efficient. Designer Kenjiro Matsuo notes that these machines require about 300 kilowatts of power, well beyond everyday needs. The compositions, crafted by noted British artist Squarepusher (Tom Jenkinson), push musical boundaries by using the robots’ unique abilities. During their Tokyo debut, Z-Machines played to an enthusiastic crowd, the music changing tempo in response to the audience’s cheers and energy. The band’s EP includes tracks like 'Sad Robot Goes Funny,' raising an intriguing question: Can robots create music that resonates emotionally with humans? Jenkinson, who has long experimented with electronic sound, is captivated by how these robots blur the line between efficiency and artistic expression. For him, the collaboration is as much an experiment in creativity as it is an exploration of technology’s possibilities. While the robots surpass human musicians in speed—like playing notes with millisecond precision—they face different limits, such as a lack of nuanced amplification. Despite these differences, each performance is still underpinned by human creativity, reflecting a partnership between person and machine.

article_content: Attorneys representing George Zimmerman, who was acquitted in Florida for the shooting death of Trayvon Martin, plan to petition the state for reimbursement of at least $200,000 in fees incurred during the trial. According to Florida law, a defendant found not guilty may be repaid for certain costs if a court clerk or judge approves. Eligible expenses include expert witnesses, travel, and transcripts, while attorney fees are not covered. Mark O'Mara, Zimmerman's primary lawyer, indicated the reimbursement request could reach $300,000, but he anticipates they will receive much less due to restrictive legal precedents. Similar procedures are routine in Florida; the defense for Casey Anthony submitted a comparable claim after her 2011 acquittal. O'Mara stated that the biggest expense during Zimmerman's defense was for voice analysis experts, costing between $75,000 and $100,000. Transcript expenses totaled roughly $20,000. He clarified that neither his legal fees—estimated at around $1 million—nor those of co-counsel Don West or other team members qualify for reimbursement under state rules. In total, the defense cost about $2 million, while O'Mara reports not having received payment for his work. He has an agreement with Zimmerman to be compensated should Zimmerman gain future wealth. Currently unemployed, Zimmerman could still generate income by writing a book or through a defamation lawsuit against NBC News, which aired a misleadingly edited version of his call to police dispatchers on February 26, 2012—the night of Trayvon Martin's death. Zimmerman was acquitted by a six-member jury in July. The case triggered significant national debate about race and the 'stand your ground' law in Florida. Trayvon Martin, an unarmed 17-year-old black teenager, was fatally shot after Zimmerman, a neighborhood watch volunteer who is Hispanic, called police to report Martin, followed him, and ultimately claimed to have shot in self-defense during an altercation. Prosecutors alleged Zimmerman targeted Martin because of his race. The case remains a catalyst for broader discussions on race and justice in America.

article_content: Anne and Clifford Arnall raised six children on their farm near Ravenscrag, Saskatchewan, but endured devastating loss when three sons died in separate accidents over six years. In 2008, their 14-year-old son Blake was killed in an ATV accident. Six years later, brothers Sean and Lyndon died together in a tractor accident. The repeated tragedies changed the family's future—Clifford left the farm for construction work five hours away and isn't sure he'll return. Anne drives those five hours weekly to see him, describing her grief as a box she opens briefly each day. She rejects criticism over her sons working on the farm, saying she wanted them to live active lives. With three adult children moved away and no one left on the farm, Anne admits to times of loneliness, but manages her emotions with her daily ritual.

In 2008 is hul 14-jarige seun Blake in ’n vierwielmotorfietsongeluk dood. Ses jaar later het die broers Sean en Lyndon saam in ’n trekkerongeluk gesterf. Die opeenvolgende tragedies het die gesin se toekoms verander—Clifford het die plaas verlaat om konstruksiewerk vyf uur ver te doen, en is onseker of hy ooit sal terugkom. Anne ry dié vyf uur elke week om hom te besoek, en beskryf haar rou as ’n boks wat sy elke dag kortliks oopmaak. Sy verwerp kritiek oor haar seuns se plaaswerk en sê sy wou hê hulle moes aktief grootword. Met drie groot kinders wat weggetrek het en niemand oor op die plaas nie, erken Anne sy ervaar tye van eensaamheid, maar hanteer haar emosies met haar daaglikse roetine.

article_content: Jay Timmons, President and CEO of the National Association of Manufacturers (NAM), shared insights from his nearly 13 years of leadership in a recent interview with Rhett Buttle. Timmons highlighted the enduring importance of manufacturing in the U.S. economy, the positive impact of recent federal investments, the value of bipartisan policymaking, the challenges posed by regulatory burdens, and the urgent need for skilled workers. He described manufacturing’s critical role during the COVID-19 pandemic when the industry rapidly shifted to produce essential goods, secured essential status for factories, and launched initiatives to encourage public health practices. Timmons noted that manufacturing employment in the U.S. is at a decade-high, with federal programs like the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and the CHIPS and Science Act offering significant growth opportunities. Nonetheless, he cautioned that complex federal regulations are inhibiting investment and job growth, costing small manufacturers $50,000 per employee annually. The NAM and the Manufacturing Institute (MI) spearhead workforce initiatives, such as Creators Wanted and FAME, to equip workers for a tech-driven industry, utilizing training in AI, robotics, and digital tools. Timmons also stressed the importance of apprenticeships, technical education, and immigration reform in addressing workforce needs. Following January 6, 2021, Timmons and NAM affirmed their support for democratic institutions, linking manufacturing's strength to the health of democracy. NAM has supported Ukraine and continues to encourage solid transatlantic partnerships and global democratic ideals. Timmons concluded by describing manufacturing as a unifying force for both economic and societal advancement, urging policymakers to prioritize solutions that strengthen U.S. competitiveness.

article_content: Kim Warren, a 44-year-old principal at Deerfield Elementary School in Novi, Michigan, has been suspended after being arrested for driving under the influence on school property. Police found her in her car with an open bottle of vodka and determined her blood alcohol content was more than twice the legal limit. Two witnesses called police after noticing Warren driving erratically before pulling into the school parking lot. She failed a roadside sobriety test and was subsequently handcuffed and placed in a patrol car. A police video showed her slipping out of her handcuffs and handing them to the officer, who instructed her not to throw them out the window. Novi Police Chief David Molloy acknowledged the handcuffs were not correctly applied, stressing the importance of proper restraint. Warren has been charged with having high blood alcohol content, referred to as 'super drunk', as well as possessing open intoxicants in a motor vehicle. She has not commented on the incident. The school district's superintendent stated Warren was deeply regretful and understood the seriousness of her actions, also expressing frustration about the impact on the school community.

article_content: Dozens of clinics have admitted that breast implants they provided to women have ruptured, but Health Secretary Andrew Lansley revealed that much of the data submitted is incomplete. Clinics have been given until Friday to supply full information on the implants, with results to be published next week. Speaking on BBC Breakfast, Lansley said: 'Some private providers had not provided any data at all, many had, some had submitted data that looks thorough, while others' submissions are of poor quality.' There is growing concern over the safety of cheaply made implants, which used low-grade industrial silicone intended for mattresses. At least 50 clinics have reported ruptured, degraded, or damaged implants made by the French company PIP to the medical regulator since Friday. The total number of women with ruptured implants is unknown, but even conservative estimates suggest it could be as high as 1,000. However, the government says there is no need for the preventative removal of all implants. Consultant plastic surgeon Fazel Fatah, on the panel investigating the issue, said there are no definitive UK figures for what proportion of devices have ruptured. As president of the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons, he said the issue is not just rupture rates, but that the silicone in these implants is not medical grade. Andrew Lansley has ordered clinics to provide data on the implants, while Shadow Health Secretary Andy Burnham criticized the cosmetic surgery industry for poor after-care when things go wrong. Surgeons can typically remove most breast implants in about an hour, going in through the original scar under the breast. All implants form a scar capsule inside, which can be removed along with the implant. If an implant ruptures, further scar tissue can build up, making removal more difficult and causing the breast to firm up. Most women have no symptoms when a silicone breast implant ruptures, but leaking gel can cause pain and affect the breast’s shape. The gel can lead to inflammation and more scar tissue. A ruptured implant can be confirmed by mammogram, ultrasound, CT scan, or MRI. Consultant plastic surgeon Douglas McGeorge said any leaked material should also be removed. These operations carry risks, including from anesthesia and infection, and recovery is usually about two weeks. "These implants are not suitable for use in humans. They are substandard and defective. The government must make sure affected women are not left in the middle of arguments over who pays for removal," said a medical expert. "With high anxiety levels, there should be clear guidance on the right course of action." Nigel Mercer, former BAAPS president, suggested it would be sensible for the government to recommend removal of the implants, with funding to be sorted out later. Labour said the public has been 'left in the dark' and called for the £2.3 billion private cosmetic surgery industry, carrying out 95% of procedures, to take responsibility. Shadow Health Secretary Andy Burnham argued that some companies are good at selling and making money, but less effective with after-care when complications arise. The trade body for private clinics, Independent Healthcare Advisory Services, said it would be irresponsible to remove all implants, as surgery carries risks and clinics cannot afford the expense. Their audit suggests the actual rupture rate is between 1% and 2%, considered within the industry standard. As many as 50,000 women in the UK, including breast cancer survivors, have these fragile implants. Even at a 2% failure rate, there could be up to 1,000 ruptures. Figures from the private chain Transform suggested a 7% rupture rate, but this was based on just seven cases from 108 patients, too small a sample for firm conclusions. In France, between 5% and 10% of implants have ruptured. The government will pay for removal from 30,000 women, and health minister Xavier Bertrand has ordered an investigation into the contaminated implants.

Klinieke het tot Vrydag kans om volledige inligting oor die inplantate te gee en die resultate sal volgende week gepubliseer word. As president van die British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons sê hy die saak is nie net oor skeuringsyfers nie, maar die silikon is nie van mediese gehalte nie. Konsultant-plastiese chirurg Douglas McGeorge sê enige lekkasie moet ook verwyder word. Hierdie operasies hou risiko's in soos narkose en infeksie, en herstel neem tipies sowat twee weke. Die regering moet sorg dat vroue nie gevang sit in argumente oor wie moet betaal vir verwydering nie," het ’n mediese kenner gesê. Arbeid het gesê die publiek is 'in die duister gehou' en eis dat die £2,3 miljard privaat kosmetiese chirurgiebedryf, verantwoordelik vir 95% van prosedures, verantwoordelikheid neem. Skadugesondheidssekretaris Andy Burnham sê maatskappye is goed met verkope en geld maak, maar nie met naverzorging as daar probleme opduik nie. Die handelsliggaam vir privaat klinieke, Independent Healthcare Advisory Services, sê dit sal onverantwoordelik wees om alle inplantate te verwyder omdat operasies risiko’s inhou en klinieke nie die koste kan dra nie. Hul oudit toon die ware skeuringskoers is tussen 1% en 2%, wat as binne die bedryfsnorm beskou word. Soveel as 50,000 vroue in die VK, insluitend borskanker-oorlewendes, het hierdie brose inplantate. Selfs by 2% mislukking kan daar tot 1,000 skeurings wees. Syfers van Transform, ’n private ketting, dui op ’n 7% skeuringskoers, maar dit is gebaseer op slegs sewe gevalle uit 108 pasiënte – te klein vir vaste afleidings. In Frankryk het 5% tot 10% van inplantate geskeur. Die regering betaal vir die verwydering van 30,000 vroue se inplantate, en gesondheidsminister Xavier Bertrand het ’n ondersoek na die besmette inplantate beveel.

article_content: ABU DHABI: Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE's Minister of Foreign Affairs, met with Annalena Baerbock, Germany’s Federal Minister for Foreign Affairs, to discuss current developments in the Middle East, focusing on their security and humanitarian impacts. They also considered regional and international actions to deliver humanitarian aid to civilians in a safe and sustainable way that addresses urgent needs and eases suffering. Sheikh Abdullah highlighted the importance of protecting civilians and enhancing humanitarian responses for the people in Gaza. He also emphasized the need for stronger global cooperation to combat extremism, tension, and violence in the region. The meeting included talks on advancing bilateral cooperation between the UAE and Germany as part of their comprehensive strategic partnership. Specific sectors reviewed included economic, trade, investment, food security, science, advanced technology, and climate. These discussions come ahead of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP28), set to be held at Expo City Dubai from November 30 to December 12. Sheikh Abdullah welcomed Baerbock’s visit, noting both countries' commitment to promoting their partnership in support of shared development goals. Mariam bint Mohammed Almheiri, the UAE’s Minister of Climate Change and the Environment, also attended the meeting.

article_content:
The debate over what to call the world's most popular sport—football or soccer—remains unresolved. While FIFA, the sport’s global governing body, uses 'football' in its official title, the backstory is more nuanced. The word 'soccer' actually has British roots, emerging as slang for 'association football' in England during the 1880s. Charles Wreford-Brown, a former England captain, is often credited with inventing the term 'soccer' to distinguish the game from rugby football, which was nicknamed 'rugger.'

Countries where other football games are played—such as American and Australian football—use 'soccer' for clarity. In fact, the United States originally called the sport football and even named its organizing body the United States of America Football Association in 1913. Later, the word 'soccer' was adopted, and today the group is called the United States Soccer Federation. Australia’s national soccer team, known as the 'Socceroos,' shows no sign of updating its famous nickname—calling them the 'Footyroos' just wouldn’t have the same effect.

Despite the prominence of 'football' in Britain, the term 'soccer' is still widely recognized, as evidenced by shows like 'Soccer Saturday.' Even FIFA itself isn’t fixed on one term: during the South Africa World Cup, the dedicated fan gathering spot was named 'Soccer City.' The continued use of both names worldwide suggests the debate is far from over. Now, it’s your turn—what do you prefer, football or soccer? Tell us your thoughts, and you can even join the discussion with a poll or submit your own videos and photos.

Die woord 'sokker' kom oorspronklik uit Engeland in die 1880’s as 'n bynaam vir 'assosiasievoetbal.' Charles Wreford-Brown, ’n vroeë Engeland-kaptein, het blykbaar die term geskep om dit van rugbyvoetbal ('rugger') te onderskei.

In lande waar ander soorte voetbal bestaan, soos Amerika en Australië, word 'sokker' gebruik om duidelikheid te gee. article_content: Nigeria is in the midst of a major diphtheria outbreak, with close to 17,000 suspected cases and about 600 deaths, reports Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), also known as Doctors Without Borders. The organization highlights especially low vaccination rates among patients—around 70% of those treated in Kano state facilities had not completed their vaccinations. To counter this, a vaccination campaign led by Nigeria's agencies, WHO, and UNICEF has started and is being implemented in three stages across 14 states such as Kano, Katsina, Bauchi, and Borno. Nevertheless, overall immunization in the North-West is still troublingly low, with Sokoto at 6%, Zamfara at 10%, and Katsina at 18%, compared to the national 36% average. Similarly, in Maiduguri, Borno state, only 15% of children receiving diphtheria care at MSF’s hospital were fully immunized. MSF is advocating for not just emergency vaccination drives, but also for ongoing, widespread immunization programs across Nigeria to help prevent outbreaks of diphtheria and other preventable diseases like measles, polio, and tetanus. They are appealing to international organizations and donors—such as GAVI and the Africa CDC—to fund both short-term responses and sustainable vaccination infrastructure, especially as neighboring countries are also experiencing diphtheria cases. Since early 2023, MSF has opened and supported treatment centers in Kano with 146 beds, a 20-bed unit in Maiduguri treating 448 patients, and one at Ganjuwa Hospital in Bauchi managing 173 cases. Their teams work alongside local health authorities to promote vaccination, support other hospitals, and increase public awareness in affected regions.

article_content: Recent studies indicate that walking just one mile a day may greatly reduce the risk of death for cancer patients. Research backed by Macmillan Cancer Support, the Ramblers, and Walking for Health demonstrates that this straightforward activity has substantial health benefits. Patients with breast or prostate cancer could lower their chance of dying by up to 40% through regular exercise, such as moderate-paced walking. Meanwhile, those with bowel cancer could see their risk cut in half by increasing their daily walking distance to two miles. A moderate walking speed—about 3 miles per hour—translates to twenty minutes for each mile, making it easily incorporated into daily life. The evidence also suggests that physical activity can help reduce common cancer treatment side effects, including swelling, anxiety, depression, fatigue, mobility challenges, and weight fluctuations. According to Macmillan Cancer Support, approximately 1.6 million out of the 2 million people living with cancer in the UK are not as physically active as guidelines recommend. Macmillan’s CEO, Ciarán Devane, has called for exercise to become a routine aspect of cancer recovery, stating that walking can be life-saving. Sandra Sayce, a cancer survivor from Middlesex, provides a real-life example: After her melanoma treatment left her struggling to walk even short distances, joining a community walking group in 2011 gave her the boost she needed to restart physical activity. She credits walking with helping her feel more energetic and improving her mood. Although the underlying reasons for these health improvements are still being researched, experts propose that exercise may do more than support weight control. It could also affect hormone levels, such as breaking down oestrogen into compounds that lower cancer risk. The information is drawn from Macmillan Cancer Support’s Move More report, which reviews international evidence. Following recommended physical activity (at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise per week) is strongly linked to better outcomes, yet only about 36% of British women achieve this target. Benedict Southworth of the Ramblers notes that even short, regular walks can significantly improve recovery and well-being for cancer patients and others with serious health concerns. Walking for Health organizes supportive group walks, led by experienced guides, to help people regain fitness and confidence. Both organizations encourage health professionals to include walking in standard recovery advice.

Pasiënte met bors- of prostaatkanker kan hul sterfterisiko tot 40% verminder deur gereeld te stap teen 'n matige tempo. Mense met dikdermkanker kan hul risiko met die helfte verminder deur twee myl per dag te loop. article_content: In the last year, falling demand has led to steep price drops for SSDs, making it an ideal time to buy portable drives. Crucial, which is owned by Micron, is one of only two brands (along with Samsung) that makes all of its SSD hardware in-house—giving it a clear competitive edge. The 4TB version of Crucial's X9 Pro is currently on sale for $182 for Black Friday. Lower storage options include the 1TB at $59 and 2TB at $109, but the 4TB gives the best price per terabyte. The X9 Pro merges fast speeds with solid durability. It can withstand drops up to 7.5 feet, has IP55 protection against dust and water, and features built-in 256-bit AES encryption. It uses USB 3.2 Gen 2 to ensure rapid data transfer, and the box comes with a USB-C to USB-C cable. However, a USB-A cable isn’t included, though USB-C fits most current devices. Rated at 1,050MB/s for both reading and writing, the X9 Pro achieved speeds of 980MB/s read and 906MB/s write in real-world tests—ranking it among the fastest portable SSDs today. Plus, it comes backed by a five-year warranty. When considering price per TB, the 4TB drive breaks down to $45.50 per terabyte, making it more economical than the 1TB and 2TB variants. Overall, the Crucial X9 Pro provides dependable, high-speed storage that matches Samsung’s performance at a lower price.

article_content: According to the Bank of America Trends in Consumer Mobility report released Monday, a survey of 1,000 adults found that only 87% considered deodorant important, while 93% considered their smartphone important. For toothbrushes, 91% of respondents rated them as important. The report highlights a generational difference: older adults consider deodorant and smartphones to have equal importance in their daily lives, with toothbrushes ranking highest at 95%. Some experts believe that younger adults, particularly millennials, may face challenges finding jobs because they may prioritize smartphones and neglect personal hygiene. NBC spoke with Susan RoAne, author of 'How to Work a Room,' who said, 'If people can smell you before they see you, you aren't getting the job.' RoAne notes that employees with poor hygiene after being hired may also struggle to be promoted, especially in positions that require face-to-face contact with clients or executives. Recent graduates may face even greater challenges, with youth unemployment rates remaining high. Data from May indicates unemployment for 25-34 year olds was 6.7%, slightly up from 6.6% in April. Unemployment for 20-24 year olds was 11.1%, up from 10.6%. Overall unemployment for adults 20 and older was 5.8%. Some commentators suggest millennials may be less interested in traditional jobs. Steve Toback, managing partner at Invisor Consulting, told NBC that some millennials embrace informal entrepreneurship, often working from their parents' homes. 'What entrepreneurialism is for many of them is hanging out in their parents' basement or childhood bedroom with their smartphone, calling themselves the CEO of a one-person company,' Toback said. He adds, 'While starting a business is admirable, gaining experience at another company first is a good idea.' Toback concluded, 'Experience is the best teacher. But buy some deodorant before you get out there.'

Wat tandeborsels betref, het 91% van die respondente dit as belangrik beskou. Die verslag beklemtoon 'n generasieverskil: ouer volwassenes beskou deodorant en slimfone ewe belangrik in hul daaglikse lewe, met tandeborsels wat eerste geplaas is teen 95%. Sekere kenners glo dat jonger volwassenes, veral millennials, moontlik sukkel om werk te kry omdat hulle slimfone prioriteit gee bo persoonlike higiëne. NBC het met Susan RoAne, outeur van 'How to Work a Room,' gepraat, wat gesê het: 'As mense jou kan ruik voordat hulle jou sien, gaan jy nie die werk kry nie.' RoAne noem ook dat werknemers met swak higiëne nadat hulle aangestel is, ook sukkel om bevorder te word, veral in poste waar dit nodig is om direk met kliënte of bestuurders te werk. Algehele werkloosheid vir volwassenes van 20 jaar en ouer is 5,8%. Sommige kommentators dink millennials stel moontlik minder belang in tradisionele werk. Steve Toback, bestuurdsvennoot by Invisor Consulting, het aan NBC gesê dat sommige millennials informele entrepreneurskap omhels en dikwels vanuit hul ouerhuis werk. article_content: Coal India Ltd., a large-cap mining company founded in 1973, operates predominantly in the coal and mining sector and has a market capitalization of Rs 208,176.96 crore. article_content: As soon as Beth Redpath stepped out of her car, she felt a familiar warning: her throat started to close, her skin flushed, and hives appeared. At 28, Beth lives with a severe latex allergy that forces her to always carry an emergency filtration mask in public spaces. Her mother acted quickly during this episode, calling 999 and using Beth’s EpiPen to inject adrenaline. Still, Beth fainted in the ambulance because of dangerously low blood pressure, a terrifying reminder of the dangers of anaphylactic shock. Beth is just one of approximately 600,000 people in Britain living with latex allergy. Latex, derived from rubber trees, appears in around 40,000 everyday products—gloves, balloons, tyres, tarmac, condoms, and paints—so avoiding it is extremely challenging. In this case, roadworks released airborne latex from fresh tarmac near her house, which she inhaled. Allergies occur when the immune system wrongly attacks harmless substances, releasing histamine and causing symptoms like itching and swelling. Repeated exposure can escalate reactions to life-threatening anaphylaxis, sometimes without prior warning. Beth has been hospitalized 27 times in the last 18 months. Her reactions have occurred in unexpected places: after drinking champagne (since latex is used in some corks), or in hospital foyers where latex balloons were present. Now, in supermarkets and busy places, Beth wears a mask to avoid airborne latex from items handled by workers using latex gloves. Widespread use of powdered latex gloves in healthcare, especially in the 1980s with heightened HIV/AIDS prevention, likely contributed to more people developing latex allergies. Modern hospitals mostly use latex-free gloves, but sensitized people still face risks. Dr. Gavin Spickett explains that the dangers are often underestimated—even by medical staff. Latex allergy triggers aren’t always obvious; items like party balloons or new paint and tarmac can cause attacks. Aleksandra Kinay of the Latex Allergy Support Group warns that simply being near latex products can be enough, and some workplaces still haven’t fully adapted. Latex allergy is also connected to allergies to bananas, avocados, kiwis, and chestnuts, due to protein similarities. Beth’s first reactions appeared at 16 in school science class, worsening through her university years in biochemistry, ultimately forcing her to leave the field. Lesley Maitland, another allergy sufferer, had to medically retire when her workplace couldn’t ensure her safety; she links her condition to growing up near rubber factories. Items like elastic bands and hair sprays can set off her symptoms. Both Beth and Lesley have created totally latex-free safe spaces at home. They continue to advocate for greater awareness and latex-free public environments to protect others from similar dangers.

article_content: A Wal-Mart customer was arrested for allegedly stealing rib-eye steaks by placing them on his scooter seat and sitting on them. The incident occurred Tuesday afternoon at a Wal-Mart in Spartanburg, South Carolina, according to a police report accessed by The Smoking Gun. The suspect, 43-year-old Rodney Fowler, was reported to weigh 350 pounds. He was charged with first offense shoplifting. A loss prevention worker, Jackie Jenkins, observed Fowler in the meat section selecting five rib-eye steaks and placing them on the seat of a motorized handicapped scooter. The report states he sat on the steaks and exited the store, passing all checkout points without attempting to pay. Jenkins stopped Fowler and brought him to the store's loss prevention office, after which Officer Adam Bailey arrived, spoke with Jenkins, and arrested Fowler. Due to his size, officers used two pairs of handcuffs linked together, which were double-locked and checked for security. The Smoking Gun also reported that Fowler was released without bond after being in police custody for about three hours.

article_content: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar recently visited London and met UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak and his wife, Akshata Murty, at 10 Downing Street during Diwali. Jaishankar conveyed Diwali greetings from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and presented Sunak with a Lord Ganesha statue and a cricket bat autographed by Virat Kohli. He publicly thanked Sunak for his warm hospitality. Jaishankar’s visit included a scheduled meeting with his UK counterpart, James Cleverly, to further develop the partnership between the two nations through the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and the India-UK Roadmap 2030. Both sides addressed the status of negotiations on a Free Trade Agreement, initiated in 2022, with hopes of achieving a deal that serves shared interests. Their conversation also celebrated recent achievements by the Indian cricket team and discussed the upcoming India-England test series. During his stay, Jaishankar and his wife, Kyoko, participated in Diwali prayers at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in London, attending the Abhishek Puja ritual. Jaishankar reflected on the growing India-UK relationship and appreciation for the Sunaks’ reception via posts on social media. Additional developments include Indian authorities probing the local units of Apple, Google, and Amazon for possible tax issues, Indian investors becoming the largest group in Dubai’s property market, and Razorpay planning to transfer its parent company’s domicile to India, which may involve significant U.S. taxes.

article_content: LeBron James made NBA history on Tuesday night by becoming the first player to surpass 39,000 career points. The 38-year-old Los Angeles Lakers star accomplished this with a three-pointer in the first quarter against the Utah Jazz. The Lakers dominated the game, winning 131-99 and securing a spot in the quarter-finals of the NBA’s in-season tournament. During the celebrations at Crypto.com Arena, James acknowledged the achievement and shared that he was still taking in the significance of the moment. He spoke humbly about being the first to reach this milestone in a league known for its great players and scorers. James finished with 17 points on 6-of-10 shooting, while Anthony Davis led the Lakers with 26 points, 16 rebounds, and four assists. On the same night, Kevin Durant also reached a major milestone by moving up to 11th place on the NBA’s all-time scoring list. He scored 31 points as the Phoenix Suns beat the Portland Trail Blazers 120-107, bringing his total career points to 27,331 and surpassing Elvin Hayes.

Die Lakers het heersend gespeel en hul plek in die kwarteindronde van die NBA se in-seisoen toernooi verseker met ’n 131-99 oorwinning. Tydens die feesvieringe by Crypto.com Arena het James sy mylpaal erken en gesê dat hy nog steeds die grootsheid van die oomblik besig is om te verwerk. article_content: Luxury Travel Intelligence (LTI) released its list of the best and worst luxury hotel openings for 2014, with London hotels topping both categories. Shangri-La Hotel at The Shard was named the worst opening, mainly due to a design flaw that allowed guests to see into neighboring rooms, raising privacy concerns and resulting in the installation of blinds that detracted from the otherwise remarkable views. By contrast, The Beaumont in Mayfair received top honors for its Art Deco design and impeccable service. Established by Chris Corbin and Jeremy King, the hotel was celebrated for its inviting atmosphere and the acclaimed Colony Grill Room. Other distinguished properties among the best openings included Portrait Florence, owned by the Ferragamo family, known for spacious rooms and panoramic views; and Andy Murray’s Cromlix House in Scotland, praised for its country charm and dedicated local staff. Additional recognitions went to Loews Regency in New York, Four Seasons in Moscow (slightly marked down due to an unfinished spa), Maalifushi in the Maldives, Cape Weligama in Sri Lanka, Raffles in Istanbul, Four Seasons in Dubai, and Waldorf Astoria in Amsterdam. On the opposite end, experts criticized SLS Las Vegas for subpar location and management, Ham Yard in London for lacking character and warmth, Park Hyatt New York for its noise issues, and ME Ibiza for poor service and food. LTI’s assessments considered factors such as design, location, service quality, guest experience, and ambiance, relying on direct visits and expert insight.

article_content: Jerusalem (CNN) -- Several Israelis and tourists arriving at Ben Gurion Airport have had their new Apple iPads confiscated by customs officials. According to Israeli authorities, the devices' Wi-Fi specifications do not align with the country's regulations, which are similar to European standards. Yechiel Shavi, spokesperson for the Ministry of Communication, told CNN that the ban only affects iPads built for the U.S. Wi-Fi standard and does not apply to devices matching European specifications. On Wednesday, Apple announced a delay in the iPad's worldwide release, citing unexpectedly high demand in the United States. "We know many international customers waiting to buy an iPad will be disappointed by this news, but we hope they will understand the reason — the iPad has been a runaway success in the U.S. so far," the company said in a statement. However, these words provide little comfort to Israeli travelers whose iPads have been confiscated, with reports describing angry scenes at the airport. Customs officials said that tourists will be able to reclaim their devices when they leave the country. Israeli consumers are known for quickly adopting the latest technology, including Apple's iPhone, which became highly popular after its recent launch in Israel. iDigital, which represents Apple in Israel, was unavailable for comment at the time of writing.

article_content: Delhi residents will soon be able to book seats on air-conditioned buses, as the government launches its new premium bus aggregator scheme. The Delhi Motor Vehicles Licensing of Aggregator (Premium Buses) Scheme, 2023, has been officially unveiled, marking a noteworthy step in improving urban transit. This initiative is India's first bus aggregator plan dedicated exclusively to premium, luxury buses within a city, aiming to make public transport more attractive by offering higher quality, comfort, and reliability. Authorities expect this move to reduce both road congestion and air pollution. A 'Premium Bus' is defined as a fully air-conditioned public bus with at least nine seats, pre-bookable reclining seats, and features like wifi, GPS, and CCTV. Applicants must have at least three years' experience running public transportation vehicles and maintain a minimum annual fleet of either 100 buses, 1,000 cars, or a proportional mix. They must also follow all standard passenger vehicle regulations. No CNG buses older than three years will be allowed, and from January 1, 2025, only electric buses can join the scheme. Applicants are required to have an office within the National Capital Region. Aggregator licences will cost Rs 5 lakh for five years with a renewal option for another five at Rs 2,500. Electric buses are exempt from licence fees. Holders must put at least 25 premium buses into operation within 90 days of licence approval. Fares must be dynamic and not lower than the highest standard set by the Delhi Transport Corporation's AC buses, and all booking and payment must be digital. Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal hopes the scheme will encourage people to use buses over private vehicles, crediting four years of hard work for the progress made. Transport Minister Kailash Gahlot called the scheme a significant achievement toward providing high-quality, sustainable metro transport. Delhi currently has 7,135 buses, though experts say at least 11,000 are needed to meet commuting demands.

Geen CNG-bus ouer as drie jaar sal toegelaat word nie, en vanaf 1 Januarie 2025 mag slegs elektriese busse by die skema aansluit. Aansoekers moet 'n kantoor in die Nasionale Hoofstadstreek hê. Versamelaarlisensies kos R5 lakh vir vyf jaar, met 'n hernuwingsopsie vir nog vyf jaar teen R2,500. Lisensiegeld word kwytgeskeld vir elektriese busse. Lisensiehouers moet binne 90 dae van goedkeuring minstens 25 premie-busse in werking stel. Tariewe moet dinamies wees en nie laer as die hoogste tarief van die Delhi Transport Corporation se lugverkoelde busse nie, en alle besprekings en betalings moet digitaal wees. Eerste Minister Arvind Kejriwal hoop die skema sal mense aanmoedig om busse bo privaat voertuie te kies, en gee krediet aan vier jaar se harde werk vir dié vordering. Vervoerminister Kailash Gahlot het die skema 'n beduidende mylpaal genoem op pad na hoëgehalte, volhoubare metrovervoer. Delhi het tans 7,135 busse, hoewel kenners meen minstens 11,000 is nodig om in die stad se pendelaarsbehoeftes te voldoen.

article_content: Chelsey Ramer, a 17-year-old student from Alabama and a member of the Poarch Band of Creek Indians, says she was fined $1,000 and had her diploma withheld after she wore an eagle feather in her graduation cap to celebrate her Native American heritage. Escambia Academy High School, a private school in Alabama, prohibits students from wearing extra items during graduation ceremonies unless they have received prior permission. Ramer and her tribal teacher, Alex Alvarez, requested permission for her to wear the eagle feather, which holds significant spiritual and cultural importance for the Poarch Creek Indians, but the school administration denied the request. Despite not signing the school's contract and knowing the rules, Ramer wore the feather during the ceremony with her family’s support. A friend tied it to her tassel. After the ceremony, the school refused to give her the diploma and imposed a $1,000 fine, stating she had violated school policy. Ramer described the school’s actions as unfair and discriminatory, saying she had looked forward to the opportunity to celebrate her heritage throughout her four years at the school. Tribal teacher Alvarez also criticized the school's decision, emphasizing the cultural and spiritual value of the eagle feather. After the incident, the school's then-head teacher, Betty Warren, resigned and was replaced. The school did not publicly comment on the issue. The Poarch Band of Creek Indians is the only federally recognized Native American tribe in Alabama, descended from the original Creek Nation, and maintains legislative, executive, and judicial branches. The tribe operates casinos and a hotel in southern Alabama, with over 1,000 of its 3,095 members living near the town of Poarch. The current chairman is Buford L. Rolin.

Escambia Academy High School, 'n privaat skool in Alabama, verbied studente om ekstra items tydens die gradeplegtigheid te dra tensy hulle vooraf toestemming gekry het. Ten spyte daarvan dat sy nie die skool se kontrak geteken het nie en die reëls geken het, het Ramer tog die veer tydens die seremonie met haar familie se ondersteuning gedra. 'n Vriend het dit aan haar tossel vasgemaak. Na die seremonie het die skool geweier om haar die diploma te bêre en 'n boete van $1,000 opgelê omdat sy glo teen die skoolbeleid opgetree het. Stamonderwyser Alvarez het ook die skool se besluit gekritiseer en die geestelike en kulturele waarde van die arendveer beklemtoon. Na die voorval het die skool se destydse hoof, Betty Warren, bedank en is sy vervang. Die skool het nie kommentaar gelewer oor die voorval nie. Die Poarch Band of Creek Indians is die enigste federale erkende Inheemse Amerikaanse stam in Alabama, oorspronklik van die Creek Nation, en beskik oor wetgewende, uitvoerende en regsprekende takke. Die stam besit casinos en 'n hotel in Suid-Alabama, met meer as 1,000 van sy 3,095 lede wat naby Poarch woon. Die huidige voorsitter is Buford L. Rolin.

article_content: India's imports of palm oil and sunflower oil in 2022/23 surged by 24% and 54% respectively, reaching record highs due to a rebound in consumption and a considerable price discount compared to soyoil, according to a leading trade group. As the world's largest importer of vegetable oils, India's increased purchases could help reduce palm oil stocks in Indonesia and Malaysia, supporting benchmark futures. This buying may also lower inventories in sunflower oil-producing Black Sea countries. Palm oil imports were 9.79 million metric tons in the 2022/23 marketing year ending October 31, while sunflower oil imports rose to 3 million tons, according to the Mumbai-based Solvent Extractors' Association of India (SEA). Soyoil imports dropped 12% to 3.68 million tons, as soyoil was priced at a premium over palm oil and sunflower oil for most of the year. Total edible oil imports surged to a record 16.47 million tons, up 17.4% from a year earlier. Lowering import taxes to 5.5% encouraged more overseas purchases, the SEA said. The government had reduced import duties when global prices increased last year but did not raise them after prices dropped, noted a New Delhi-based dealer with a global trading company. "Lower world prices and reduced import duties made edible oil cheaper, boosting consumption," the dealer said. Consequently, vegetable oil stocks rose to 3.3 million tons on November 1, up from 2.46 million tons a year earlier, the SEA stated. India imports palm oil mainly from Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand, and sources soyoil and sunflower oil from Argentina, Brazil, Russia, and Ukraine. Indian refiners bought oil actively from November to January and July to September, when prices were favorable, but reduced imports in October due to high stocks, said Rajesh Patel, managing partner at edible oil trader and broker GGN Research. Palm oil imports in October fell 15% from the previous month to 708,706 tons, the lowest in four months. Soyoil imports in October dropped 62% from September to 135,325 tons, the lowest in 34 months. Sunflower oil imports declined 49% to 153,780 tons, the lowest in seven months, according to the SEA.

As die wêreld se grootste invoerder van plantaardige olies, kan Indië se verhoogde aankope help om palmolie-voorrade in Indonesië en Maleisië te verminder, wat die maatstawende termynkontrakte ondersteun. Hierdie aankope kan ook voorrade in sonneblomolie-produsente van die Swartsee-lande verlaag. Palmolie-invoere was 9.79 miljoen metrieke ton in die 2022/23 bemarkingsjaar wat op 31 Oktober geëindig het, terwyl sonneblomolie-invoere tot 3 miljoen ton gestyg het, volgens die Mumbai-gebaseerde Solvent Extractors' Association of India (SEA). Sojapolie-invoere het met 12% gedaal tot 3.68 miljoen ton, omdat sojapolie die grootste deel van die jaar teen 'n premie bo palmolie en sonneblomolie geprys was. Totale invoer van eetbare olie het tot ’n rekord van 16.47 miljoen ton gestyg, 17.4% hoër as ’n jaar tevore. Die verlaging van invoerbelasting tot 5.5% het meer oorsese aankope aangemoedig, volgens die SEA. Die regering het invoerbelasting verlaag toe wêreldpryse verlede jaar gestyg het, maar dit nie verhoog nadat pryse gedaal het nie, het ’n handelaar van ’n wêreldwye handelsmaatskappy in Nieu-Delhi genoem. "Laer wêreldpryse en verminderde invoerbelasting het eetbare olie goedkoper gemaak en verbruik laat toeneem," het die handelaar gesê. Gevolglik het voorrade van plantaardige olie op 1 November tot 3.3 miljoen ton gestyg, vanaf 2.46 miljoen ton 'n jaar tevore, sê die SEA. Indiese verfyners het olie aktief aangekoop van November tot Januarie en van Julie tot September toe pryse gunstig was, maar invoere in Oktober verminder as gevolg van hoë plaaslike voorrade, sê Rajesh Patel, bestuurvennoot van die eetbare oliehandelaar en makelaar GGN Research. Palmolie-invoere in Oktober het met 15% vanaf die vorige maand tot 708,706 ton gedaal, die laagste in vier maande. Sojapolie-invoere het in Oktober met 62% vanaf September na 135,325 ton gedaal, die laagste in 34 maande. Sonneblomolie-invoere het met 49% gedaal tot 153,780 ton, die laagste in sewe maande, volgens die SEA.

article_content: Andrew Fleming has been appointed as the new British Deputy High Commissioner to East and Northeast India. Fleming arrived in Kolkata on Wednesday and will focus on strengthening the UK’s relationship with East and Northeast India. Prior to this role, Andrew Fleming served as British Deputy High Commissioner to Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for five years, and later as Officer on Special Temporary Duty in Bengaluru. He then spent several months in London, where he helped organize the visit of Indian Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar during the King's Coronation. While posted in Hyderabad, Fleming promoted business and trade between the UK and local states, facilitated research and academic partnerships, and worked to enhance 'living bridge' connections and better understand local issues. He has supported initiatives related to community cohesion, interfaith dialogue, preventing violence against women, fighting human trafficking, addressing child sexual abuse, tackling fake news, and empowering youth. His interest in heritage led him to occasionally lead heritage walks in Hyderabad. Fleming stated, "I am thrilled to take up my role as British Deputy High Commissioner to East & North-East India. I am determined to ensure the UK-India 2030 Roadmap is seen as relevant across all 13 states and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands that our Kolkata office covers. I will seek to build meaningful connections that support our shared priorities across this vibrant and diverse region." Fleming joined the British Civil Service in 1986 and has held various roles in the UK and overseas. He has lived in Uganda, Ghana, and Nigeria, and has worked on international policy in many regions, visiting 117 countries to date. In addition to his work on international migration, he has advised government ministers on policies related to community cohesion and faith. He also served as an election observer in Ghana (2008) and Nigeria (2015).

article_content: Last week, the combined market value of four of India's ten most-valued firms increased by Rs 65,671.35 crore, with Reliance Industries leading as the top gainer. The BSE benchmark index rose by 175.31 points, or 0.26%. Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Bharti Airtel reported growth in their market valuations. Meanwhile, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Hindustan Unilever, ITC, State Bank of India (SBI), and Bajaj Finance saw a decline in value. Reliance Industries' market capitalization surged by Rs 26,014.36 crore, reaching Rs 16,19,907.39 crore. HDFC Bank added Rs 20,490.90 crore to reach Rs 11,62,706.71 crore. Bharti Airtel rose by Rs 14,135.21 crore to Rs 5,46,720.84 crore, and ICICI Bank increased by Rs 5,030.88 crore to Rs 6,51,285.29 crore. On the other hand, TCS’s value dropped by Rs 16,484.03 crore to Rs 12,65,153.60 crore, and Bajaj Finance fell by Rs 12,202.87 crore to Rs 4,33,966.53 crore. Hindustan Unilever decreased by Rs 3,406.91 crore to Rs 5,90,910.45 crore, while SBI fell by Rs 2,543.51 crore to Rs 5,00,046.01 crore. ITC declined by Rs 1,808.36 crore to Rs 5,46,000.07 crore, and Infosys dipped by Rs 290.53 crore to Rs 5,96,391.22 crore. Reliance Industries retained its position as India’s most valuable firm, followed by TCS, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Infosys, Hindustan Unilever, Bharti Airtel, ITC, SBI, and Bajaj Finance. Additionally, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has approved a new framework for fractional ownership of real estate assets. Experts noted an increase in offshore hiring by multinational companies in India, which is likely to create more jobs in engineering disciplines. Market analysts expect India’s smartphone market to rebound in 2024, fueled by affordable 5G devices and pre-election offers.

article_content: Diego Maradona, the legendary Argentine footballer, has revealed that he is a potential candidate to become the next head coach of the Venezuelan national football team. If selected, the 1986 World Cup winner will aim to lead Venezuela—currently the only South American country never to qualify for the FIFA World Cup—to their first-ever appearance at the 2018 tournament in Russia. Venezuela has been without a head coach since Cesar Farias resigned in November 2013 after the team's failure to qualify for the World Cup in Brazil. Maradona, along with experienced Venezuelan club managers, is among those reportedly being considered for the position. Speaking to Telesur, Maradona stated, 'I look for serious projects... and I think that yes, if there is security, then maybe.' At 53, Maradona is widely recognized not only for his football achievements but also for his leftist political views. He has maintained strong ties with Venezuela's socialist government and President Nicolas Maduro, and he plans to meet the president following the conclusion of the 2014 World Cup in Brazil. Maradona, who scored 34 goals in 91 appearances for Argentina, mentioned having discussions about the Venezuelan team. Speculation around Maradona’s potential appointment has been growing in Venezuela. The late President Hugo Chavez had a close friendship with Maradona. Previously, Maradona has managed both the Argentina national team and the UAE’s Al Wasl club. Venezuela, known as 'La Vinotinto' due to their burgundy kit, have never qualified for the World Cup finals. Current statistics: FIFA ranking 40, captain Juan Arango, most caps held by Juan Arango (120), top scorers Juan Arango and Giancarlo Maldonado, home stadium Estadio Jose Antonio Anzoategui in Puerto La Cruz, and their best Copa America finish was fourth place in 2011.

article_content: The UK's Illegal Migration Act is being challenged in court by the Northern Ireland Human Rights Commission (NIHRC), which claims it breaches the Windsor Framework. The Framework is the revised post-Brexit agreement between the UK and EU for Northern Ireland. While it mainly addresses trade, it also contains important human rights commitments, requiring the UK not to weaken protections established by the Good Friday Agreement. The challenge by NIHRC coincides with Home Secretary Suella Braverman preparing to address migration at the Conservative party conference. Since January 2021, NIHRC has had the authority to monitor and enforce the UK Government's human rights obligations under Article 2 of the Windsor Framework. The Illegal Migration Act is a key part of the Prime Minister's plan to stop small boats crossing the English Channel. The law obliges the Home Secretary to detain and remove anyone entering the UK illegally. However, the central plan to send migrants to Rwanda is on hold, pending a Supreme Court ruling expected later this year. During the law's passage through Parliament, NIHRC advised that it was incompatible with Article 2, the European Convention on Human Rights, and other international standards. NIHRC Chief Commissioner, Alyson Kilpatrick, described legal action as a 'last resort, but a necessary step', expressing concern that the Act would prevent people arriving irregularly from seeking refugee status. She further noted that the Act introduces sweeping new detention powers with limited judicial oversight, and that removing vulnerable people to third countries without guaranteed protection is deeply concerning. A government spokesperson stated, 'Tackling illegal migration is a top priority for the government, and there are an unacceptable number of people risking their lives making dangerous crossings on small boats. The Illegal Migration Act is vital for breaking the cycle, ending gang exploitation, and saving lives.' This marks the first government challenge under Article 2 and takes the form of a judicial review at the High Court in Belfast. The government reportedly views the claim as speculative and plans to argue the Act does not reduce any rights under Article 2. If NIHRC wins, parts of the law could be disapplied in Northern Ireland. A similar case is at a preliminary stage, after Phoenix Law began proceedings against the Home Secretary on behalf of a minor asylum seeker who arrived by small boat. The court is expected to issue case management directions soon.
translated_content: Die VK se Wet op Onwettige Migrasie word deur die Noord-Ierland Menseregtekommissie (NIHRC) in die hof betwis, omdat hulle meen dit skend die Windsor-raamwerk. Die raamwerk is die gewysigde post-Brexit-ooreenkoms tussen die VK en EU vir Noord-Ierland. Alhoewel dit meestal handel oor handel, bevat dit ook belangrike menseregtebepalings wat vereis dat die VK nie beskerming wat deur die Goede Vrydag-ooreenkoms ingestel is, mag verswak nie. Die NIHRC se uitdaging val saam met die Minister van Binnelandse Sake, Suella Braverman, wat voorberei om migrasiekwessies by die Konserwatiewe Party-kongres aan te spreek. Sedert Januarie 2021 het die NIHRC die reg om toesig te hou oor en af te dwing dat die VK-regering aan haar menseregte-verpligtinge voldoen volgens Artikel 2 van die Windsor-raamwerk. Die Wet op Onwettige Migrasie vorm 'n kerndeel van die Eerste Minister se belofte om bote met onwettige migrante oor die Engelse Kanaal te stop. Die wet verplig die Minister van Binnelandse Sake om enigiemand wat onwettig die VK binnekom, in hegtenis te neem en te verwyder. Die plan om migrante na Rwanda te stuur, kan egter nog nie plaasvind nie, omdat die saak tans by die Hoogste Hof is, met 'n uitspraak later vanjaar verwag. Tydens die wet se parlementêre proses het die NIHRC gewaarsku dat dit nie strook met Artikel 2, die Europese Konvensie van Menseregte en ander internasionale standaarde nie. NIHRC-hoofkommissaris, Alyson Kilpatrick, het die regstappe as ‘n laaste uitweg, maar ‘n noodsaaklike stap beskryf en beklemtoon dat die wet dit feitlik onmoontlik maak vir mense wat onreëlmatig aankom om as vlugtelinge te registreer. Sy het bygevoeg dat die wet ingrypende nuwe aanhoudingsmagte met beperkte regterlike toesig daarstel, en dat die verwydering van kwesbare mense na derde lande sonder waarborge van beskerming diep kommerwekkend is. 'n Regeringswoordvoerder het gesê: 'Om onwettige migrasie te takel is 'n topprioriteit vir die regering, en daar is onaanvaarbaar baie mense wat hul lewens waag deur gevaarlike bote te neem. Die Wet op Onwettige Migrasie is noodsaaklik om die siklus te breek, bendes te stop, en lewens te red.' Hierdie is die eerste uitdaging teen die regering onder Artikel 2 en dit is 'n aansoek om regterlike hersiening by die Hooggeregshof in Belfast. Die regering beskou glo die eis as spekulatief en gaan probeer bewys die wet doen nie afbreuk aan regte onder Artikel 2 nie. Indien die NIHRC slaag, kan dele van die wet in Noord-Ierland nie toegepas word nie. ‘n Soortgelyke saak is in ‘n vroeë stadium waar Phoenix Law regsaksie namens ‘n minderjarige asielsoeker, wat per boot opgedaag het, ingedien het. Die hof behoort binnekort ‘n rigting te gee oor die saakbestuur.

article_content: Nigeria’s Foreign Affairs Minister, Ambassador Yusuf Tuggar, has officially dismissed recent media stories claiming the country was rejected by the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC). According to reports issued on October 26, Nigeria allegedly failed in its bid to secure a seat at the council, while Ghana, Malawi, and Cote d’Ivoire were said to have won with 197, 182, and 181 votes, and Nigeria purportedly received only three votes. Yet, Alkasim Abdulkadir, media aide to the Minister, clarified that Nigeria had initially signaled its intention to vie for a seat but later chose to withdraw from the race. This move was to support a consensus for West Africa, allowing Ghana and Cote d’Ivoire to run unopposed for the region’s two available seats as part of an ECOWAS agreement. Abdulkadir further emphasized that Nigeria was never on the ballot, meaning the vote figures mentioned do not apply to the country. He noted that Nigeria intends to contest in the upcoming cycle after Senegal’s term ends. The Nigerian government plans to pursue its candidacy through established diplomatic channels in Geneva, New York, Addis Ababa, and other pertinent locales, making sure all procedural steps are carefully followed.

Volgens berigte van 26 Oktober het Nigerië glo onsuksesvol vir ‘n setel aan die raad meegeding, terwyl Ghana, Malawi en Ivoorkus onderskeidelik 197, 182 en 181 stemme gekry het, en daar beweer is dat Nigerië net drie stemme ontvang het. Maar Alkasim Abdulkadir, die minister se mediaskakel, het verduidelik dat Nigerië aanvanklik sy voorneme aangedui het om deel te neem, maar toe besluit het om uit te tree. Dié besluit is geneem om West-Afrika te ondersteun sodat Ghana en Ivoorkus sonder opposisie vir die streek se twee sitplekke kon meeding, soos bepaal deur ‘n ECOWAS-ooreenkoms. Abdulkadir het verder beklemtoon dat Nigerië nie op die stemming was nie; daarom is die genoem stemsyfers nie van toepassing nie. Hy het bygevoeg dat die land beplan om in die volgende verkiesingsiklus mee te ding nadat Senegal se termyn klaar is. Die regering gaan sy kandidatuur deur erkende diplomatieke kanale in Genève, New York, Addis Abeba en ander betrokke plekke bevorder om te verseker dat almal behoorlik ingelig word en alle prosedures gevolg word.

article_content: Parents often have difficulty deciding whether their toddler's injury is an emergency, needs a doctor's visit, or can be managed at home. Dr. Lara Zibners, a pediatric emergency physician, recommends calling your pediatrician before going to the ER unless it is life-threatening. Key guidelines for common accidents include: Burns: Go to the ER if the burn affects a large area, face, hands, feet, genitals, or looks severe (third-degree). Otherwise, quickly remove wet clothing, cool the area with running water for 10–15 minutes, and cover loosely with a dry bandage. Do not use ointments or break blisters. Head injuries: Children over 12 months old who bump their heads can usually be monitored at home, unless they show symptoms like vomiting, sleepiness, limping, refusing to move a limb, irritability, or unresponsiveness—in which case, seek medical help. For infants under a year, always consult a physician after more than a minor bump. Bite wounds: For bites breaking the skin, wash thoroughly with soap and water and call your pediatrician since human bites risk infection. Car accidents: If your securely restrained child is alert and calms within 20 minutes after a minor accident, medical attention isn't usually needed. Seek help if the child continues crying, has bruising, blood in urine, pain, or movement issues. Tongue injuries: Apply direct pressure with a damp washcloth if there is bleeding; cold treats like ice pops can help. If bleeding continues for more than 15 minutes, go to the ER. Diaper-changing safety: Use a changing pad with a concave middle, always fasten the safety strap, and keep diaper supplies near but out of baby's reach. Watch for signs after accidents like unusual bruising, blood in urine, unwillingness to move, or motionlessness, and contact your doctor if they occur.
translated_content: Ouers sukkel gereeld om te besluit of ŉ kleuter se besering ŉ noodgeval is, ŉ doktersbesoek verg of tuis behandel kan word. Dr. Lara Zibners, ŉ pediatriese noodarts, beveel aan dat ouers hul pediater skakel, tensy die situasie lewensbedreigend is. Hier is sleutelriglyne vir algemene ongelukke: Brandwonde: Gaan ER toe as die brand ŉ groot area, gesig, hande, voete of geslagsdele affekteer of ernstig lyk (derdegraads). Verwyder klere vinnig, koel die plek met lopende water vir 10–15 minute, en bedek losweg met ŉ droë verband. Moet nie salf aanwend of blase breek nie. Kopbeserings: Kinders ouer as 12 maande wat hul koppe stamp, kan tuis dopgehou word, tensy simptome soos naarheid, erge slaperigheid, hink, weiering om ŉ arm/been te beweeg, of bewusteloosheid voorkom — roep dan hulp in. Babas jonger as ŉ jaar moet altyd ná meer as ŉ geringe stamp deur ŉ dokter gesien word. Bytwonde: As ŉ byt die vel breek, was dit deeglik met seep en water en skakel jou pediater, want menslike bytwonde infekteer maklik. Motorongeluk: As jou kind vasgegord is en binne 20 minute kalmeer na ŉ ligte ongeluk, is doktershulp gewoonlik nie nodig nie. Kry hulp as hy nie kalmeer nie, kneusing, bloed in urine, pyn of bewegingsprobleme toon. Tongbeserings: Druk ŉ nat waslap op die wond. Roomyse kan help. As bloeding langer as 15 minute duur, gaan hospitaal toe. Veilige luierwisseling: Gebruik ŉ verskuiwingsmat met ŉ hol middel, maak die veiligheidsgordel vas, en hou voorsienings naby maar buite baba se bereik. Let op na tekens soos ongewone kneusing, bloed in urine, nie wil beweeg nie, of bewegingsloosheid, en skakel jou dokter as dit voorkom.

article_content: William Thomas, 69, from Borth, Ceredigion in Wales, was initially told by his doctors that a lump on his arm was a harmless cyst, when in reality it was an aggressive form of skin cancer. In June 2012, Mr. Thomas visited his GP, Dr Juliana Hood, about a lump on the same arm where he’d had a previous cancer scare in 1995. Nine weeks later, during a follow-up appointment, Dr Ian Hosker found no record of the earlier visit. Instead of making an urgent referral, Dr Hosker diagnosed the lump as a ganglion—a benign, fluid-filled swelling—and scheduled a standard referral to the local hospital in four weeks. While at work, Mr. Thomas accidentally knocked the lump, causing it to bleed persistently. He went to the emergency department, where he was diagnosed with Merkel cell carcinoma, a rare and aggressive skin cancer. He was sent to Gobowen hospital the next day for a biopsy and received emergency surgery to remove the tumour. The operation left Mr. Thomas with reduced strength and function in his right arm, limiting his ability to work. His daughter, Mandy Daniel, said the experience was traumatic for the family and that the news of the cancer left a lasting impact. After the family’s complaint, the Public Service Ombudsman for Wales found that the doctors responsible had made serious mistakes, including poor record-keeping and delayed referral. Mr. Thomas was awarded £750 in compensation for the delay in diagnosis, while his daughter received £200 for issues with the complaint process. Ombudsman Carys Williams stated that opportunities to diagnose sooner were missed, and although the delay may only have been two weeks, the failures in patient care were significant. Dr Hood explained she had mistakenly closed Mr. Thomas’s file before entering details from the initial visit, and said she was devastated when she learned of the diagnosis. She later left the practice. Both Dr Hood and Dr Hosker have apologized. Practice manager Jacqui Jones Brown declined to comment.

article_content: Thousands of people gathered outside the headquarters of Greece's state broadcaster, ERT, in Athens on Wednesday to protest the government's unexpected decision to suspend its activities as part of austerity measures. ERT's television and radio services were taken off the air overnight, though some employees continued broadcasting online. Most demonstrators were ERT employees, but many regular citizens joined in solidarity, holding banners such as 'All in the streets' and encouraging further participation. Greek labor unions also condemned the move, announcing a general strike and urging their members to support ERT journalists. The government, represented by spokesman Simon Kedikoglou, cited long-standing corruption and financial mismanagement within ERT as reasons for the closure. He stated that during times of public sacrifice, there is no tolerance for inefficiency or misuse of funds. The closure immediately affected 2,656 employees, who lost their jobs. The Greek government needs to reduce the wider public sector workforce by 2,000 by the end of the year and 15,000 by the end of 2014 to meet creditor requirements from the European Commission, European Central Bank, and International Monetary Fund. Kedikoglou announced that a new, modern broadcaster with a smaller staff would be established, with former ERT employees eligible to apply for new roles. The new outlet, to be called the Organization of Modern State Television, is set to operate before the end of the summer. The European Commission clarified it had not demanded ERT's closure but recognized the Greek government's authority to manage its public sector. It also remarked on the importance of public broadcasting in European democracies. Reporters Without Borders criticized the government's decision as 'bizarre' and expressed concern over the impact on press freedom. In recent years, Greece's ranking in the organization's press freedom index has dropped by almost 50 places, partly due to violence against journalists and threats from groups like the Golden Dawn party. The closure of ERT was described as a severe blow to information pluralism and freedom. Reporters Without Borders' secretary-general Christophe Deloire traveled to Athens to meet with ERT staff. The protests and international attention continue as Greece faces ongoing economic and social challenges.

ERT se televisie- en radiodienste is oornag van die lug gehaal, hoewel sommige werknemers steeds aanlyn uitgesaai het. Meeste betogers was ERT-werknemers, maar baie gewone burgers het solidêr aangesluit en baniere soos 'Almal in die strate' gehou om ander aan te moedig om deel te neem. Griekse vakbonde het die stap veroordeel, 'n algemene staking aangekondig en hul lede aangespoor om ERT-joernaliste te ondersteun. Die regering, verteenwoordig deur woordvoerder Simon Kedikoglou, het dekadelange korrupsie en die wanbestuur van fondse by ERT as redes vir die sluiting genoem. Hy het gesê dat daar in 'n tyd van openbare opoffering geen plek vir traagheid of vermorsing van fondse is nie. Die sluiting het 2 656 werknemers onmiddellik geraak, wat hul werk verloor het. Hulle het ook die belangrikheid van openbare uitsaaidienste in Europese demokrasieë beklemtoon. Reporters Without Borders het die regering se besluit as 'bisar' gekritiseer en besorgdheid uitgespreek oor die impak op persvryheid. Die afgelope paar jaar het Griekeland byna 50 plekke verloor op die persvryheidsindeks van die organisasie, deels weens geweld teen joernaliste en dreigemente van groepe soos die Golden Dawn-party. ERT se sluiting word as 'n ernstige slag teen pluralisme en vryheid van inligting beskryf. Die sekretaris-generaal van Reporters Without Borders, Christophe Deloire, het na Athene gereis om met ERT-personeel te vergader. Die protesaksies en internasionale aandag duur voort terwyl Griekeland deur voortdurende ekonomiese en sosiale uitdagings gaan.

article_content: Cordelia Okonye, mother of the late model Augusta Osedion, has detailed her efforts in helping authorities arrest her daughter's alleged murderer, Nnanyereugo Benjamin Best (also known as Killaboi), in Sierra Leone. Killaboi made headlines in July by confessing on social media to the murder of Augusta Osedion. In an emotional Facebook post, Okonye explained that, after her repeated pleas to Killaboi to surrender were ignored, she sent his passport photo and a description of his distinctive tattoo to friends and relatives worldwide. Her cousin in Sierra Leone recognized someone resembling Killaboi, prompting Okonye’s son and cousin to travel to Sierra Leone to aid the search. Authorities in Sierra Leone declared Killaboi wanted shortly before Okonye’s relatives arrived, and local police were informed about his presence. Okonye alleged that Killaboi escaped Nigeria by obtaining a Sierra Leonean passport using a false name on July 28th, about two weeks after the murder occurred on July 13th. He was ultimately apprehended by police on Thursday. Okonye stated that, while the pain of losing her daughter remains, she feels some relief now that the suspect has been arrested.

Killaboi het in Julie opslae gemaak toe hy op sosiale media erken het dat hy Augusta Osedion vermoor het. In 'n emosionele Facebook-plasing het Okonye verduidelik dat sy, nadat haar herhaalde versoeke aan Killaboi om oor te gee geïgnoreer is, haar sy paspoortfoto en beskrywing van sy kenmerkende tatoeëermerk aan vriende en familie wêreldwyd gestuur het. Haar neef in Sierra Leone het iemand opgemerk wat soos Killaboi lyk, wat veroorsaak het dat Okonye se seun en neef na Sierra Leone gereis het om met die soektog te help. Owerhede in Sierra Leone het Killaboi as gesoek verklaar kort voordat Okonye se familielede daar aangekom het, en die plaaslike polisie is ingelig oor sy teenwoordigheid. Okonye het beweer dat Killaboi Nigerië ontvlug het deur op 28 Julie 'n Sierra Leoneaanse paspoort met 'n vals naam te bekom, sowat twee weke na die moord wat op 13 Julie plaasgevind het. Hy is uiteindelik op Donderdag deur die polisie in hegtenis geneem. Okonye het gesê dat, hoewel die pyn van haar dogter se dood bly, sy nou deels verlig voel omdat die verdagte gevang is.

article_content: The quiet village of Hroza in Ukraine's Kharkiv region was devastated when a ballistic missile struck during a funeral wake, killing 52 residents—about a fifth of the village's population. The small community of 300 people was left in shock and mourning. The missile hit as villagers gathered to rebury a local man who had previously been buried in territory controlled by opposing forces. Tragically, his son and wife were among those killed. After the attack, the damaged remains of the café and grocery store stood as a stark reminder, with medical gloves and bloodstains still visible. A memorial with candles on a tractor tire marked the lives lost, while undisturbed playground equipment offered a haunting contrast. Locals like Andriy are searching for their missing loved ones. Andriy's wife, Lyubov, was at the wake and is still unaccounted for, leading her family to provide DNA samples in hope of identification. Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko stressed that every family in Hroza was affected. Local officials, including the prosecutor, believe the strike was deliberate, citing the use of a ballistic missile and absence of military targets. Ukraine blames Russia for the attack, but Russian authorities have not responded. This single attack has left a deep emotional and social scar on Hroza, forcing the village to confront immense loss and devastation.
translated_content: Die rustige dorpie Hroza in die Charkiv-streek van Oekraïne is verwoes toe 'n ballistiese missiel 'n begrafnisdiens getref en 52 inwoners doodgemaak het—ongeveer 'n vyfde van die dorp se bevolking. Die klein gemeenskap van 300 mense is in skok en rou gelaat. Die missiel het toegeslaan terwyl inwoners byeengekom het om 'n plaaslike man weer te begrawe wat vroeër in besette gebied begrawe is. Ongelukkig was sy seun en vrou onder diegene wat gesterf het. Na die aanval was die stukkende kafee en kruidenierswinkel tasbare oorblyfsels van die ramp, met mediese handskoene en bloedvlekke wat steeds daar lê. 'n Gedenkteken met kerse op 'n trekkersband het die lewens wat verloor is, herdenk, terwyl ongeskonde speelgrondapparaat 'n spookagtige agtergrond geskep het. Inwoners soos Andriy bly steeds op soek na hul vermiste geliefdes. Sy vrou, Lyubov, was by die diens en word steeds vermis, wat haar familie hoop gee dat DNA-monsters haar sal kan identifiseer. Minister van Binnelandse Sake Ihor Klymenko het beklemtoon dat elke gesin in Hroza geraak is. Plaaslike amptenare, insluitend die aanklaer, meen die aanval was opsetlik, gegewe die gebruik van 'n ballistiese missiel en geen militêre teikens nie.
